Pair it with a workflow mode whenever the judgment feeds an edit.\n\nOrchestrate `jev` for decisions a script can consume: a yes/no probability, one key from explicit\noptions, an ordered level, or several typed answers in one request. Jev returns a small\nmachine-readable object where prose generation would return a paragraph, which makes it the right\ntool when the caller needs a value to branch on rather than text to read.\n\n**Core principle**: send only the state the judgment needs, choose the narrowest question type that\nanswers the question, read the exit code before the payload, and keep every consequence behind the\ncaller's own authorization.\n\n---\n\n## 1. WHEN TO USE\n\n### Activation Triggers\n\n- **Typed judgment**: a task needs a probability, a category from a known set, or an ordered level\n  rather than generated text.\n- **Branch input**: a script, hook or gate needs a value it can compare, so `--value` and the exit\n  code are the whole interface.\n- **Batched classification**: several unrelated questions apply to one state, answered together by\n  `run` instead of by several calls.\n- **Judgment transport discovery**: a request names `jev`, Jev, TypeSafe Jev, `noul`, `choice`,\n  `score`, or `jev-mcp`.\n\n### When NOT to Use\n\n- **The state is a secret or private record.** Jev forwards the state verbatim to the selected\n  provider. Authorization to send it is the caller's to hold, and a judgment is not worth a leak.\n- **The question is a fact this repository can answer.** A grep, a test run or a read settles those,\n  and a model opinion about them is a guess wearing JSON.\n- **The request needs an edit, a build or a test.** Jev has no file or process tools; dispatch a\n  workflow mode instead, and use this packet only for the judgment that steers it.\n- **No credential resolves for the selected provider.** Without one every call exits 3 with no\n  judgment, so the route is unavailable rather than degraded; `auth status` is the check, not an\n  assumption about the machine.\n- **A prose answer is the deliverable.** Use a dispatched CLI session; Jev deliberately returns no\n  explanation.\n\n---\n\n## 2. SMART ROUTING\n\n### Prerequisite Detection\n\nRun these before constructing a command:\n\n```bash\ncommand -v jev && jev --version      # jev 0.6.2 at the pinned contract\njev auth status                      # {\"ok\": true, \"stored\": true, \"store\": \"...\"} or exit 3\n```\n\n`command -v jev` decides whether the route exists. `auth status` decides whether a judgment is\npossible, and it never prints the key. Use `jev auth test` when the key must be proven accepted: it\nsends a minimal request and reports `{\"ok\": true, \"valid\": true, \"model\": \"...\"}`.\n\n### Phase Detection\n\n```text\nJEV TASK\n    |\n    +- STEP 0: Detect the intent: JEV_JUDGMENT, JEV_QUESTION, JEV_PROVIDER or JEV_MCP\n    +- STEP 1: Score intents (top-2 when ambiguity is small)\n    +- Phase 1: Availability (command -v jev and jev auth status before the first judgment)\n    +- Phase 2: Judgment (one typed subcommand: noul, choice, score or run)\n    +- Phase 3: Verification (read the exit code before trusting the payload)\n```\n\n### Resource Domains\n\nThe router discovers markdown resources recursively from `references/` and `assets/` and then applies\nintent scoring from `INTENT_MODEL`.\n\n```text\nreferences/   one document per routed intent\nassets/       the question-shaping card\n```\n\n- `references/` holds the CLI contract, the integration patterns, the provider setup and the MCP\n  server, selected by intent.\n- `assets/` holds the question-shaping card, loaded when the question itself needs drafting.\n- `feature-catalog/` and `manual-testing-playbook/` hold the capability index and the deterministic\n  scenarios, read only on explicit request.\n\n### Resource Loading Levels\n\n| Level | When to Load | Resources |\n| ----------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------- |\n| ALWAYS | Every skill invocation | `references/cli-reference.md`, `references/integration-patterns.md` |\n| CONDITIONAL | If intent signals match | `references/providers-and-models.md`, `references/mcp-server.md`, `assets/question-shaping-card.md` |\n| ON_DEMAND | Only on explicit request | `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md`, `manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md` |\n\n### Smart Router Pseudocode\n\n```python\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nRESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / \"references\", SKILL_ROOT / \"assets\")\nDEFAULT_RESOURCES = [\"references/cli-reference.md\", \"references/integration-patterns.md\"]\n\nINTENT_MODEL = {\n    \"JEV_JUDGMENT\": {\"keywords\": [(\"ask jev\", 4), (\"jev judgment\", 4), (\"jev noul\", 4), (\"jev choice\", 4), (\"jev score\", 4), (\"jev urgency check\", 4), (\"jev yes or no\", 4), (\"jev probability\", 4), openrouter\", 3), (\"jev official provider\", 3), (\"jev auth status\", 3), (\"jev auth\", 3)]},\n    \"JEV_MCP\": {\"keywords\": [(\"jev mcp\", 3), (\"jev mcp host\", 3), (\"jev mcp server\", 3), (\"expose jev\", 3)]},\n}\n\nRESOURCE_MAP = {\n    \"JEV_JUDGMENT\": [\"references/cli-reference.md\", \"references/integration-patterns.md\"],\n    \"JEV_QUESTION\": [\"references/cli-reference.md\", \"assets/question-shaping-card.md\"],\n    \"JEV_PROVIDER\": [\"references/providers-and-models.md\"],\n    \"JEV_MCP\": [\"references/mcp-server.md\"],\n}\n\nLOAD_LEVELS = {\n    \"JEV_JUDGMENT\": \"ALWAYS\",\n    \"JEV_QUESTION\": \"CONDITIONAL\",\n    \"JEV_PROVIDER\": \"CONDITIONAL\",\n    \"JEV_MCP\": \"CONDITIONAL\",\n}\n\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [\n    \"Confirm whether the request is a judgment, a question to shape, a provider question or an MCP host question\",\n    \"Confirm which judgment type is needed: noul, choice, score or run\",\n    \"Confirm the question and the state the judgment is scored against\",\n    \"Confirm a credential resolves for the selected provider before a judgment is expected\",\n]\n\nAMBIGUITY_DELTA = 1\n\ndef _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) are routable: {relative_path}\")\n    return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()\n\ndef discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:\n    docs = []\n    for base in RESOURCE_BASES:\n        if base.exists():\n            docs.extend(path for path in base.rglob(\"*.md\") if path.is_file())\n    return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}\n\ndef get_routing_key(task, intents: list[str]) -> str:\n    override = str(getattr(task, \"routing_key\", \"\")).strip().lower()\n    if override:\n        return override\n    return (intents[0] if intents else \"unknown\").lower()\n\ndef classify_intents(user_request, task=None):\n    text = (user_request or \"\").lower()\n    scores = {intent: 0 for intent in INTENT_MODEL}\n    for intent, cfg in INTENT_MODEL.items():\n        for keyword, weight in cfg[\"keywords\"]:\n            if keyword in text:\n                scores[intent] += weight\n\n    ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda pair: pair[1], reverse=True)\n    primary, primary_score = ranked[0]\n    if primary_score == 0:\n        return (\"JEV_JUDGMENT\", None, scores)\n\n    secondary, secondary_score = ranked[1]\n    if secondary_score > 0 and (primary_score - secondary_score) <= AMBIGUITY_DELTA:\n        return (primary, secondary, scores)\n    return (primary, None, scores)\n\ndef route_jev_resources(user_request, task=None):\n    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()\n    primary, secondary, scores = classify_intents(user_request, task)\n    intents = [primary] + ([secondary] if secondary else [])\n    routing_key = get_routing_key(task, intents)\n    loaded, seen = [], set()\n\n    def load_if_available(relative_path: str):\n        guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)\n        if guarded in HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Transport Guard\n\nJev does not dispatch itself. Two bounds apply unchanged by this packet:\n\n- **No spawn chain, by construction.** Jev cannot start an agent, a CLI or a loop: it has no `Task`,\n  file or process tools, and each call returns one value and exits. No runtime refusal backs this.\n  The deep-loop recursion guard checks fan-out lineage and the dispatch stack only for a registered\n  `ExecutorKind`, and Jev has none, so the tool surface is the whole bound.\n- **A transport pairs with a workflow before any effecting operation.** The judgment selects; the\n  workflow acts. A `choice` answer is evidence about the caller's options, never permission.\n\n### Transport Selection\n\nA `choice` or `noul` question can run on either backend. With no transport named, Pi's classifier\nruntime answers when its preflight passes and the `jev` CLI answers otherwise with no skip line. A\nroute that names Pi keeps its one skip line when Pi cannot answer. The switch is resolved per call in\n`shared/scripts/jev-transport.mjs` (`resolveTransport`):\n\n| Input | Route |\n|---|---|\n| `JEV_TRANSPORT` unset or `''`, and no `transport` option | the automatic route: Pi when its preflight passes, otherwise the `jev` CLI with no line |\n| `JEV_TRANSPORT=jev` | the `jev` CLI, silently |\n| `JEV_TRANSPORT=pi`, or the per-call `transport: 'pi'` option | Pi for a `choice` or `noul` request, with one skip line and then the CLI when Pi cannot answer |\n| any other value | one line `skip: unknown transport '<value>', using jev CLI`, then the CLI |\n\nThe per-call option wins over the environment, except that a `JEV_TRANSPORT=jev` kill switch forces the\nCLI. Only `''` counts as unset, and an empty `transport` option is unset too. The environment being\nread is the `env` object the caller already passes to `jev`, never `process.env`, so a narrow env\nmeans the CLI.\n\n**`choice` and `noul`.** The Pi route is entered when the arguments are the declared `choice` shape,\n`choice [--provider <p>] [-q <text>] (-o <key>=<desc>)+`, or the declared `noul` shape,\n`noul -q|--question <text> [--provider <name>]`, with the state on stdin. Any other flag keeps the call\non the CLI; every other invocation, including `auth`, `score`, `run` and a call with an unmappable\nflag, is spawned there unchanged and prints nothing.\n\n**Provider map.** The transport uses the call's `--provider`, then `JEV_PROVIDER`, defaulting to\n`official`. `official` maps to Pi `typesafe/jev-latest`; `openrouter` maps to Pi\n`openrouter/typesafe/jev-1.13`. `vercel` and `custom` stay on the CLI. The preflight cache is keyed by\n`PATH` and the Jev provider.\n\n**Four gates, then the backend.** `ModelRuntime.create()` is imported from the package `pi` resolves\nto. The gates run in order before any classifier call, and the first failure stops the Pi path. On a\nroute that named Pi the failure prints exactly one line and then runs the CLI:\n\n| Gate | Failure line |\n|---|---|\n| package: `resolvePiPackage` resolves, and `ModelRuntime.create()` does not throw | `skip: pi transport unavailable (package), using jev CLI` |\n| version: the resolved package is 0.99.2 | `skip: pi transport unavailable (version), using jev CLI` |\n| model: `getModelOfType('classifier', piProvider, classifierId)` returns the mapped model | `skip: pi transport unavailable (model), using jev CLI` |\n| credential: `getAvailableOfType('classifier', piProvider)` lists the mapped `classifierId` | `skip: pi transport unavailable (credential), using jev CLI` |\n| backend: `classify()` throws or errors, or the answer cannot be read as the submitted question | `skip: pi transport unavailable (backend), using jev CLI` |\n\nThe call is `runtime.classify(model, context, { signal })` under the caller's own timeout, and its answer\nis written back on stdout in the CLI's shape: `answers.answer.choice` with `answers.answer.probabilities`,\n`answers.answer.noul` as a probability, a top-level `model`, `usage` with `input_tokens` and\n`output_tokens` when Pi reports token counts, compact JSON with a trailing newline, and\nexit code 0. A caller keeps its parsing. No retry runs inside the transport. A failed preflight on the\nautomatic route falls back to the CLI with no line, and a failure after the gates pass falls back on\neither route. Pi receives the stdin text as `state: { text: <stdin> }`, because its state must be a JSON\nobject while the CLI sends the bare string. Measured against the CLI's answers on recorded rows, the\n`text` key came closer to them than the earlier `request` key. Every outcome also names the route that answered as\n`transport` and the model that answered as `model`, which is `<provider>/<model>` from Pi's result when\nPi answered, such as `typesafe/jev-latest`, the `model` field the CLI printed when the CLI answered, or\n`null` when neither names one.\n\n**Credentials stay in Pi's store.** The transport calls `ModelRuntime.create()` and lets Pi resolve its\nown credential. It reads no `.env`, prints no environment variable and copies no key into Pi's options.\nOn `official`, Pi can answer only when the caller's process environment holds `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or Pi's\nown store holds a `typesafe` key. The `env` object reaches the `jev` child only.\n\nA Pi answer carries the same standing as a CLI answer: evidence about the caller's options, never\npermission to act.\n\n### Execution Ownership\n\nThe calling agent owns the question, the state and the consequence. Jev owns one thing: the typed\nanswer. Nothing in this packet decides what to do with it.\n\n### The Dispatch Shape\n\n```bash\njev noul -q 'Does this message express urgency?' -s 'Please restore service today.' --value </dev/null\njev choice -q 'Which team should handle this?' -s @state.txt \\\n  -o billing='Payment, charge, or refund issues' -o technical='Bugs or integration failures' --pretty\njev score -q 'How severe is this incident?' -s @state.txt \\\n  -l 'no user impact' -l 'degraded' -l 'outage' --value\njev run @request.json --pretty\n```\n\nThe grammar is positional and small: one subcommand, `-q/--question`, a state from\n`-s/--state` (text, `@file`, or `-`), and the type-specific criteria (`-o` pairs for `choice`, `-l`\nlevels for `score`, a JSON request for `run`). `--provider`, `--model`, `--json-state`, `--pretty`\nand `--value` are shared across the judgment subcommands; `--endpoint` exists but is hidden from\nhelp.\n\n### Output Contract\n\nDefault output is compact JSON on stdout, `--pretty` indents it, and `--value` prints only the\nprimary answer (`noul` → probability, `choice` → the selected key, `score` → the zero-based\nposition, which may be fractional). Errors are structured JSON on **stderr** with `ok: false`, and\nthe process exit code carries the class.\n\n| Exit | Meaning | Caller's move |\n|---|---|---|\n| 0 | A judgment was produced | Read the payload; it is a judgment, not a fact |\n| 1 | Unexpected or unclassified API response | Do not retry blindly; inspect the body |\n| 2 | Usage error: bad flags, unreadable state, malformed JSON, or `--value` with `run` | Fix the command; no quota was spent |\n| 3 | Credential missing, empty or rejected (401/403) | Operator step: set the key, then re-run |\n| 4 | Retryable transport: 429, 5xx, connection or timeout | Back off and retry; never read as a judgment |\n| 130 | Interrupted | Operator aborted |\n\n### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas\n\n1. **State defaults to stdin.** Omit `-s` and Jev reads stdin to EOF; on an inherited terminal that\n   is a hang with no output. Every non-interactive dispatch closes or feeds stdin.\n2. **`--value` is unavailable with `run`** and the CLI only says so *after* a successful call,\n   because the check runs on the parsed answer. Batched requests always need the JSON.\n3. **Cardinality is enforced by the MCP tools, not by the CLI.** `choice` with one option and\n   `score` with one level both reach the provider from the shell and both are refused by `jev-mcp`.\n   Treat two as the floor in either direction.\n4. **The credential store is the CLI's own.** `~/.config/jev-cli/credentials.json` (or\n   `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/jev-cli/credentials.json`), directory `0700`, file `0600`, written atomically.\n   It is not shared with any other tool that uses the same upstream key.\n5. **`custom` sends its bearer to whatever endpoint you name.** Point it at a trusted HTTPS origin,\n   and expect the native System One request and response shape, not chat completions.\n6. **`vercel` is translated.** The client rewrites `noul` to `boolean`, moves the model id into an\n   `ai-model-id` header and normalizes the answer back, so a response you compare across providers\n   is the normalized one, not the wire one.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n- Run `command -v jev && jev --version` before the first dispatch of a session, and `jev auth status`\n  before the first judgment.\n- Choose the narrowest question type: `noul` for a yes/no probability, `choice` for one key from\n  explicit options, `score` for an ordered level, `run` only for several questions at once.\n- Close or feed stdin whenever the state arrives from stdin.\n- Give `choice` keys that are stable output values and descriptions that make the categories\n  mutually exclusive; give `score` levels in ascending order from lowest to highest.\n- Read the exit code before the payload, and treat exit 4 as retryable transport rather than an\n  answer.\n- Send only the state the judgment needs, stripped of credentials and private records.\n- Keep the consequence behind the caller's authorization; a judgment is input to a decision, not the\n  decision.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n- Never inline an API key on the command line, print it, or commit it.\n- Never run `jev-mcp` by hand, and never claim a repo file wires an MCP host.\n- Never pass `--value` with `run`, and never pass a single option or level where the type requires\n  a choice or a scale.\n- Never let a judgment stand in for a repository fact this repo can answer directly.\n- Never claim a provider is reachable without a key that resolves: `auth status` or `auth test` is\n  the evidence.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n- No provider credential exists for the selected provider: report the operator step rather than\n  routing around it.\n- The selected provider returns 401/403 after a key was believed present: the key is stale, and\n  rotation is the operator's.\n- A `custom` endpoint must be reached: confirm the operator trusts the origin, because the bearer\n  travels with the request.\n- A judgment would drive an irreversible action: the operator owns that call, not the model.\n\n---\n\n## 5. REFERENCES\n\n### Core References\n\n- `references/cli-reference.md` — every subcommand, flag, input form, exit code and output shape.\n- `references/providers-and-models.md` — the four providers, their key variables, endpoints, default\n  models and translation behavior.\n- `references/integration-patterns.md` — the shipped judgment patterns: gate, triage, branch, batch.\n- `references/mcp-server.md` — the `jev-mcp` stdio server, its four tools, and the host-only rule.\n\n### Templates and Assets\n\n- `assets/question-shaping-card.md` — how to phrase a jev question so the answer is usable.\n- `manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md` — deterministic scenarios with expected\n  observables.\n- `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md` — the capability index with source anchors.\n\n### Evidence Base\n\n- Contract pin: `specs/cli-jev/001-cli-jev-creation/001-jev-contract-research-and-pin/implementation-summary.md`,\n  with the captured probes beside it at `scratch/probe-matrix.txt` and `scratch/probe-surface.txt`.\n- Vendored source: `specs/cli-jev/001-cli-jev-creation/context/jev-cli-main/`\n  (read-only; `src/jev_cli/__init__.py` is the CLI contract and `src/jev_cli/mcp_server.py` the MCP\n  contract).\n\n---\n\n## 6. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\n### Dispatch Completion\n\nA judgment dispatch is complete when it exits 0, the payload parses, the answer shape matches the\nquestion type (`noul` a number in `[0, 1]`, `choice` one of the submitted keys, `score` a position\nin the submitted list), and the caller has recorded which provider and model produced it.\n\n### Packet Quality\n\nA reader can decide whether to use Jev, compose a correct command for all four judgment types, wire\na provider, recognize every exit class, and know that `jev-mcp` belongs to a host — without opening\nanother packet.\n\n---\n\n## 7. INTEGRATION POINTS\n\n### Hub Integration\n\n`cli-jev` is the packet of mode `cli-jev` in the `cli-classifier` hub and its only registered mode today. A future classifier backend joins the same parent hub as a new mode with its own packet. It is declared in `mode-registry.json` as `packetKind: \"transport\"` under the `transport-axis` extension,\n`mutatesWorkspace: false`, forbidding `Write`, `Edit` and `Task`, and it routes by hub membership\nlike every other mode. `hub-router.json` carries its intent signal and `leaf-manifest.json` its\nleaf set; the hub's `ROUTER.md` is the stage-two surface router, `router_state: active`, and maps\nthis mode's judgment, question, provider and MCP intents to its leaves.\n\n### Not a Deep-Loop Executor\n\nJev cannot run a lineage: it has no file tools, no iteration model and no stop policy. `/deep:research`\nand `/deep:review` do not accept it, and no `ExecutorKind` exists for it. A lineage that needs a\njudgment gets one from a workflow executor and reads the result.\n\n### Code and Spec Integration\n\n- A gate or hook may call `jev noul --value` and compare the number to its own threshold; the\n  threshold is the gate's, and the judgment is only one input to it.\n- A triage step may call `jev choice` or `jev score` and switch on the returned key or position.\n- Nothing here writes to a spec packet, and the judgment is not evidence until a human or a check\n  confirms the consequence.\n\n### Tool Roles\n\n- **Bash**: runs `jev`; the only surface this packet uses.\n- **Read / Glob / Grep**: read the state file, the request JSON, and this packet's references.\n- **Write / Edit / Task**: forbidden. A transport that edits is a workflow wearing the wrong\n  `packetKind`.\n\n---\n\n## 8. It carries no procedure of its own: it decides which mode owns the\ndecision in front of you and hands over. The work lives in the modes.\n\n---\n\n## 1. WHEN TO USE\n\nUse this hub when the question is what a surface should look like, why it looks wrong, or what\nvisual artifact answers it: spacing, type, colour, contrast, hierarchy, a review of an existing\nsurface against design criteria, a data chart, or a process diagram. The surface can be screen UI, a\nslide deck, a printed page or a document layout.\n\n### When NOT to Use\n\n- **Measuring a surface that already exists into a written specification.** That is this hub's\n  EXTRACT mode, reached by naming the source; it is not the values path.\n- **Authoring documentation prose.** `sk-doc` owns that, including READMEs, changelogs and playbooks.\n- **Implementing the values once decided.** `sk-code` owns the code that renders them; this hub\n  decides what they should be and never writes the component.\n- **A canvas question that names its own form.** A chart or diagram request goes to its mode\n  directly rather than through the values mode.\n\n---\n\n## 2. SMART ROUTING\n\nRouting is **registry-driven at runtime and mode-authored at source**, in two stages. Stage 1\n(hub → mode): the advisor scores this hub as one identity, then `mode-registry.json` and\n`hub-router.json` pick the mode without re-deriving mappings during a request. Stage 2\n(mode → leaves): the root `ROUTER.md` maps the design intent to the exact mode-local resources that\nmode loads. The two layers stay separate: the hub never emits leaf paths, and the surface router\nnever re-decides the mode.\n\n> **Compiled routing (default-on, flag-gated, additive).** Resolve the mode via the compiled router contract first:\n>\n> node .skilled/bin/compiled-route.cjs --hub sk-design --prompt \"<task>\"\n>\n> Follow the returned decision. A `route` names its targets, a `clarify` or `defer` asks for disambiguation, and a `reject` refuses. On a `{\"servingAuthority\":\"legacy\"}` sentinel or any error, use the routing below. The front door self-gates on serving authority. Compiled routing is now the default for this hub. Set `SPECKIT_COMPILED_ROUTING=0` to force legacy routing fleet-wide, the explicit kill-switch.\n\n| Mode | Command | Owns | Reach it by asking about |\n|------|---------|------|--------------------------|\n| `sk-design-fundamentals` | routes via aliases | The values a surface is built from, and reviewing a surface against them | spacing, padding, type scale, colour, contrast, hierarchy, design review |\n| `sk-design-md-generator` | `/design:extract` | Measuring an existing surface into a Style Reference, and validating one | extract, design.md, design tokens, style reference, from a url |\n| `sk-design-chart` | `/design:chart` | Chart forms: which one answers the question, and building it as a self-contained file | chart, plot, heatmap, bar chart, chart catalog |\n| `sk-design-diagram` | `/design:diagram` | Flowcharts and text diagrams | diagram, flowchart, ascii diagram, mermaid, drawio |\n\nFour modes. Fundamentals and the generator are complements rather than alternatives: one decides values, the other reads values back\noff something that already exists. A request that names an existing surface belongs to the\ngenerator; a request that asks what a value should be belongs to fundamentals.\n\n### Surface Router, per-intent leaf sets\n\nStage 2 lives in `ROUTER.md` at the hub root, beside this file. It defines the five-intent leaf\nmodel (VALUES, REVIEW, CHART, FLOWCHART, EXTRACT), the machine-readable `INTENT_SIGNALS` and\n`RESOURCE_MAP` block the deterministic router-replay parses, and the how-to-read rules: a dominant\nintent takes one leaf set, near-tied intents take a deduped union, and no keyword match is the hub's\nUNKNOWN fallback rather than a silent default. Every `RESOURCE_MAP` path resolves on disk and\ndual-reads to a canonical `(workflowMode, leafResourceId)` pair through `leaf-manifest.json`.\n\n`ROUTER.md` stays a separate document on purpose. The machine block must not move into this file,\nwhere a replay would read it as the hub's own router and lose the mode projection, nor into\n`hub-router.json`, which is a different schema.\n\n### The discriminator\n\n- **`workflowMode`** — the public mode key: `sk-design-fundamentals`, `sk-design-md-generator`,\n  `sk-design-chart`, `sk-design-diagram`.\n- **`packetKind`** — `workflow` for all four. There is no surface axis on this hub.\n- **`backendKind`** — `surface-router` for fundamentals and the generator, which resolve leaves from\n  a reference set; `template-scaffold` for chart and diagram, which build an artifact from a form.\n\n### Routing rule\n\n```\nSKILL_ROOT  = path containing this SKILL.md\nREGISTRY    = SKILL_ROOT / \"mode-registry.json\"\nHUB_ROUTER  = SKILL_ROOT / \"hub-router.json\"\n\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [\n    \"Confirm whether this decides a value, reviews a surface, measures an existing surface, or builds a chart or diagram\",\n    \"Confirm the surface: screen UI, slide deck, printed page, document layout, or a chart or diagram canvas\",\n    \"For a measure request, provide the live URL or path; there is nothing to read without one\",\n    \"For a canvas request, state the question the artifact must answer, not the form you want\",\n]\n\ndef _guard_in_skill(relative_path):\n  resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()\n  resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)\n  if resolved.suffix.lower() not in {\".md\", \".json\", \".css\"}:\n    raise ValueError(\"only skill-local markdown/json/css router resources are routable\")\n  return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()\n\ndef load_if_available(relative_path, seen):\n  guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)\n  if guarded not in seen and (SKILL_ROOT / guarded).exists():\n    load(guarded)\n    seen.add(guarded)\n    return True\n  return False\n\nseen = set()\nif not REGISTRY.exists() or not HUB_ROUTER.exists():\n  return defer(\"router metadata missing; inspect sk-design/mode-registry.json and sk-design/hub-router.json\")\n\nread mode-registry.json and hub-router.json\nclassify the request to one or more workflowMode values using hub-router.json\n  (dominant design intent; a command like /design:chart resolves directly)\n\nif two intents tie within routerPolicy.ambiguityDelta:\n  apply routerPolicy.tieBreak, then take the deduped union of their leaf sets\n  VALUES and REVIEW resolving together is not ambiguity: they are one mode loading both sets\n\nif confidence is low or the intent is contradictory:\n  return UNKNOWN_FALLBACK with disambiguation_checklist = UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST\n\nfor each resolved workflowMode:\n  entry = the matching mode-registry.json modes[] item\n  if entry is missing or entry.packetKind != \"workflow\":\n    return defer(\"unknown sk-design workflowMode; extend mode-registry.json and create the mode first\")\n  if not load_if_available(f\"{entry.packet}/SKILL.md\", seen):\n    return defer(\"registered mode SKILL.md is missing; repair the mode before routing\")\n\nreturn single or ambiguous according to hub-router.json routerPolicy.outcomes\n```\n\n`routerPolicy.defaultMode` is `sk-design-fundamentals`: a design question with no clearer owner is a\nvalues question. That differs from `sk-doc`, whose default is `null` because an unclear documentation\nintent has no safe default. Outcomes are `single`, `ambiguous` or `none`.\n\n### Why a registry row proves nothing\n\nNested modes carry `routingClass: metadata`, so they are resolved by hub membership and hold no\nadvisor entry of their own: their vocabulary reaches the advisor only through this hub's\n`graph-metadata.json` `intent_signals`. A row in the registry, a keyword in `description.json` and a\ngreen gate all leave a request unable to arrive. Only replaying the request proves it does, and\n`ci-router-vocabulary-reach.cjs` probes every phrase this hub's router advertises for exactly that.\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Layout\n\n```\nsk-design/\n├── SKILL.md                 routing only; this hub authors nothing\n├── ROUTER.md                stage two: which resources a chosen mode loads\n├── mode-registry.json       what modes exist, and what each may touch\n├── hub-router.json          signals, vocabulary classes, tie-break\n├── graph-metadata.json      the only vocabulary the advisor scores\n├── command-metadata.json    the commands this hub owns, and which mode owns each\n├── shared/scripts/          tooling both canvas modes use\n├── sk-design-fundamentals/  the values mode, and everything it owns\n├── sk-design-md-generator/  the extraction mode, its engine and style corpus\n├── sk-design-chart/         the chart corpus, its checker, gallery and screenshots\n└── sk-design-diagram/       the diagram forms, their validator and screenshots\n```\n\nPer-mode behaviour is **not flattened**: each mode keeps its own contract, references, assets and\nscripts. This hub has no root `references/` or `assets/` directory, and mode resources stay inside\ntheir owning mode.\n\n---\n\n## 4. REFERENCES\n\n| Resource | Purpose |\n|----------|---------|\n| `mode-registry.json` | What modes exist, and what each may touch |\n| `hub-router.json` | Signals, vocabulary classes, tie-break |\n| `ROUTER.md` | Stage two: which resources a chosen mode loads |\n| `sk-design-fundamentals/` | The values mode, and everything it owns |\n| `sk-design-md-generator/` | The extraction mode, its engine and its style corpus |\n| `sk-design-chart/` | The chart corpus, its checker and its gallery |\n| `sk-design-diagram/` | The diagram forms and their validator |\n| `command-metadata.json` | The commands this hub owns, and which mode owns each |\n\n---\n\n## 5. WHEN TO USE\n\n### What is a Spec Folder?\n\nA **spec folder** is a numbered directory (e.g., `007-auth-feature/`) that contains documentation for a single feature/task or a coordinated packet of related phase work:\n\nSpec folders may also be nested as coordination-root packets with direct-child phase folders (e.g., `specs/02--track/022-feature/011-phase/002-child/`).\n\n- **Purpose**: Track specifications, plans, tasks, and decisions for one unit of work\n- **Location**: Under `specs/` using either `###-short-name/` at the root or nested packet paths for phased coordination\n- **Contents**: Markdown files (spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md, and implementation-summary.md when work is complete) plus optional support folders such as `scratch/`, `research/`, or `review/`\n\nThink of it as a \"project folder\" for AI-assisted development - it keeps context organized and enables session continuity.\n\n### Activation Triggers\n\n**MANDATORY for ALL file modifications:**\n- Code files: JS, TS, Python, CSS, HTML\n- Documentation: Markdown, README, guides\n- Configuration: JSON, YAML, TOML, env templates\n- Templates, knowledge base, build/tooling files\n\n**Request patterns that trigger activation:**\n- \"Add/implement/create [feature]\"\n- \"Fix/update/refactor [code]\"\n- \"Modify/change [configuration]\"\n- Positive keywords include add, implement, fix, update, create, modify, rename, delete and configure. The authoritative Gate 3 classifier intentionally omits `analyze`, `decompose` and `phase` from positive triggers; `analyze` is a read-only disqualifier unless a real write, memory-save or resume trigger is also present.\n\n**Example triggers:**\n- \"Add email validation to the signup form\" → Level 1-2\n- \"Refactor the authentication module\" → Level 2-3\n- \"Fix the button alignment bug\" → Level 1\n- \"Implement user dashboard with analytics\" → Level 3\n\n### When NOT to Use\n\n- Pure exploration/reading (no file modifications)\n- Single typo fixes (<5 characters in one file)\n- Whitespace-only changes\n- Auto-generated file updates (package-lock.json)\n- User explicitly selects Option D (skip documentation)\n\n**Rule of thumb:** If modifying ANY file content → Activate this skill.\nStatus: ✅ This requirement applies immediately once file edits are requested.\n\n### Distributed Governance Rule\n\nAny agent writing authored spec folder docs (`spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `acceptance-criteria.md`, `implementation-summary.md`, `decision-record.md`, `handover.md`, `review-report.md`, `debug-delegation.md`, `resource-map.md`, `goal.md`, `before-after.md`, `timeline.md`, `roadmap.md` (the last six optional)) MUST use contract-backed templates through `create.sh` or the inline renderer. `goal.md` may also come from `/create:goal`, whose per-kind templates are parity-checked copies of `goal.md.tmpl`. SMART ROUTING\n\n### Resource Domains\n\nThis skill uses simple intent/domain routing, not keyed runtime resource routing. It does not select whole `references/<key>/` or `assets/<key>/` subtrees from project, mode, stack, or model signals. Instead, the router discovers markdown resources recursively from `references/` and `assets/`, then applies intent scoring from `RESOURCE_MAP` to load real, guarded resources from the current inventory. Keep this section domain-focused rather than static file inventories.\n\n- `references/retrieval/` for the trigger-index lookup and the ripgrep recipes.\n- `references/memory/` for continuity save workflows, trigger-phrase behavior, and the shared embedding stack.\n- `references/templates/` for level selection, template selection, and structure guides.\n- `references/validation/` for checklist policy, verification rules, decision formats, and template compliance contracts.\n- `references/structure/` for folder organization and sub-folder versioning.\n- `references/workflows/` for command workflows, shared intake, rename procedures, and worked examples.\n- `references/debugging/` for troubleshooting and root-cause methodology.\n- `references/cli/` for daemon CLI behavior, shared smart-router behavior, and continuity handback contracts.\n- `references/config/` for runtime environment configuration and launcher/lease contracts.\n- `assets/*.md` for shared decision matrices, template mapping, and parallel dispatch support.\n\n**Typed leaf projection (fleet routing standard).** system-spec-kit is a normal, registry-less single-mode skill whose sole workflow mode is `system-spec-kit` (there is no `mode-registry.json`). Its router routes ONLY into the `references/` and `assets/` doc corpora, so those are the only routable leaves: every one is enumerated in `leaf-manifest.json`, generated from `leaf-manifest.config.json` (`generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --write .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit`; byte-stable under `--check`). `leaf-aliases.json` binds each router-emitted root-relative path (e.g. `references/memory/memory-system.md`) to its typed `(system-spec-kit, leafResourceId)` identity so a deterministic router replay recovers real typed pairs against the manifest. The `RESOURCE_MAP` below names every leaf in that manifest under at least one intent, so each reference and asset is reachable through the router as well as by browsing; the manifest stays the inventory, and a leaf added to the corpus without an intent is a routing gap to close, not a browse-only tier. The rest of the package is deliberately NOT routable: `runtime/cli/`, `runtime/`, `shared/`, `templates/`, `changelog/` and other engine dirs are the spec-kit runtime, and `feature-catalog/` + `manual-testing-playbook/` are runtime-engine capability docs and behavior-test fixtures — no `RESOURCE_MAP` intent selects them, so they are excluded from `leafRoots` and never appear in the manifest. This is an intentionally thin router: it maps spec-folder workflow intents (plan, implement, complete, memory, phase, hooks, …) to a small set of reference docs, while the large playbook chiefly exercises validation and generator behavior rather than doc routing (most scenarios carry empty typed gold). \"/speckit:complete\": \"COMPLETE\",\n    \"/speckit:plan --intake-only\": \"INTAKE\",\n    \"/speckit:plan :with-phases\": \"PHASE\",\n    \"/speckit:search\": \"MEMORY\",\n    \"/speckit:save\": \"MEMORY\",\n    \"/speckit:resume\": \"MEMORY\",\n}\n\nLOADING_LEVELS = {\n    \"ALWAYS\": [DEFAULT_RESOURCE],\n    \"ON_DEMAND_KEYWORDS\": [\"deep dive\", \"full validation\", \"full checklist\", [\n        \"references/validation/phase-checklists.md\",\n        \"references/templates/template-guide.md\",\n        \"references/workflows/intake-contract.md\",\n    ],\n}\n\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [\n    \"Confirm whether this is planning, memory, validation, phase, debug, or completion work\",\n    \"Confirm the target spec folder or command surface\",\n    \"Provide one concrete file, error, or expected output\",\n    \"Confirm which verification gate must pass\",\n]\n\ndef _task_text(task) -> str:\n    parts = [\n        str(getattr(task, \"query\", \"\")),\n        str(getattr(task, \"text\", \"\")),\n        \" \".join(getattr(task, \"keywords\", []) or []),\n        str(getattr(task, \"command\", \"\")),\n    ]\n    return \" \".join(parts).lower()\n\ndef _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Allow markdown loads only within this skill folder.\"\"\"\n    resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()\n guarded.startswith(\"references/\"):\n                tail = guarded.removeprefix(\"references/\")\n                if \"/\" not in tail and \"-\" in Path(tail).stem:\n                    raise routable markdown docs for this skill only.\"\"\"\n    docs = []\n    for base in RESOURCE_BASES:\n        if base.exists():\n            docs.extend(p for p in base.rglob(\"*.md\") if p.is_file())\n    return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}\n\ndef score_intents(task) -> dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Weighted scoring from request text, keywords, and explicit command boosts.\"\"\"\n    text = _task_text(task)\n    scores = {intent: 0.0 for intent in INTENT_SIGNALS}\n\n    for intent, cfg in INTENT_SIGNALS.items():\n        for keyword in cfg[\"keywords\"]:\n            if keyword in text:\n                scores[intent] += cfg[\"weight\"]\n\n    command = str(getattr(task, \"command\", \"\")).lower()\n    for prefix, intent in COMMAND_BOOSTS.items():\n        if command.startswith(prefix):\n            scores[intent] += 6\n\n    return scores\n\ndef select_intents(scores: dict[str, float], ambiguity_delta: float = 1.0, max_intents: int = 2) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Return primary intent and secondary intent when scores are close.\"\"\"\n    ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda item: item[1], reverse=True)\n    if not ranked or ranked[0][1] <= 0:\n        return []\n\n    selected = [ranked[0][0]]\n    if len(ranked) > 1:\n        primary_score = ranked[0][1]\n        secondary_intent, secondary_score = ranked[1]\n        if secondary_score > 0 \"load_level\": \"UNKNOWN_FALLBACK\",\n            \"needs_disambiguation\": True,\n            \"disambiguation_checklist\": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST,\n            \"resources\": loaded,\n        }\n\n    # CONDITIONAL: intent-scored resources\n    matched_intents = []\n    for intent in intents:\n        before_count = len(loaded)\n        for relative_path in RESOURCE_MAP.get(intent, []):\n            load_if_available(relative_path)\n        if len(loaded) > before_count:\n            matched_intents.append(intent)\n\n    # ON_DEMAND: explicit deep-dive requests\n    text = load_if_available(relative_path)\n\n    if not loaded:\n        load_if_available(DEFAULT_RESOURCE)\n\n    result = {\"intents\": intents, \"intent_scores\": scores, \"resources\": loaded}\n    if not matched_intents:\n        result[\"notice\"] = f\"No knowledge base found for intent(s): {', '.join(intents)}\"\n    return result\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Core Workflow\n\n1. Gate 3 selects an existing, new, related, skipped, or phase spec folder before file changes.\n2. For new folders, estimate level from LOC, risk, affected systems, and verification needs; create from contract-backed templates.\n3. Keep phase parents lean: parent folders hold `spec.md`, `description.json`, and `graph-metadata.json`; child phases hold working docs.\n4. Clear both completion gates before claiming done: the priority-ordered checklist in the `tasks.md` verification section, and the closure verdict in `acceptance-criteria.md`. See Two Completion Gates below.\n5. Preserve continuity in `implementation-summary.md` or through canonical `/speckit:save` with `generate-context.js`.\n\n### Two Completion Gates\n\nLevel 2+ packets close through two different documents. They are often conflated, so keep the question each one answers distinct.\n\n| | `tasks.md` verification section | `acceptance-criteria.md` |\n|---|---|---|\n| Answers | Is the work done? | May the packet close? |\n| Unit | A checklist item | A criterion, written Given / When / Then |\n| Vocabulary | `[ ]` / `[x]`, tagged P0, P1 or P2 | `Met`, `Unmet`, `Waived`, `Superseded` |\n| Enforced by | `check-completion.sh` | `AC_CLOSURE` and `AC_COVERAGE` in `validate.sh` |\n| Blocks when | A P0 or P1 item is incomplete, an item carries no priority tag, or a completed P0/P1 item cites no evidence. P2 blocks only under `--strict` | Any criterion is still `Unmet`, or a `Waived` or `Superseded` row names a decision record that does not exist |\n\nThe two are linked rather than parallel. `AC_COVERAGE` requires every criterion's evidence to trace back into the merged tasks document, so `tasks.md` is where the proof lives and `acceptance-criteria.md` is where the verdict lives. A criterion marked `Met` with no traceable item behind it is the failure that rule exists to catch.\n\n`acceptance-criteria.md` is an optional add-on: `validate.sh` warns when a Level 2+ packet has none. Once the file exists, `AC_CLOSURE` is an error-severity gate on that packet.\n\n### Retrieval and Continuity\n\nRetrieval is file-based and needs no running service. Gate 1 resolves a prompt against the committed trigger index with `node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lookup-trigger-index.mjs --json -- \"<prompt>\"`, which exits `0` on candidates, `1` on a clean no-hit and `2` on a bad invocation or unreadable index. Free-text retrieval uses the literal ripgrep recipes in [`references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md`](references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md), scoped by track and packet through the trailing positional path. Those recipes are precise only because the corpus is regular: [`references/structure/grep-convention.md`](references/structure/grep-convention.md) holds the frontmatter, anchor, naming and body-preservation rules that `validate.sh` enforces on every spec document.\n\nRecovery walks the continuity ladder rather than inferring a session: `handover.md`, then the `_memory.continuity` frontmatter block, then packet-first spec docs, then the bounded context recipe. `/speckit:resume` owns that ladder. Saves go through `node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js`, invoked by `/speckit:save`; the writer updates the packet's continuity surfaces in place and there is no indexing hand-off afterwards.\n\nRegenerate the index with `node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/generate-trigger-index.mjs` after spec-doc frontmatter changes. The artifact at `runtime/data/trigger-index.json` is committed, so a fresh clone answers Gate 1 before anything is built.\n\n**Declared loss.** Semantic paraphrase matching, vector and BM25 fusion, decay scoring, access tracking, session dedup and causal traversal are gone and have no file-based successor. A lookup that matches nothing returns nothing; callers must say so plainly rather than degrading to a guess. What `trigger_phrases` never declared, the index cannot find — see `references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md` §8 for what belongs in that field.\n\n### Reranking\n\nModel-based cross-encoder/local-GGUF reranking was removed in the 014 deprecation: the local model path was removed in phase 003 and the local rerank sidecar skill was deleted in phase 004 (cloud rerankers were removed earlier in 022/013). Nothing reranks retrieval today. Ripgrep produces matches, paths and lines and never orders them by relevance; ordering is the caller's job, using the deterministic tuple in `references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md` §5. That tuple is a stable sort, not a relevance model. The `SPECKIT_CROSS_ENCODER`/`RERANKER_LOCAL` flags are no longer wired.\n\n### Security\n\n- `VOYAGE_API_KEY` is read from the process environment only. It must never be logged, written into spec docs, or persisted to disk by Spec Kit. Operators should set it in shell init files owned by the operator with mode `600`.\n- Tests may mutate env vars, but must restore them in `afterEach`. Production code paths should not treat mutable process env as request-time configuration.\n\n### Validation and Recovery\n\nRun `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <spec-folder> --strict` before completion claims. Validation errors block completion; warnings must be addressed or documented. Startup, resume, hook, goal plugin, code graph, and Code Graph readiness details live in `references/config/hook-system.md`, `.skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/skill-advisor-hook.md`, `.skilled/hooks/goal/goal-plugin.md`, `runtime/hooks/README.md` (Claude and OpenCode hook folders; OpenCode uses plugin-backed delivery), and the code graph references.\n\n### OpenCode Goal Plugin\n\nThe packet `goal.md` is the source of goal state. A session binds to it (`opencode_goal({ action: \"bind\", packetPath })` on OpenCode, `bin/goal.cjs bind <packet>` on Pi), the runtime injects the objective slice built from the file on every turn, and the per-session record under `.skilled/skills/.state/goal/` keeps only the pointer, liveness and telemetry. When an operator says \"set the goal\", \"bind the goal\", \"update the goal\" or \"resend the goal\" in conversation, that is this surface: render the parent's chat slice from the file and hand it over to be set, keep reminding while it stays unset and never stop work for it. `node .skilled/hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs packet <packet> --workspace <repo root>` prints it as `chat_slice`. What that slice contains and when it may be sent are section 4 of `sk-create-goal`'s [budget-and-handoff.md](../sk-doc/sk-create-goal/references/budget-and-handoff.md), and authoring or amending a `goal.md` is `/create:goal`'s. The OpenCode surface is `.skilled/plugins/opencode-goal.js` plus `.skilled/commands/goal-opencode.md`; it injects with `experimental.chat.system.transform`, observes lifecycle events through the plugin `event` hook, and exposes `opencode_goal` / `opencode_goal_status` plugin tools. Use [`.skilled/hooks/goal/goal-plugin.md`](../../hooks/goal/goal-plugin.md) for the operator contract, restart requirement, environment variables, validation commands, and boundary between raw `objective` and generated `goalPrompt`.\n\n### Code Graph and Search Routing\n\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. **Determine level (1/2/3/3+) before ANY file changes** - Count LOC, assess complexity/risk\n2. **Scaffold from contract-backed templates** - Use `create.sh` or `inline-gate-renderer`, NEVER create from scratch\n3. **Fill ALL placeholders** - Remove placeholder markers and sample content\n4. **Ask A/B/C/D when file modification detected** - Present options, wait for selection. **Child dispatch:** when `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` marks a non-interactive worker bound to a lineage directory, Gate 3 is pre-resolved to that directory and the worker does not ask. Interactive sessions always ask.\n5. **Prefer coordinated related packets before new top-level folders** - Check active and related specs, their scope, status, and Phase Documentation Map. When related work qualifies for phase decomposition, recommend one phased packet rather than separate single-spec folders.\n6. **Get explicit user approval before changes** - Show level, path, templates, approach. **Child dispatch:** when `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` marks a non-interactive worker bound to a lineage directory, record the approval request in that directory and continue. Interactive sessions always ask.\n7. **Use consistent folder naming** - `specs/###-short-name/` format\n8. **Clear both completion gates (Level 2+)** - The `tasks.md` verification checklist AND the `acceptance-criteria.md` closure verdict. Load both before claiming done; see §3 Two Completion Gates\n9. **Mark items `[x]` with evidence** - Include links, test outputs, screenshots\n10. **Complete P0/P1 before claiming done** - No exceptions\n11. **Suggest handover.md on session-end keywords** - \"continue later\", \"next session\"\n12. **Run validate.sh before completion** - Completion Verification requirement\n13. **Create implementation-summary.md at end of implementation phase (Level 1+)** - Document what was built\n14. **Suggest /speckit:save when session-end keywords detected OR after extended work (15+ tool calls)** - Proactive context preservation\n15. **Suggest Task-tool debug delegation after 3+ failed fix attempts on same error** - Do not continue without offering a fresh debugging pass\n16. **Apply the phased-packet preference without bypassing qualification** - Suggest `/speckit:plan :with-phases` only when phase complexity score >= 25 AND documentation level >= 3. If either condition fails, use a standard packet; if the work is new or unrelated, create a separate packet and evaluate that packet independently. A series parent is the exception: a different change to the same artifact as an existing packet in the same track joins or creates a series parent (`references/structure/phase-definitions.md` §2).\n17. **Route all code creation/updates through `sk-code`** - Full surface alignment is mandatory before claiming completion\n   - **Authoring-time vs review-time load**: `sk-code` is loaded at TWO distinct points in `/speckit:complete`. (a) Authoring-time (Step 10 development): when the implementation target is under `.skilled/skills/`, `.skilled/agents/`, `.skilled/commands/`, or `.opencode/specs/`, load the matching sk-code authoring checklist (`../sk-code/sk-code-opencode/assets/checklists/{surface}-authoring.md`) and, for `.opencode/specs/` targets, the system-spec-kit spec-folder docs (`references/workflows/spec-folder-authoring-checklist.md` + `references/workflows/spec-folder-write-recipe.md`) BEFORE the first write. (b) Review-time (Step 11 review): the existing `sk-code` code-review mode (findings-first baseline + router-selected surface evidence) overlay runs after writes complete. Authoring-time load surfaces invariants the writer needs to honor; review-time load catches drift the writer didn't honor. See the `cross_skill_authoring_load` block in `speckit-complete.yaml` for the YAML contract.\n18. **Route all documentation creation/updates through `sk-doc`** - Full alignment is mandatory before claiming completion\n19. **Enforce ToC policy from validation rules** - Only `research/research.md` may include a Table of Contents section; remove ToC headings from standard spec artifacts\n20. **Literal naming for AI-derived spec folders and phases** - When the AI (not the user) picks a spec-folder or phase slug, the name MUST describe the concrete work being built or fixed. Names must include a specific subject token (the component, behavior, or bug being addressed). Forbidden as standalone slugs: `remediation`, `cleanup`, `fix`, `phase-N`, `review-remediation`, `round-N`. Good remediation-packet examples: `fix-deep-review-p1-p2-findings-for-sk-doc-skill`, `harden-mcp-server-startup-races`, `fix-singleton-leak-in-launcher`. Good phase-decomposition examples: `data-model-design`, `api-implementation`, `ui-integration`. **Remediation-packet source/target rule** - remediation slugs MUST follow `NNN-fix-<source>-for-<target>` where: **Source** = the event or evidence that triggered the packet (e.g. `deep-review-p0-p1-findings`, `verdict-fail`, `audit-finding-NN`); **Target** = the specific component being remediated (e.g. `skill-local-benchmarks-format`, `trigger-index-generator`, `launcher-cache`). The source names WHERE the work comes from; the target names WHAT is being fixed. Do not conflate them: the thing being remediated is the target, not the source. Worked example: `007-fix-deep-review-p0-p1-findings-for-skill-local-benchmarks-format` (source=`deep-review-p0-p1-findings`, target=`skill-local-benchmarks-format`). This rule is documentation-layer guidance; `validate.sh` does not lint slugs today (operator decision; may be lifted in a follow-on packet).\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. **Create documentation from scratch** - Use templates only\n2. **Skip spec folder creation** - Unless user explicitly selects D\n3. **Make changes before spec + approval** - Spec folder is prerequisite. **Child dispatch:** when `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` marks a non-interactive worker bound to a lineage directory, record the approval request in that directory and continue. Interactive sessions always ask.\n4. **Leave placeholders in final docs** - All must be replaced\n5. **Decide autonomously update vs create** - Always ask user. When `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` marks a non-interactive child, record the update-or-create question with its default in the lineage directory and continue.\n6. **Claim done without clearing both completion gates** - Level 2+ requires the `tasks.md` verification checklist verified with evidence AND every `acceptance-criteria.md` criterion `Met`, `Waived` or `Superseded`\n7. **Proceed without spec folder confirmation** - Wait for A/B/C/D. **Child dispatch:** when `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` marks a non-interactive worker bound to a lineage directory, Gate 3 is pre-resolved to that directory and the worker does not ask. Interactive sessions always ask.\n8. **Skip validation before completion** - Completion Verification hard block\n9. **Add ToC sections to standard spec artifacts** - `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `acceptance-criteria.md`, `decision-record.md`, `implementation-summary.md`, `handover.md`, `debug-delegation.md`, and `resource-map.md` must not contain ToC headings\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. **Scope grows during implementation** - Run `upgrade-level.sh` to add higher-level templates (recommended), then auto-populate all placeholder content:\n   - Read all existing spec files (spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md, implementation-summary.md) for context\n   - Replace every placeholder marker pattern in newly injected sections with content derived from that context\n   - For sections without sufficient source context, write \"N/A - insufficient source context\" instead of fabricating content\n   - Run `check-placeholders.sh <spec-folder>` to verify zero placeholders remain (see level specifications reference for the full procedure)\n   - Document the level change in changelog\n2. **Uncertainty about level <80%** - Present level options to user, default to higher. When `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` marks a non-interactive child, record the level question with the higher level as its default in the lineage directory and continue.\n3. **Template doesn't fit requirements** - Adapt closest template, document modifications\n4. **User requests skip (Option D)** - Warn about tech debt, explain debugging challenges, confirm consent. When `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` marks a non-interactive child, record the skip request in the lineage directory with documentation kept as the default and continue.\n5. **Validation fails with errors** - Report specific failures, provide fix guidance, re-run after fixes\n\n---\n\n## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\nSuccess means the selected spec folder uses the right template set, placeholders and sample content are removed, links between packet docs work, continuity is saved or updated, Level 2+ `tasks.md` P0/P1 checklist items are verified with evidence, every `acceptance-criteria.md` criterion is `Met`, `Waived` or `Superseded`, and `validate.sh --strict` has no blocking errors.\n\n---\n\n## 6. INTEGRATION POINTS\n\nP0 blocks, P1 requires completion or approved deferral, and P2 is optional. Code updates route through `sk-code`; documentation updates route through `sk-doc`; git handoff routes through `sk-git`.\n\n### Quick Reference Commands\n\n| Command | Usage |\n| --- | --- |\n| Canonical intake | `/speckit:plan --intake-only \"Description\"` |\n| Create spec folder | `./runtime/cli/spec/create.sh \"Description\" --short-name name --level 2` |\n| Create in a track | Add `--track <track>` to the create command. When intake runs, the returned `start_state` is the canonical downstream field.\n\n**Remember**: This skill is the foundational documentation orchestrator. It enforces structure, template usage, context preservation, and workflow-required validation for all file modifications. Every conversation that modifies files MUST have a spec folder.\n\n---\n\n## 7. REFERENCES AND RELATED RESOURCES\n\nThe router discovers reference, asset, and script docs dynamically.
