It produces a standalone HTML chart from a corpus of chart forms that lives inside this packet.\n\n---\n\n## 1. WHEN TO USE\n\n### Activation Triggers\n\nUse this packet when the request involves:\n\n- Building a chart that plots data: a ranked comparison, a part-to-whole split, a time series, a distribution, a relationship or a matrix.\n- Deciding which chart form answers the comparison a reader needs to make.\n- Choosing or applying one of the packet's three stock colour systems, or a provenance-gated design-md delivery.\n- Applying a local v3 `DESIGN.md` Style Reference to a chart delivery.\n- Adding a chart form to the corpus, or checking that the corpus still renders.\n\nKeyword triggers: `create a chart`, `plot the data`, `data visualization`, `treemap`, `waterfall chart`, `heatmap`, `box plot`, `histogram`, `chart catalog`, `chart colour system`, `standalone html chart`, `DESIGN.md`, `style reference`, `measured site's look`, `theme a chart`.\n\n### When NOT to Use\n\nUse another `sk-doc` packet when:\n\n- The artifact explains a structure rather than plotting values. A flow, an architecture, a sequence or a state machine is `sk-design-diagram` work.\n- The request is about the prose around a chart rather than the chart. That is `sk-create-readme` or `sk-create-quality-control`.\n- The request asks to extract interface design values from a site. Extraction belongs to `sk-design-md-generator`; applying an already extracted local `DESIGN.md` stays here.\n\nThe boundary against `sk-design-diagram` is the one that actually gets tested, because that packet already names bar, line, scatter and radar in its own selection guide. The split is what the artifact carries. A diagram carries a structure a reader follows. A chart carries values a reader compares.\n\nThe hub router splits the two by name. `sk-design-diagram` keeps the bare type names it documents, which are `bar chart`, `line chart`, `scatter plot`, `radar chart`, `gantt chart` and `org chart`. This packet answers the form names that packet has no file for, such as `treemap`, `waterfall chart`, `heatmap`, `box plot` and `histogram`, plus the data-qualified phrasings `bar chart of`, `line chart of` and `scatter plot of`. A request that names a bare type and asks for a diagram reaches both, and the router asks which one rather than guessing.\n\n`radar chart` is the one name where the split by name and the split by artifact disagree, and the\ntwo documents used to answer it differently with nothing saying so. By name it goes to\n`sk-design-diagram`, which has a radar file and a type reference for it. By artifact it is values a\nreader compares, which is this side of the line, and `catalog.md` section 6 records why this corpus\ndraws no radar and what answers the same comparison instead: `parallel-axes`, one scale per axis\nrather than every dimension normalised onto one radial scale. Both hold, in that order. The name\nroutes to the diagram packet; a reader who arrives here comparing entities across several measures\nis handed `parallel-axes` rather than sent away. The disagreement is recorded rather than resolved,\nbecause resolving it means moving a file between packets and that is a decision about the hub.\n\n### Packet Boundary\n\nThis packet may create and edit chart artifacts, its own corpus and its own validator. It does not own the `sk-doc` hub identity, and it never carries its own `graph-metadata.json` or `description.json`.\n\n---\n\n## 2. SMART ROUTING\n\nThe hub resolves this packet through `mode-registry.json`. Routing below that point selects packet-local resources only.\n\n```python\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK = {\n    \"load_level\": \"UNKNOWN_FALLBACK\",\n    \"needs_disambiguation\": True,\n    \"resources\": [],\n}\n\ndef discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:\n    return {\n        path.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()\n        for path in SKILL_ROOT.rglob(\"*.md\")\n        if path.is_file()\n    }\n\ndef _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:\n    resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()\n    resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)\n    if resolved.suffix.lower() != \".md\":\n        raise ValueError(\"Only packet-local markdown resources are routable\")\n    return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()\n\ndef route_resources(request):\n    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()\n    selected = select_resources_for_request(request, inventory)\n    if not selected:\n        return UNKNOWN_FALLBACK\n    return {\n        \"resources\": [\n            _guard_in_skill(path)\n            for path in selected\n            if _guard_in_skill(path) in inventory\n        ]\n    }\n```\n\n### Resource Domains\n\n| Domain | Where it lives | Use |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Chart lookup | `references/catalog.md` | Turn the comparison a reader needs into one chart form and the file that draws it |\n| Chart forms | `assets/templates/` | One self-contained file per form, copied whole rather than extracted from |\n| Style References | `assets/style-reference/` | One directory per reference. Each owns its `DESIGN.md`, its `palettes.json` and its proof sheets, so adding a reference means deciding its colour rather than inheriting somebody else's |\n| Stock colour | `assets/style-reference/evilcharts/palettes.json` | The default reference's own palette: the three named systems, the corner ladder and the type scale every stock form reads, and what `--default` themes to |\n| Design Reference application | `scripts/apply-design-md.cjs`, `references/design-md-theming.md` | Derive a gated delivery palette from a local v3 `DESIGN.md` without fetching or changing stock forms; pass any other reference's path to override the stock one |\n| Template contract | `references/template-contract.md` | What a form file has to contain before the corpus check passes it |\n| Corpus validation | `scripts/` | Prove every form still renders after a change |\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\n\nThe workflow is template-first, and that is a constraint rather than a preference. A chart assembled from a form file renders the way that file already rendered. A chart written freehand does not, and the failure shows up in a browser rather than in a check.\n\n1. Read the request and name the comparison the reader needs to make.\n2. Open `references/catalog.md` and resolve that comparison to one row.\n3. Copy the file that row names. Do not rewrite its render code.\n4. Swap the data block for the reader's data.\n5. Apply one colour system from the default reference's palette. One per artifact.\n6. Keep the result a single self-contained file. It opens in a browser with no install step.\n7. Run the corpus check before reporting the result: `node scripts/check-corpus.cjs` over the packet, and `node scripts/check-corpus.cjs --extra <dir>` over a delivery written outside it. Both must print `RESULT: PASSED`.\n\nWhen the request names a `DESIGN.md`, a style reference or a measured site's look, route the\napplication branch to `scripts/apply-design-md.cjs`. It reads the v3 headings documented by\n`references/design-md-theming.md`, derives both grounds from local values, and writes themed\ncopies only after the corpus gates pass. A request that asks for themed charts without naming a\nreference runs it with `--default`, the evilcharts reference carried at `assets/style-reference/evilcharts/`. If the request asks to create the Style Reference itself,\nroute that extraction to `sk-design-md-generator`; this packet owns application, not extraction.\n\n### What the corpus holds\n\nTwenty-nine chart forms across six question families: comparison, composition, time, distribution, relationship and matrix. `references/catalog.md` is the index and the corpus check reads it in both directions, so a row naming a missing file and a file carrying no row both fail. One form is one file. There are no gallery pages to lift a block out of, because what reaches a reader is a delivery and a gallery ships every other form's demo data alongside the one they asked for. When no row answers the question in front of you, report the gap rather than improvising a form.\n\nThe corpus shares a measured visual register for card anatomy, type scale, bare axes, bar and line geometry, positioned HTML tooltip cards and keyed legend chips. Each template accepts `?scheme=light` or `?scheme=dark` and sets `data-scheme` before it paints, because a capture on a dark machine has no other way to see the light rendering.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n- Copy a form file that already renders, and change only its data block.\n- Apply exactly one colour system per artifact; a `design-md` delivery is accepted only with its provenance comment and both inline gate checks.\n- Produce a single self-contained file that opens with no install step.\n- Run the corpus check before reporting a result: `scripts/check-corpus.cjs` over the packet, `scripts/check-corpus.cjs --extra <dir>` over a delivery written outside it, and require `RESULT: PASSED` from both.\n- Author every chart and every palette in this packet.\n\n### ❌ NEVER\n\n- Never copy a template, a fragment or a snippet from an outside chart library into this packet. The corpus is authored here, and content under a license this repository cannot grant onward must not enter the tree.\n- Never write a chart freehand when a form for its question exists.\n- Never mix two colour systems in one artifact.\n- Never act as a separate advisor identity and never carry packet-level identity metadata.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n- No row in `references/catalog.md` answers the comparison the reader needs.\n- The request wants a structure rather than values, which puts it on the `sk-design-diagram` side of the boundary.\n- The corpus validator fails on a form you did not change.\n\n---\n\n## 5. REFERENCES\n\n- `README.md` - packet overview and navigation.\n- `references/README.md` - the reference index, which routes to the catalog, the colour systems and the template contract.\n- `../mode-registry.json` - authoritative packet registration.\n- `../hub-router.json` - parent routing policy.\n- `../ROUTER.md` - stage-two leaf selection.\n\n---\n\n## 6. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\n- The artifact is one self-contained file that opens in a browser.\n- The file traces back to one named row in `references/catalog.md`.\n- One colour system is applied throughout.\n- A local `DESIGN.md` can produce a deterministic, provenance-bearing delivery without changing stock forms or palettes.\n- The corpus check printed `RESULT: PASSED` over the packet, and `--extra <dir>` printed it over the delivered file.\n\n---\n\n## 7. INTEGRATION POINTS\n\n- Input: chart requests routed from the `sk-doc` hub.\n- Output: a standalone HTML chart.\n- Neighbour: `sk-design-diagram` owns structural visuals, and the two are separated by what the artifact carries rather than by which one was asked first.\n\n---\n\n## 8. SMART ROUTING\n\nRouting is two-stage. Stage 1 (hub → mode): the compiled router / `hub-router.json` scores the request and resolves it to one workflow mode — or an ordered bundle — per `mode-registry.json`. Stage 2 (mode → leaves): the surface router below maps the request's CLI-dispatch intent to the exact packet-local leaf resources that mode loads. The two layers stay separate: the hub never emits leaf paths, and the surface router never re-decides the mode. The surface router is a first-class document at the hub root — `ROUTER.md` — carrying the intent model, the machine-readable `INTENT_SIGNALS` / `RESOURCE_MAP` block, and the how-to-read rules.\n\n> **Compiled routing (default-on, flag-gated, additive).** Resolve the mode via the compiled router contract first:\n> ```bash\n> node .skilled/bin/compiled-route.cjs --hub cli-external-orchestration --prompt \"<task>\"\n> ```\n> Follow the returned decision — `route` (use its `targets`), `clarify`/`defer` (disambiguate), `reject` (refuse). On a `{\"servingAuthority\":\"legacy\"}` sentinel or any error, use the routing below. The front door self-gates on serving-authority. Compiled routing is now the default for `cli-external-orchestration`; set `SPECKIT_COMPILED_ROUTING=0` to force legacy routing fleet-wide — the explicit kill-switch.\n\n### Two-Axis Model\n\n- `packetKind: \"workflow\"` — `cli-opencode`, `cli-claude-code`, `cli-codex`, `cli-cursor`, `cli-devin`, `cli-pi`, and `cli-hermes` orchestrate a CLI binary and their dispatched writes land in THIS repo's workspace (`mutatesWorkspace:true`). None is a transport packet: all classify intent, choose/confirm a provider, and conduct the dispatched session. (`cli-cursor`'s native worktree/cloud-worker surfaces are opt-in escape hatches, not its default dispatch shape.)\n- No extension is declared: the `transport-axis` left with the `cli-jev` transport, no mode here is read-only evidence, and none converges on a loop. The seven workflows stay primary, independently-routable dispatch modes.\n\n### Routing Rule\n\n```text\nread hub-router.json\n  -> score routerSignals and vocabularyClasses\n  -> apply routerPolicy.tieBreak\n  -> read mode-registry.json for packetKind, backendKind, toolSurface, and advisorRouting\n  -> load the selected packet(s)\n```\n\n### Outcomes\n\n- `single`: one dominant executor signal routes to one mode.\n- `orderedBundle`: multiple explicitly requested executors route in tie-break order.\n- `defer`: unclear or contradictory dispatch intent asks for disambiguation — the router does not silently default to `cli-opencode` on genuine ambiguity.\n\n### Surface Router — per-mode leaf sets\n\nStage 2 of routing lives in `ROUTER.md` at the hub root, next to `SKILL.md` and `README.md`. It defines the per-mode leaf-intent model (every mode in `mode-registry.json`, plus the deliberate absence: a bare CLI-dispatch phrase that names no executor fires no intent and defers at the hub), the machine-readable `DEFAULT_RESOURCE` / `INTENT_SIGNALS` / `RESOURCE_MAP` block that the deterministic router-replay and benchmarks parse, and the how-to-read rules (dominant intent → one leaf set; near-tied intents → deduped union, the `orderedBundle` outcome; no keyword match → hub `defer`, never a silent default to `cli-opencode`). Every `RESOURCE_MAP` path is packet-qualified and converts to the canonical `(workflowMode, leafResourceId)` pair at the one contract boundary.\n\n`ROUTER.md` stays a separate document on purpose: the router-replay contract resolves the hub's mode from `hub-router.json` and reads the leaf sets from the surface document — the machine block must not move into `SKILL.md` (the replay would treat it as the hub's own router and lose the mode projection) or into `hub-router.json` (schema handoff-ambiguity rule).\n\n### Executor Delegation\n\nA prompt naming a specific executor (e.g. \"use cli-opencode\", \"delegate to opencode\", \"get a claude code second opinion\", \"delegate to codex\", \"delegate to cursor\", \"delegate to devin\", \"delegate to pi\", or a small model that dispatches through one) is resolved by the system-skill-advisor's executor-delegation scorer, which sources its alias table from THIS hub's `mode-registry.json` — keyed by each mode's `packetSkillName` — and resolves to `cli-opencode`, `cli-claude-code`, `cli-codex`, `cli-cursor`, `cli-devin`, `cli-pi`, or `cli-hermes`. See `system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/executor-delegation.ts`.\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Layout\n\n```text\ncli-external-orchestration/\n  SKILL.md\n  README.md\n  mode-registry.json\n  hub-router.json\n  description.json\n  graph-metadata.json\n  changelog/\n  feature-catalog/\n  manual-testing-playbook/\n  benchmark/\n  leaf-manifest.json\n  ROUTER.md\n  cli-opencode/\n    SKILL.md\n    README.md\n    references/\n    assets/\n    manual-testing-playbook/\n    changelog/\n  cli-claude-code/\n    SKILL.md\n    README.md\n    references/\n    assets/\n    manual-testing-playbook/\n    changelog/\n  cli-codex/\n    SKILL.md\n    README.md\n    references/\n    assets/\n    manual-testing-playbook/\n    changelog/\n  cli-cursor/\n    SKILL.md\n    README.md\n    references/\n    assets/\n    manual-testing-playbook/\n    changelog/\n  cli-devin/\n    SKILL.md\n    README.md\n    references/\n    assets/\n    manual-testing-playbook/\n    changelog/\n  cli-pi/\n    SKILL.md\n    README.md\n    references/\n    assets/\n    manual-testing-playbook/\n    changelog/\n  cli-hermes/\n    SKILL.md\n    README.md\n    references/\n    assets/\n    manual-testing-playbook/\n    changelog/\n```\n\n### Companion Metadata\n\n- `mode-registry.json` owns `workflowMode`, `packetKind`, `backendKind`, `toolSurface`, packet folder identity, alias phrases, and `advisorRouting`. Two asymmetries are deliberate and preserved: `cli-opencode` carries a parallel-detached carve-out that `cli-claude-code` intentionally does not, and `cli-pi` is exempt from the two layers that mean \"the caller is inside this CLI\" — Pi has no in-process delegation left, so refusing those would leave a Pi session no way to hand work out. The layers that bound a spawn chain, fan-out lineage and dispatch stack, apply to every mode without exception.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n- Resolve packets through `mode-registry.json`; never hardcode packet roots in prose-only logic.\n- Keep `SKILL.md` thin: routing, invariants, and navigation only.\n- Keep every packet in `modes[]` and give every packet a `packetKind`.\n- Keep a transport mode's policy surface minimal: `routingClass: \"metadata\"`, `mutatesWorkspace: false`, `Write`/`Edit`/`Task` forbidden, and the mode named in the `transport-axis` extension's `transports[]`. `tieBreak` lists workflow modes first, so a prompt that names no mode never resolves to a transport by ordering.\n- Keep exactly one `graph-metadata.json`, at the hub root.\n- Keep `hub-router.json` signal keys and registry `workflowMode` values bidirectionally aligned.\n- Keep the surface router's `RESOURCE_MAP` in sync with `leaf-manifest.json` — the leaf sets dual-read to canonical typed pairs at the one contract boundary (`sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/lib/leaf-resource-contract.cjs`).\n- Keep every `RESOURCE_MAP` path packet-qualified (`<packet>/references|assets/…`) and resolving on disk.\n- Treat the installed binary as the authority for flags and enum values, and `--help` as an incomplete summary of it. A value this skill documents but help omits is not thereby fabricated — several CLIs here accept aliases and legacy names their help text never prints. Before changing or reporting a documented flag value as invalid, probe the binary with an argument that forces parse-time validation without starting a billable session (e.g. pointing a file-taking flag at a nonexistent path: a rejected enum fails first, an accepted one reaches the file error). Enums also move between releases, so re-probe after an upgrade instead of trusting a recorded result.\n- Read the target mode's `SKILL.md` before composing any dispatch prompt (constitutional cli-dispatch-skill-preload rule) — the advisor recommendation alone does not waive this.\n- Attach the resolved agent persona to every external-CLI dispatch (AGENTS.md §9 runtime agent dir; the right agent per subtask, never a bare task) — each mode's `SKILL.md` carries the native-surface-vs-inline mechanic, and the canonical contract is `../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` \"Persona Injection\".\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n- Never add a second packet array.\n- Never add packet-local `graph-metadata.json` files.\n- Never let any mode dispatch itself from inside a fan-out lineage or a repeated dispatch stack — those bounds are non-negotiable for every mode. Whether being *inside* the target CLI also refuses is packet-owned, and `cli-pi` deliberately allows it.\n- Never let the executor CLI (the HOW) override the calling skill's own workflow (the WHAT) — \"use cli-opencode gpt-5.5 high\" still runs inside the caller's skill-owned route.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n- A packet cannot be classified as `workflow` or `transport` (every current mode is one of the two; a future mode may be neither — if it is read-only evidence it is a surface, and this hub would then need the surface-axis extension too).\n- Router signals, vocabulary classes, and registry modes cannot be made bidirectionally consistent.\n- The executor-delegation scorer resolves a delegation prompt to `cli-external-orchestration` itself instead of a real executor — that is the exact silent-misroute failure mode ADR-005 rewrote the scorer to prevent; report it rather than working around it.\n\n---\n\n## 5. REFERENCES\n\n- Registry: `mode-registry.json`.\n- Router: `hub-router.json`.\n- Surface router: `ROUTER.md`.\n- Advisor description: `description.json`.\n- Skill graph identity: `graph-metadata.json`.\n- Workflow packets: `cli-opencode/SKILL.md`, `cli-claude-code/SKILL.md`, `cli-codex/SKILL.md`, `cli-cursor/SKILL.md`, `cli-devin/SKILL.md`, `cli-pi/SKILL.md`, `cli-hermes/SKILL.md`.\n- Per-mode provider/model/invocation catalogs: each mode's `references/providers-and-models.md` is the dedicated single-source index of that mode's providers, model ids, personas/effort tiers, and dispatch shapes.\n- Executor-delegation scorer (hub-aware, sources from this hub's registry): `../system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/executor-delegation.ts`.\n- Constitutional CLI dispatch skill-preload rule: the retired constitutional rule docs.\n- Persona-injection contract (canonical): `../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` \"Persona Injection\" — every mode attaches the resolved agent persona on dispatch.\n"

The cli-X skills are for **cross-AI delegation only** — never self-invocation.\n\nOrchestrate Cognition's Devin CLI for tasks that benefit from a second AI perspective, multi-model selection (DeepSeek, GLM-5.2, GPT-5.6 Luna Max, Grok (4.5 and 4.6), SWE-2), subagent delegation with `run_subagent`, cloud handoff via `/handoff`, or parallel code generation.\n\n**Core Principle**: Use Devin for what it does best. WHEN TO USE\n\n### Activation Triggers\n\n- **Cross-AI Validation** — code review second perspective, security audit alternative analysis, bug detection, independent implementation attempts.\n- **Cloud Handoff** — long-running tasks, complex refactors, CI-like validation, browser-dependent workflows offloaded to a cloud Devin session via `/handoff`.\n- **Subagent Delegation** — specialized profile matches (`subagent_explore`, `subagent_general`, custom `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md` profiles), parallel task processing through Devin's native subagent system.\n- **Multi-Model Dispatch** — tasks that specifically want a model available through Devin's multi-model surface (DeepSeek, GLM-5.2, GPT-5.6 Luna Max, Grok (4.5 and 4.6), SWE-2), selected per-dispatch with `--model`.\n- **Parallel Code Generation** — offloading generation, simultaneous code generations, background docs/test generation through subagents.\n- **Specialized Generation** — explicit Devin requests, test suite generation, code translation, batch documentation, visual input via clipboard paste or `@` file mentions.\n\n### When NOT to Use\n\n- **You ARE Devin already.** If your runtime is Devin (detection signal: `$DEVIN_PROJECT_DIR` env var set, `devin` in process ancestry, or credentials present at `~/.local/share/devin/credentials.toml` while a session is active), this skill refuses to load. Self-invocation creates a circular dispatch loop and burns tokens for no value.\n- Simple, quick tasks where CLI overhead is not worth it, or tasks needing an immediate response (auth/network round-trips may delay).\n- Context already loaded and understood by the current agent.\n- Interactive refinement requiring the full-screen REPL (use `devin` directly instead).\n- Tasks where Devin CLI is not installed.\n\n---\n\n## 2. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Prerequisites\n\nInstall via `devin setup` (interactive wizard) or `curl -fsSL https://devin.ai/install | bash`. cli-devin authenticates through **Devin account OAuth** — run `devin auth login` and complete the browser flow (or `--force-manual-token-flow` for SSH/remote sessions). Full install, auth, flag, permission-mode, session, and troubleshooting tables live in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) — this section keeps only the routing decisions and dispatch-critical gotchas.\n\n### Execution Ownership\n\nThis packet owns user-facing routing, the `command -v devin` availability probe, prompt construction, and the self-invocation guard. Research and review lineages delegate process construction and execution to the already-shipped deep-loop runtime at `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs`, using executor kind `cli-devin`. That runner accepts only the `research` and `review` loop types, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5.\n\nThe runtime is the single Devin execution adapter. Do not add a packet-local wrapper, command builder, or spawn path. Direct `devin -p` snippets below are operator reference and manual-testing examples; research and review lineages use the shared runtime, and a one-shot dispatch uses the child envelope.\n\n### Provider Auth Pre-Flight (Devin Account OAuth)\n\n**MANDATORY before any first dispatch in a session.** cli-devin authenticates through Devin account OAuth only. If `devin auth login` has not been completed on this machine, a dispatch fails with an authentication error mid-round-trip. Run this check once per session, cache the result, and re-run it only if a dispatch fails with an auth error.\n\n```bash\n# One-shot pre-flight: capture Devin auth status for routing\nDEVIN_AUTH=$(devin auth status 2>&1)\necho \"$DEVIN_AUTH\" | grep -qi \"logged in\" && DEVIN_AUTH_OK=1 || DEVIN_AUTH_OK=0\n```\n\n**Decision tree** (apply in order — first match wins):\n\n| State | DEVIN_AUTH_OK | Action |\n|-------|---------------|--------|\n| OAuth ready | 1 | Proceed with `devin -p --model <model> --permission-mode <mode> -- \"<prompt>\"` |\n| Not logged in | 0 | **ASK user** to run `devin auth login` — surface the command, do NOT dispatch. Never substitute a different auth method or skip the check. |\n\n**User prompt template — not logged in:**\n\n```\nDevin is not authenticated on this machine. cli-devin uses Devin account OAuth only.\nRun `devin auth login` (browser flow; or `devin auth login --force-manual-token-flow` for SSH/remote),\nthen confirm when login finishes — the skill will retry the original dispatch.\n```\n\n**Error-recovery contract.** If a dispatch returns an auth error after pre-flight passed (OAuth expired or revoked), invalidate the cache, rerun `devin auth login`, and re-check before retrying. Never substitute a model the user didn't approve.\n\n### Default Invocation (Skill Default)\n\n**Default model + permission mode**: `swe` (alias → `swe-2`) · `dangerous` permission mode.\n\n```bash\ndevin -p \\\n  --model swe \\\n  --permission-mode dangerous \\\n  -- \\\n  \"<prompt>\"\n```\n\n> **Why `dangerous` is the default for implementation work.** Under `accept-edits` Devin may\n> edit files but every other tool call is refused with\n> `warning: rejected a tool call that requires confirmation`. In a non-interactive `-p` session\n> there is nobody to confirm, so the dispatch cannot read a module to check an export, cannot\n> grep, and cannot run the tests it was asked to run. The observed failure is not an error —\n> it is a dispatch that spends its whole budget exploring, writes nothing, and exits 0. A\n> caller who does not diff the worktree afterwards will read that as success.\n>\n> The marginal risk is smaller than the name suggests: `accept-edits` already grants arbitrary\n> file modification, which is the destructive capability. `dangerous` adds the ability to run\n> commands, which is what lets the executor verify its own work instead of handing back\n> unverified edits. Use `auto` for read-only review, analysis, and research, where no\n> elevation is needed.\n>\n> **`auto` is read-only, not tool-free.** It refuses any tool call that wants confirmation,\n> and a shell command counts even when the command only reads. Observed on 2026-09-15: a\n> crawl dispatched under `auto` decided on its own to run a `git` command to check state,\n> was refused with `warning: rejected a tool call that requires confirmation`, and exited 0\n> having reported almost nothing. A research dispatch that might shell out therefore needs\n> `dangerous` with a read-only instruction in the prompt, and the caller diffs the worktree\n> afterwards to confirm it wrote nothing. Reserve `auto` for a dispatch whose whole job is\n> reading files.\n\n**User override** (honor explicit user phrasing verbatim):\n\n| User says | Resolve to |\n|-----------|------------|\n| (nothing specified) | `--model swe-2-max --permission-mode dangerous` |\n\n> **Fan-out fallback:** a deep-loop lineage that pins no model runs **SWE 2 Max**. The family is named here on purpose, without a version or an effort tier, so this line does not go stale when the family ships a point release; the runner resolves the current id. A drift test keeps the two in the same family.\n| \"Use glm\" / \"Use glm high\" | `--model glm-5-2 --permission-mode dangerous` |\n| \"Use glm no-thinking\" | `--model glm-5-2-none --permission-mode dangerous` |\n| \"Use glm max\" | `--model glm-5-2-max --permission-mode dangerous` |\n| \"Use deepseek\" | `--model deepseek-v4-flash-max --permission-mode dangerous` |\n| \"Use swe max\" | `--model swe-2-max --permission-mode dangerous` |\n| \"Use glm accept-edits\" | `--model glm-5-2 --permission-mode accept-edits` |\n| \"Use autonomous sandbox\" | `--sandbox --permission-mode autonomous` |\n\nHonor the dimensions the user names. Otherwise the model stays `swe` and the permission mode stays `dangerous`.\n\n### Model Selection\n\nDefault `swe` (alias → `swe-2`). Switch per-dispatch with `--model <name>`; there is no headless reasoning-effort flag, so autonomy is set through `--permission-mode`. Curated families, alphabetical: DeepSeek (`deepseek-v4-1-flash-high`, `deepseek-v4-1-flash-max`, `deepseek-v4-flash-max`), Gemini (`gemini-3-8-flash-high`; the uid spells the family with dashes while the Cursor scope spells the same model with dots), GLM-5.2 (`glm-5-2` = **GLM-5.2 High**, free tier; `glm-5-2-1m` = High 1M; `glm-5-2-max` = Max; `glm-5-2-max-1m` = Max 1M; `glm-5-2-none` = No Thinking; `glm-5-2-none-1m` = No Thinking 1M), GLM-5.3 (`glm-5-3-flash-high`, `glm-5-3-flash-max`), GPT-5.6 Luna Max (`gpt-5-6-luna-max`, `gpt-5-6-luna-max-priority`), GPT-6 Luna Max (`gpt-6-luna-max`, `gpt-6-luna-max-priority`; a separate family from GPT-5.6), SWE-2 (`swe-2-max`, `swe-2-high`, `swe-2-medium`; free, 262K context), SWE-1.7 (`swe-1-7`, `swe-1-7-lightning`, `swe-1-7-medium`) — full roster and the permission-mode effort lever in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md).\n\n**Selection Strategy**: default `swe` for quick edits and cost-sensitive work; switch to `gpt-5-6-luna-max` for reasoning-heavy work (architecture, security, deep planning); use `glm-5-2` / `glm-5-2-max` for general generation; use `swe-2-max` for max-effort SWE work. Per-task rationale table: [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) §5.\n\n### Devin Subagent Delegation\n\nThe calling AI is the conductor; Devin's `run_subagent` tool spawns independent workers that share tools and codebase context but operate in their own conversation chain. Two built-in profiles (`subagent_explore` read-only, `subagent_general` full-access) plus custom `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md` profiles shape HOW Devin processes the subtask. Full roster and invocation patterns: [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md).\n\n| Task Type | Profile | Model |\n|-----------|---------|-------|\n| Read-only codebase exploration | `subagent_explore` | Default subagent model (SWE-1.6) |\n| General-purpose code changes | `subagent_general` | Same as parent agent |\n| Custom specialized worker | `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md` | Pinned in AGENT.md or default |\n\nSubagents run foreground (parent pauses) or background (parallel, auto-deny unapproved tools). The `run_subagent` tool takes a profile, not a model — to pin a model on a write-capable subagent, use a custom AGENT.md with a `model:` field.\n\n### Devin Skills, Rules, and Native Agent Profiles\n\nDevin discovers the skills and rules already in the repository, and this packet adds no adapter for either. A session loads the checkout's root `AGENTS.md`, cut at Devin's fixed 16,384-byte limit per rule file, because `.devin/config.json` turns the Claude import off. The live `devin skills list` and `devin rules list` output is recorded in [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md) §10.\n\n#### Agent Roster Parity\n\nAll 11 repo agents are dispatchable through `run_subagent`: `ai-council`, `code`, `context`, `debug`, `deep-research`, `deep-review`, `design`, `markdown`, `orchestrate`, `prompt-improver`, `review`. A live roster probe lists them alongside Devin's own `subagent_explore` and `subagent_general`.\n\nEach `.devin/agents/<name>/AGENT.md` is a **symlink** to the canonical `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, matching the discovery-mirror precedent already used for `.claude/hooks/` and `.codex/hooks/`. One source of truth, so a mirror can never drift from the agent it mirrors.\n\nThis works because Devin's failure with Claude-format agents is a *discovery-path* limitation, not a *format-parsing* one: the same file Devin ignores at `.claude/agents/<name>.md` registers correctly once reachable at Devin's own `.devin/agents/<name>/AGENT.md` path -- Claude's `tools:` frontmatter field is accepted as-is, so no per-agent translation to `allowed-tools:` is needed.\n\nInvoke by naming the profile explicitly:\n\n```bash\ncommand -v devin\ndevin --permission-mode bypass -p \\\n  \"Use the review subagent to review the current diff for correctness, security, and repository-convention consistency. Cite file paths and line numbers.\" \\\n  2>&1\n```\n\nThe experimental native profile format ([docs.devin.ai/cli/subagents](https://docs.devin.ai/cli/subagents)) and its YAML fields are in [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md) §5.\n\n#### Installed-Version Findings\n\nDevin `3000.2.17` does not import `.claude/agents/*.md` as its docs claim, which is why the `.devin/agents/<name>/AGENT.md` symlinks above exist, and it has no command-file system. The probes behind both findings are in [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md) §10.\n\n### Cloud Handoff\n\nDevin's unique `/handoff` command transfers the current session to a cloud Devin session with its own VM, shell, browser, and full repo access. Use for long-running tasks, complex refactors, CI-like validation, browser-dependent workflows, and parallel execution. Full mechanics and state transfer: [cloud-handoff.md](./references/cloud-handoff.md).\n\n### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas\n\nThe full flag glossary, permission modes, unique capabilities (`/handoff`, `run_subagent`, `devin mcp`, session resume/continue, `--sandbox`), essential command examples, and troubleshooting table are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md). Four gotchas that silently break a dispatch and must be honored at routing time:\n\n- **`devin -p` is non-interactive and exits after one turn** — it prints the response to stdout and exits. For multi-turn work, use `devin -c` (continue) or `devin -r <session-id>` (resume). Do not expect a REPL from `-p`.\n- **`--permission-mode` defaults to `auto` (read-only auto-approve)** — file-modification tasks silently prompt or no-op without elevated mode. Pass `--permission-mode dangerous` whenever the task requires edits, and note that `accept-edits` is only half a grant: it permits writes but refuses the reads and commands an implementer needs, so a dispatch under it can burn its whole budget and exit 0 having written nothing. The `--sandbox` flag selects `autonomous` mode and is the only mode available in sandbox sessions.\n- **`devin -p` rejects MCP tool calls under `auto`/`accept-edits`** (and `smart` may be unavailable). When a least-privilege MCP allowlist is preferable to blanket elevation, grant it in a machine-local config:\n```json\n// .devin/config.local.json\n{ \"permissions\": { \"allow\": [\"mcp__<server>__*\"] } }\n```\nThen `auto`/`accept-edits` auto-approve exactly those MCP tools; reserve `dangerous` for throwaway isolated runners.\n- **Always pass `--model` explicitly in scripts** — omitting it relies on the caller's `~/.config/devin/config.json` default, which may be a different model. Explicit means reproducible regardless of who runs it.\n- **Model ids carry no `-high` suffix, but the interactive picker shows one** — the TUI labels `glm-5-2` as \"GLM-5.2 High\", so an operator asking for \"GLM 5.2 high\" means the id `glm-5-2`. There is no `glm-5-2-high`. `devin models list` is the authority for every id and its display name; this document's roster is a convenience copy.\n- **A free-tier model still dispatches when the Pro quota reads 0%** — `glm-5-2` is billed as Free, and a dispatch succeeded with `Pro · 0% remaining` showing in the TUI. Quota exhaustion gates the paid families, so do not abandon a dispatch on the quota banner alone; probe with a trivial read-only call first.\n- **`devin --help` is NOT the authoritative `--permission-mode` enum** — it prints 4 values; the binary accepts 8. Canonical set with aliases: `normal` (`auto`), `accept-edits`, `smart`, `dangerous` (`yolo`, `bypass`), `autonomous` (requires `--sandbox`). Do not \"correct\" a mode value in this skill because help omits it — that conclusion is wrong and has been reached before. Probe instead: `devin --permission-mode <value> --prompt-file /nonexistent` (exit 2 = rejected, exit 1 = accepted). The enum also moves between releases, so re-probe after an upgrade rather than trusting either help or this line.\n- **Use `--` before every print-mode prompt** — `devin -p -- \"list all TODO comments\"` prevents the prompt from being parsed as CLI flags. The prompt must follow the separator, or load it with `--prompt-file`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. Verify Devin CLI is installed before first invocation (`command -v devin`).\n2. Delegate research and review lineages to `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` with executor kind `cli-devin`. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5. Never build a second adapter in this packet.\n3. Use `--permission-mode auto` for review/analysis/research; `--permission-mode dangerous` for code generation and file modification — `devin -p` itself defaults to `auto`, so omitting the flag causes a silent no-op on edit tasks. Prefer `dangerous` over `accept-edits` for any task that must read files or run its own verification; `accept-edits` refuses those calls and the dispatch fails silently.\n4. Validate Devin-generated code (XSS, injection, eval, syntax checks via `node --check`, `tsc --noEmit`, etc.) before applying.\n5. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) so rate-limit messages and errors surface.\n6. **Redirect devin stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch** — not only inside a `while read` loop, which is the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped. Pattern: `devin -p -- \"$PROMPT\" > \"$LOG\" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Without `</dev/null`, the backgrounded devin process inherits the loop's stdin and silently consumes the remaining lines. See `references/integration-patterns.md#background-execution` → \"Silent Stdin Consumption\".\n7. **Specify model + permission mode explicitly** — never rely on caller environment. Default: `--model swe --permission-mode dangerous`. Honor user overrides verbatim. Use `gpt-5-6-luna-max` for reasoning-heavy tasks (architecture, security, deep planning).\n8. Route to the appropriate subagent profile when the task matches a specialization (see Section 3 routing table); use `subagent_explore` for read-only research, `subagent_general` for code changes.\n9. **Pass the spec folder to the delegated agent** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating — the delegated agent cannot answer Gate 3 in non-interactive `-p` mode.\n10. **Prompt construction & model-craft (cli-* family precedence).** Compose every dispatch prompt via the 2-tier rule canonical in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`:\n    1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.\n    2. **Deep path (escalation).** Dispatch `@prompt-improver` via the Task tool (never load full `sk-prompt` inline) when any canonical **Tier 2** trigger applies — the trigger list lives in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` under \"Tier 2 — Deep path\"; do not re-enumerate it here.\n11. **Never inject user-level voice/personalization content into AI-orchestrated Devin delegations.** Devin CLI reads user-level rules from `~/.config/devin/` and project `.devin/` config. When an AI delegates via `devin -p`, the calling AI's own voice rules govern the response — do NOT read user config and paste into delegation prompts. Keep delegations focused on task/model/permission-mode/(spec-folder pre-approval). This skill supplies that guidance: which connector does what, the rules that keep edits in the user's file, and, in one reference file per app, how each API really behaves. Most of the app-specific rules in the references were tested against Google's Docs, Sheets and Slides APIs; the rest were seen through the connectors, and a few have not been checked yet.\n\n## Read the reference before you touch the file\n\n| Working on | Read first | Why it matters |\n|---|---|---|\n| A Google Doc | `references/docs.md` | Docs edits address UTF-16 positions that shift after every insert and go stale after every write. Tabs and pending suggestions change the positions too. |\n| A Google Sheet | `references/sheets.md` | Both write tools parse input like the Sheets UI, so text can silently become numbers or dates. Formatting needs numeric sheet IDs, 0-based ranges, and field masks without parentheses. |\n| A Google Slides deck | `references/slides.md` | Positions are in EMU, an element's real size is its size times its scale, and an unmasked read can exceed 150 KB for three slides. Slides never shrinks text to fit. |\n\nRead the reference for every app the task touches before the first edit. Embedding a Sheets chart in a deck means reading both. The references are short, and skipping one is how edits land in the wrong place.\n\n## 1. Check the connectors before you start\n\n| Connector | What it can do |\n|---|---|\n| Google Drive | Create files, upload and convert content, rename, read a file as text, export (PDF and other formats), search, trash |\n| Google Docs | Read a doc's full structure and edit it in place, directly or as suggestions |\n| Google Sheets | Read values and structure, write values and formulas, format, add tabs and charts |\n| Google Slides | Read a deck, add and edit slides, shapes, text, tables, and linked charts |\n\nDrive can create all three file types. It can't edit a file after that. Without the matching editor connector, every change means a new file and a new link, and the user loses the link they already have.\n\n1. Check which Google tools are available in this conversation. On surfaces where tools are deferred, search for and load the tools you need first, such as \"google sheets update\". Tool names differ by surface, so use the names your surface lists. If a search returns nothing, list all available tools before deciding the connector is missing, because the tool may exist under a different name.\n2. If the editor tools are missing, tell the user. Rules for every file\n\n- **A change goes in the same file.** \"Change\", \"update\", \"fix\", \"add\", and \"switch it to\" all mean the user wants the same file and link. Do not recreate the file to skip an edit.\n- **A missing editor connector is a choice for the user, not a workaround for you.** When the user asks for a change to an existing file and the editor connector is missing, your whole reply is a short question, not a deliverable. Building the next-best thing feels helpful, but the user's file is still untouched and now there are two artifacts, which is the exact failure this skill exists to prevent. Lead with the fix: name the connector and say that with it on, the edit lands in their existing file and the link stays the same. The Docs, Sheets, and Slides connectors can't open a trashed file.\n- **Read before you edit, and guard the write.** Send every Docs and Slides batch with `writeControl.requiredRevisionId` set to the `revisionId` from a read taken after your last write, including batches built on IDs or positions from your own earlier writes. The only exception is a batch made entirely of `replaceAllText` requests, even one limited to some tabs or slides. If the file changed since that read, whether from your own write or someone else's, Google rejects the whole batch instead of applying it at stale positions or IDs. Read again before each guarded batch, and don't reuse a revision ID from a write reply. On a rejection, read again and rebuild; never drop the guard. `read_doc` and `read_presentation` (the mask in `references/slides.md` includes it) return the ID. `read_slide_page` returns it only if its mask includes `revisionId`; `read_slide_page_thumbnail` and Drive `read_file_content` never do. For a saved read, the first line of `docs_index.py outline` or `slides_helper.py outline` shows it; if that line says `None`, read again with `read_doc` or `read_presentation`. `get_spreadsheet` returns a `revisionId` even with a field mask, but don't send it: send Sheets writes without `writeControl`, and read again right before a write that depends on positions.\n- **Put everything for one step in one batch.** Batch requests run in order and atomically: if one is invalid, none apply. One call per logical step is faster and leaves no half-finished state.\n- **Sheets field masks.** Write each path in full, with no parentheses: one path per item in `get_spreadsheet`'s `fields` list (`[\"spreadsheetId\", \"sheets.properties\"]`), and comma-separated in a batch update request's `fields` string (`\"userEnteredFormat.numberFormat,userEnteredFormat.textFormat.bold\"`).\n- **Verify the result.** Read the file again after each edit and check the result before you report it. A tool accepting the call does not mean the content is correct. Each reference has a Verify section.\n- **Rename with Drive `update_file`.** A rename keeps the same link.\n- **Link every file you name.** When you name a Google file you created, copied, found, or edited, make its title a link, inside the sentence that says what you did: \"I added the row to [Team roster](its link).\" Don't set the file apart after a colon or on a line of its own (\"I've created a file for you: Team roster\"). If a Drive result says the user can already see or open a file from the chat, leave that file's link out unless they ask. Always give the link when the user asks for it, wants to send it to someone, or says they can't see or open the file, even if a result said they could. Don't tell the user to use a card or preview unless a result said one is shown. After an edit, say that the link stays the same.\n\n## 3. Drive, for all three apps\n\n- **Find a file:** use Drive search when the user names a file without a link. Confirm the match with the user if more than one file fits. A page can be short even when more files match (5 files at page size 20) and can repeat the previous page's last file, so follow the next-page token until none comes back, and drop repeated ids.\n- **Create:** `create_file` with `contentMimeType` set to `application/vnd.google-apps.document`, `.spreadsheet`, or `.presentation` creates an empty file. Uploading content with a source type (HTML, CSV, .xlsx, .pptx) converts it into the matching Google type. Each reference says which route fits that app.\n- **Read as text:** `read_file_content` returns a compact text rendering: Markdown for a Doc. It is a few KB where the editor connector's full read can be over 100 KB, so use it to understand content, then use the editor read when you need positions. Point the script at that path; the scripts read the file as the app saved it. When a result comes back in context and is small (a few KB, such as a masked read or sheet metadata), write it to a file and run the script on it. Don't re-type a large result into a file: that doubles the cost and invites copying errors. Common failures across apps\n\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| \"No such tool available\" | The tool is deferred, or the name is different on this surface | Search for and load the tool. Use the exact name your surface lists. |\n| Permission denied on a file you created | The file is in the trash | Ask the user to restore it from Drive's trash. If \"this\" or \"here\" isn't clear from the chat, ask which file, heading, slide number or cell range they mean. *Reported.*\n- **Comments:** `read_doc` with `commentsIncluded: true` has returned each comment with its place in the text. WHEN TO USE\n\n### Activation Triggers\n\n- A document needs a frontmatter block and you do not know which fields its class carries.\n- A validator rejected a frontmatter block and the message names a field rather than a fix.\n- A `description` is over budget and needs trimming without losing its routing signal.\n- A `version` field needs deriving, inserting or reconciling against a changelog anchor.\n- Someone asks what `trigger_phrases`, `importance_tier` or `contextType` are for.\n- A document class is being added and needs a frontmatter rule of its own.\n\nKeyword triggers: `yaml frontmatter`, `frontmatter block`, `frontmatter template`, `frontmatter field`, `frontmatter fields`, `trigger_phrases`, `trigger phrases`, `importance_tier`, `contextType`, `description budget`, `4-part version`, `X.Y.Z.W`, `frontmatter versioning`, `frontmatter version`, `version field`, `frontmatter validation`, `missing frontmatter`, `frontmatter contract`, `yaml header`, `goes at the top of the file`, `version number at the top`, `importance tier`, `versioning pass`, `stopped showing up in suggestions`, `validator says my file is missing`, `description too long`, `edit count`, `field the validator wants`.\n\n### When NOT to Use\n\n- **The document itself needs writing.** Frontmatter is the block at the top. The mode that owns the document class owns its body.\n- **A validator needs changing.** The scripts live in the shared tier and are enforcement, not contract. Changing what they check starts here. Changing how they check it does not.\n- **The question is which skill to route to.** That is the hub router's job.\n- **A changelog entry needs writing.** The changelog mode owns that, including the version number that appears in its filename.\n\n---\n\n## 2. SMART ROUTING\n\n### Resource Domains\n\n- `assets/frontmatter-templates.md`. The field reference and the per-class templates. Eleven sections covering every document class, the description budget, validation rules and the common fixes.\n- `references/frontmatter-versioning.md`. The 4-part `X.Y.Z.W` standard: scope, format, the changelog-anchored derivation, the numstat gate, and the insertion rule.\n\n### Resource Loading Levels\n\n| Level | When to Load | Resources |\n|-------|--------------|-----------|\n| ALWAYS | Any frontmatter question | `assets/frontmatter-templates.md` |\n| CONDITIONAL | The question is about `version`, its derivation, or the corpus gate | `references/frontmatter-versioning.md` |\n\n### Smart Router Pseudocode\n\nThe canonical resilient router discovers resources at call time, guards and loads only\nwhat exists, scores the intents, and returns a disambiguation checklist rather than\nsilently loading nothing:\n\n```python\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nRESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / \"references\", SKILL_ROOT / \"assets\")\nDEFAULT_RESOURCE = \"assets/frontmatter-templates.md\"\n\nINTENT_MODEL = {\n    \"FIELDS\":     {\"weight\": 5, \"keywords\": [\"frontmatter block\", \"which fields\", \"trigger_phrases\", \"importance_tier\", \"contexttype\", \"add frontmatter\", \"missing frontmatter\"]},\n    \"BUDGET\":     {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"description budget\", \"description too long\", \"trim the description\", \"description length\"]},\n    \"VERSION\":    {\"weight\": 5, \"keywords\": [\"4-part version\", \"x.y.z.w\", \"version field\", \"frontmatter version\", \"changelog anchor\", \"edit count\"]},\n    \"VALIDATION\": {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"frontmatter invalid\", \"validator rejected\", \"malformed frontmatter\", \"frontmatter fix\"]},\n}\nRESOURCE_MAP = {\n    \"FIELDS\":     [\"assets/frontmatter-templates.md\"],\n    \"BUDGET\":     [\"assets/frontmatter-templates.md\"],\n    \"VERSION\":    [\"references/frontmatter-versioning.md\", \"assets/frontmatter-templates.md\"],\n    \"VALIDATION\": [\"assets/frontmatter-templates.md\", \"references/frontmatter-versioning.md\"],\n}\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [\n    \"Confirm the document class: skill manifest, readme, reference, asset, command, agent or spec doc\",\n    \"Confirm the operation: author a new block, fix a rejected one, or derive a version\",\n    \"Confirm whether the file is in scope for the version field at all\",\n]\n\ndef discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:\n    docs = []\n    for base in RESOURCE_BASES:\n        if base.exists():\n            docs.extend(path for path in base.rglob(\"*.md\") if path.is_file())\n    return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}\n\ndef _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:\n    resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()\n    resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)\n    if resolved.suffix.lower() != \".md\":\n        raise ValueError(f\"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}\")\n    return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()\n\ndef load_if_available(relative_path, inventory, loaded, seen) -> None:\n    guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)\n    if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:\n        load(guarded)\n        loaded.append(guarded)\n        seen.add(guarded)\n\ndef score_intents(request) -> dict:\n    text = request.text.lower()\n    scores = {intent: 0 for intent in INTENT_MODEL}\n    for intent, cfg in INTENT_MODEL.items():\n        for kw in cfg[\"keywords\"]:\n            if kw in text:\n                scores[intent] += cfg[\"weight\"]\n    return scores\n\ndef route_frontmatter_request(request):\n    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()\n    loaded, seen = [], set()\n\n    # The field reference loads on every path. Every frontmatter question resolves\n    # against a document class first, and that is the only place classes are defined.\n    load_if_available(DEFAULT_RESOURCE, inventory, loaded, seen)\n    scores = score_intents(request)\n\n    if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 4:                       # Tier 1: unclear scope\n        return {\n            \"load_level\": \"UNKNOWN_FALLBACK\",\n            \"needs_disambiguation\": True,\n            \"disambiguation_checklist\": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST,\n            \"resources\": loaded,\n        }\n\n    intent = max(scores, key=scores.get)                      # Tier 2: happy path\n    for resource in RESOURCE_MAP[intent]:\n        load_if_available(resource, inventory, loaded, seen)\n    return {\"intent\": intent, \"resources\": loaded}\n```\n\nUnknown intent returns the disambiguation checklist with the field reference already\nloaded, because \"which class is this document\" is the first question on every path.\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Author a block\n\n1. **Name the document class.** Skill manifest, readme, reference, asset, feature catalog, testing playbook, command, agent or spec doc. The class decides the field set, and guessing it is the usual source of a rejected block.\n2. **Copy the class template** from the field reference section 4. Do not compose one from memory. Several classes differ by a single field.\n3. **Fill `description` against the budget.** It shares a project-wide allowance, and an over-budget description is silently dropped from discovery rather than reported.\n4. **Derive `version` last.** It is inserted as the final key before the closing delimiter, which is field-relative and never a fixed line number.\n5. **Validate** with the shared-tier validator for the surface you are on.\n\n### Fix a rejected block\n\nRead what the validator named, then read the class row rather than the field row. Most\nrejections are a field that is required for one class and forbidden for another, so the\nfield in isolation looks correct. The common fixes are catalogued in section 6 of the\nfield reference: missing block, missing field, wrong field name, malformed delimiters.\n\n### Derive a version\n\nThe anchor is the higher of the skill's own frontmatter version and its highest changelog\nfilename version, compared as integer tuples. Major and minor are inherited from it,\npatch is reserved and seeded zero, and build is the file's real edit count.\n\nReal edit count is the rule that matters. It counts commits whose own added-plus-deleted\nline count for that file is above zero. A naive commit count over-counts, because a\nhistorical repository-wide move left files carrying zero-line \"edits\" and bulk sweeps\ntouch siblings without changing the file. Measured across the 1,214 in-scope documents of\n`sk-doc` and `system-spec-kit` on 2026-09-02, the ungated count is 1.06 to 1.09 times the\ngated one in aggregate and 2.25 times at the worst single file, so the gate changes the\nanswer often while the gap itself stays small.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. Resolve the document class before reading any field rule. The class decides the field set.\n2. Insert `version` as the last key before the closing delimiter, field-relative.\n3. Edit frontmatter line-wise. A YAML re-serializer reflows multi-line block sequences and corrupts `trigger_phrases`.\n4. Gate the edit count through per-file numstat. An ungated count is wrong by a large multiple, not a small one.\n5. Keep `description` inside its budget, and keep the routing tokens when trimming.\n6. Report a skipped file. A versioning pass that cannot resolve a file says so rather than synthesizing a block.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. Synthesize a frontmatter block for a file that has none during a versioning pass. Skip and report.\n2. Overwrite a human-set `version` that differs from the computed one without an explicit update flag. The one exception is a `SKILL.md`, which is the anchor of record.\n3. Add `version` to a class the standard puts out of scope. Commands, agents and a skill's own `INSTALL-GUIDE.md` are governed elsewhere.\n4. Left-pad or shift segments when normalizing a 3-part version. Append one zero, once.\n5. Change what a validator checks by editing the validator. The contract changes here first.\n6. Enumerate stacks or products in a `description` to fill it out. The budget is shared and every character costs another document its discovery.\n7. Declare hard rules as a frontmatter key. They live in a `hard-rules.json` sidecar beside the skill's `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects the dispatch preflight reads.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. A document class needs a field the contract does not define for it, which is a contract change rather than a document fix.\n2. A computed version conflicts with a human-set one and the correct answer is not obvious from the changelog.\n3. Two validators disagree about the same block, which means the contract is ambiguous rather than the document wrong.\n\n---\n\n## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\n- A block authored from a class template passes the validator for that surface on the first run.\n- A rejected block is fixed by reading one class row, not by trying fields until one is accepted.\n- A versioning pass over an already-versioned tree is a byte-level no-op.\n- A trimmed description keeps the tokens the advisor routes on.\n\n---\n\n## 6. REFERENCES\n\nRouted by `references/README.md`. The field reference in `assets/` loads on every path. The versioning standard is\nconditional on the question being about `version`.\n\n---\n\n## 7. INTEGRATION POINTS\n\n- **sk-doc parent hub.** This packet is registered in `../mode-registry.json` and `../hub-router.json`. The advisor scores the hub on `../graph-metadata.json`, so every keyword trigger above is also a stage-one entry there. A trigger present in one of the three and absent from another routes on one stage only.\n- **Shared-tier enforcement.** `../shared/scripts/quick_validate.py` reads the description budget from `../shared/assets/skill-contract.json`, `../shared/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs` implements the versioning standard, and `../shared/scripts/check-frontmatter-versions.sh` wraps its `gate` mode. This mode owns what they check, and never edits how.\n- **Value lists.** `assets/frontmatter-values.json` holds the `contextType` and `importance_tier` values and aliases. spec-kit's `shared/context-types.ts` and `FRONTMATTER_VALUES` rule, `../shared/scripts/validate_document.py` and the skill-advisor `check-skill-doc-frontmatter.mjs` read it by path, so moving or reshaping it breaks all four.\n- **Post-edit hook.** `.skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/` resolves the corpus gate by literal path on every qualifying edit. That path is why the scripts stay in the shared tier.\n- **Templates that cite this contract.** `sk-create-skill`'s manifest, reference and asset templates, the feature-catalog and playbook templates, and the `/create:skill` and `/create:agent` workflow assets all point at `assets/frontmatter-templates.md`. A rule changed here changes what they emit.\n- **Doctor budget audit.** `/doctor:skill-advisor skill-budget` and `.skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/audit_descriptions.py` measure the project against the budget this contract documents.\n\n---\n\n## 8. RELATED RESOURCES\n\n- `README.md`: what the mode owns, the silent-budget and numstat-gate concepts, troubleshooting and the verification table.\n- `references/README.md`: the reference router.
