SMART ROUTING\n\nThese triggers route a request into this command-authoring packet. Execution-mode suffixes are command syntax, not packet-selection triggers. When the surface is a slash command, stay in this packet and continue to the creation workflow below.\n\n### Router Resilience\n\nThis packet routes by command-authoring intent and the requested component surface. It does not use runtime keyed resource discovery through `references/<key>/` because its references are flat.\n\n- Load optional markdown resources only after resolving them under this packet and confirming they exist.\n- Treat `references/README.md` as the fallback route map when command intent or component surface is unclear.\n- Ask for the missing command purpose, invocation shape, or component type instead of silently loading no resources.\n- Do not add a full `references/<key>/` or `assets/<key>/` runtime-key router unless this packet gains real keyed resource subdirectories.\n\n### Resource Loading Sequence\n\nThe packet keeps its existing flat-resource routing while using the shared resilience call sequence:\n\n```python\ndef discover_markdown_resources():\n    return flat markdown resources under this packet's `references/` and `assets/` folders\n\ndef _guard_in_skill(relative_path):\n    # Keep packet-local markdown paths in scope; retain explicitly documented shared routes.\n    confirm the path is an allowed markdown resource for this packet\n\ndef load_if_available(relative_path, inventory, seen):\n    guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)\n    if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:\n        load(guarded)\n        seen.add(guarded)\n\ndef route_create_command_request(request):\n    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()\n    intents = score_intents(request)  # command-authoring intent and component surface\n    selected = select_intents(intents)\n    routing_key = get_routing_key(request, selected)\n    if not selected or the command purpose or component surface is unclear:\n        load_if_available(\"references/README.md\", inventory, seen)\n        return UNKNOWN_FALLBACK\n    return route by the existing command-authoring intent and component-surface rules\n```\n\n`UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` asks for the command purpose, invocation shape, or component type. The sequence discovers the current flat resources at routing time, guards and loads only available resources without duplicates, then applies the activation triggers and command-type rules already defined below.\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS: CREATION WORKFLOW\n\nFollow these steps in order.\n\n### Step 1: Decide Whether A Command Is Correct\n\nCreate a command only when the workflow is repeatable and has defined steps.\n\nUse a command when the workflow:\n\n- Automates a multi-step process.\n- Needs repeatable execution across sessions.\n- Needs `$ARGUMENTS` parsing or mode routing.\n- Needs user-controlled execution pace such as `:auto` or `:confirm`.\n- Needs confirmation gates for destructive or privileged actions.\n- Benefits from explicit tool restrictions.\n\nUse a skill instead when the content is reusable reference knowledge, domain guidance, standards, or patterns shared by multiple workflows. Do not create a command for one-off work.\n\n### Step 2: Resolve Invocation And Path\n\nDetermine the command invocation before writing:\n\n- Root command: `.skilled/commands/<command>.md` becomes `/<command>`.\n- Namespace command: `.skilled/commands/<namespace>/<action>.md` becomes `/<namespace>:<action>`.\n- Namespace and action names use lowercase hyphen-case.\n- Each command, namespace and action segment matches `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`. Reject underscores, empty segments and ambiguous normalization. The emitted `.md` stem must equal the validated action name.\n\nFor grouped related actions, prefer a namespace directory:\n\n```text\n.skilled/commands/\n└── <namespace>/\n    ├── <action1>.md\n    ├── <action2>.md\n    └── <action3>.md\n```\n\n### Step 3: Read Existing Files First\n\nBefore editing an existing command or owned asset, read it completely enough to understand current behavior. Preserve behavior unless the user explicitly asks to change it.\n\nFor new commands, inspect nearby commands in the same namespace when available so structure and vocabulary match the command family.\n\n### Step 4: Classify The Command Type\n\nChoose the smallest command type that fits:\n\n| Type | Use When | Typical Shape |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Simple | Single action, few arguments | One `.md` file, direct steps |\n| Workflow | Multi-step process with checkpoints | One `.md` file with overview, instructions, recovery |\n| Mode-based | Supports `:auto` / `:confirm` | Thin router plus owned assets when complex |\n| Router | Thin dispatcher: verify agent, resolve mode/args, hand off to owned assets | Router `.md` plus owned presentation `.txt` and optional workflow YAML or scripts |\n| Argument dispatch | Multiple action keywords or query forms | ASCII routing tree plus handlers |\n| Destructive | Deletes data or irreversible changes | Explicit confirmation, affected-state display, recovery guidance |\n| Namespace | Related commands grouped together | Directory under `.skilled/commands/` |\n\nIf the command combines patterns, parse mode first, then dispatch remaining arguments.\n\n### Step 5: Choose The Output Package Shape\n\nFor a simple or medium command, create or update:\n\n```text\n.skilled/commands/<command>.md\n```\n\nFor a namespace command, create or update:\n\n```text\n.skilled/commands/<namespace>/<action>.md\n```\n\nFor a split mode-based workflow command, create or update:\n\n```text\n.skilled/commands/<namespace>/<action>.md\n.skilled/commands/<namespace>/assets/<namespace>-<action>-presentation.txt\n.skilled/commands/<namespace>/assets/<namespace>-<action>-auto.yaml\n.skilled/commands/<namespace>/assets/<namespace>-<action>-confirm.yaml\n```\n\nUse `-auto.yaml` and `-confirm.yaml` only for workflow-backed families that route execution into workflow assets. Direct-router families dispatch directly to tools/scripts and do not need workflow YAML.\n\n**Asset stems are hyphen-joined, never underscore-joined.** The stem carries the namespace, the action and the kind: `create-readme-auto.yaml`, `speckit-plan-presentation.txt`, `deep-research-confirm.yaml`. A family whose action names already read unambiguously on their own drops the namespace and names assets `<action>-<kind>`: `memory` ships `save-presentation.txt`, `design` ships `extract-auto.yaml`. Follow the family you are extending. A new family takes the namespace prefix. The contract's `metadata.asset_naming` carries the same rule in machine-readable form, and `generate-command-routers.cjs --check` compares each router's tables against it.\n\nFor a compiled-stub router, the `.md` is a generated thin stub carrying the `render-command-contract` marker. Its section shape is rendered from a compiled source at invocation, not authored in the file. Do not hand-write section headings into a compiled stub, and keep its owned presentation/workflow assets alongside it:\n\n```text\n.skilled/commands/<namespace>/<action>.md            # compiled stub (render-command-contract marker)\n.skilled/commands/<namespace>/assets/<namespace>-<action>-presentation.txt\n```\n\n### Step 6: Author Frontmatter First\n\nEvery command starts with YAML frontmatter.\n\nRequired:\n\n```yaml\n---\ndescription: Action-oriented single-line description\n---\n```\n\nRecommended when applicable:\n\n```yaml\nargument-hint: \"<required> [optional] [--flag]\"\nallowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash\n```\n\nRules:\n\n- Keep `description` single-line, action-oriented, and concise.\n- Target descriptions at or under 110 characters.\n- Do not use YAML block scalars for `description`.\n- Use `argument-hint` whenever the command expects user input.\n- Use `<angle-brackets>` only for required arguments.\n- Use `[square-brackets]` for optional arguments.\n- Keep `argument-hint` at or under 140 characters: the hint **summarizes** the invocation shape while the router's **EXECUTION TARGETS** section **enumerates** the full flag surface. Over-budget hints warn (never block). Move the exhaustive flag list into the router body.\n- List every tool the command actually uses in `allowed-tools`.\n- Do not add broad tools just in case.\n- For MCP tools in `allowed-tools`, use fully qualified names such as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`.\n- Bare tool names such as `advisor_recommend` belong in prose only, not `allowed-tools`.\n\n### Step 7: Add Mandatory Input Gates\n\nIf `argument-hint` contains any required `<argument>`, add the mandatory gate after the H1 and its purpose line, before mode routing, asset loading and every workflow step.\n\nThe gate must:\n\n- Check whether `$ARGUMENTS` is empty, undefined, or whitespace-only.\n- Ignore mode suffixes when determining whether required content exists.\n- Stop immediately when required input is missing.\n- Ask a context-specific question with clear options or expected reply format.\n- Wait for the user response.\n- Use only `$ARGUMENTS` or the user's explicit answer as the input.\n- Forbid inference from context, screenshots, conversation history, or open files.\n\nFor multi-input commands, use a blocking phase pattern:\n\n- Phase 1: input collection.\n- Phase 2: prerequisite/context verification.\n- Phase status verification table.\n- Violation self-detection block.\n\nEvery workflow command with blocking phases must include violation self-detection: if a required phase was skipped, stop, state the violation, return to the phase, and complete it properly.\n\n### Step 8: Write The Command Body\n\nUse executable, instruction-oriented sections. Commands are workflows, not long reference manuals.\n\nCommon section order:\n\n1. Title and purpose.\n2. Contract.\n3. Workflow overview or argument routing.\n4. Instructions.\n5. Failure recovery and error handling when needed.\n6. Examples.\n7. Status output patterns or completion report.\n\nUse these conventions:\n\n- H1: plain command title, or a blocking semantic title for mandatory gates.\n- H2: `## N. SECTION-NAME`, using full integers only.\n- H3 steps: `### Step N: Description`.\n- Do not use decimal steps such as `1.5` or `2.5`.\n- Put sub-activities in bullets under a numbered step.\n- Use dividers between major sections when they improve scanability.\n- Return structured statuses such as `STATUS=OK`, `STATUS=FAIL ERROR=\"<message>\"`, or `STATUS=CANCELLED ACTION=cancelled`.\n- Keep the body **behavioral**: routing, gates, contracts, and executable steps only. Do NOT embed design rationale, prose-register or prompt-framework labels (e.g. \"written objective-first\", \"(COSTAR)\"), development notes (benchmark timings, spec/packet cross-references), maintainer chores (\"keep AGENTS/skills synchronized to this entrypoint\"), or defensive self-attestations (\"no workflow-asset gap exists\"). That context belongs in the decision-record, changelog, or presentation asset (never in the shipped command a user sees rendered).\n\nApproved common H2 section names include:\n\n- `PURPOSE`\n- `CONTRACT`\n- `WORKFLOW OVERVIEW`\n- `INSTRUCTIONS`\n- `ARGUMENT ROUTING`\n- `REFERENCE`\n- `EXAMPLES`\n- `RELATED COMMANDS`\n- `TOOL SIGNATURES`\n- `USER INPUT`\n\nApproved canonical H2 section names for router commands (see Step 11):\n\n- `ROUTER CONTRACT`\n- `OWNED ASSETS`\n- `MODE ROUTING`\n- `EXECUTION TARGETS`\n- `PRESENTATION BOUNDARY`\n- `WORKFLOW SUMMARY`\n\n### Step 9: Implement Argument Dispatch When Needed\n\nFor commands with multiple entry points, include an ASCII routing tree based on `$ARGUMENTS`.\n\nRoute by:\n\n- Empty arguments.\n- First-word action keywords, case-insensitive.\n- Natural-language query patterns.\n- Single ambiguous words.\n- Flags and options.\n\nThen define one handler section per action. Show example routing in a table so future maintainers can verify behavior quickly.\n\n**Argument-echo deprecation.** Do not end a command with a bare `User request: $ARGUMENTS` line. The command already receives `$ARGUMENTS`. Echoing it verbatim adds no routing behavior and duplicates the argument surface the router resolves. Resolve arguments in the router body. The validator warns on the raw-echo idiom.\n\n**Loader gating.** Frontmatter is the load gate: `allowed-tools` authorizes exactly the tools and MCP surfaces a command may use, and any agent the router dispatches must both be admitted by that gate and resolve to a real agent definition in the active runtime's agent directory. Do not dispatch a handle the frontmatter does not admit or that does not exist.\n\n### Step 10: Implement Mode Routing When Needed\n\nFor commands supporting `:auto` and `:confirm`, document mode detection:\n\n| Pattern | Mode | Behavior |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `/command:auto` | Autonomous | Execute without user approval gates |\n| `/command:confirm` | Interactive | Pause at each step for user approval |\n| `/command` | Prompt | Ask user to choose execution mode |\n\nAutonomous mode self-validates at checkpoints, makes informed decisions, and records significant decisions.\n\nInteractive mode pauses after each step for approval, presents options such as approve, review details, modify, skip, or abort, and records user decisions.\n\nIf the mode-based command is large or has visible dashboards/prompts/results, use the router/presentation split.\n\n**Mode completeness.** Every mode a command advertises must be fully realized, not merely reachable. For each mode in the argument hint (`:auto`, `:confirm`), the command must have both its workflow asset (the `-auto.yaml` / `-confirm.yaml`) and an EXECUTION TARGETS row that resolves the mode to that asset. A hint that lists `:auto` with no `-auto.yaml` or no `:auto` execution row is incomplete (a reader cannot route the advertised mode), so declare only the modes you have wired end to end.\n\n### Step 11: Author The Router As A First-Class Command Type\n\nA router is a first-class command type, not a loose refactor. Its `.md` is a thin dispatcher: verify the orchestrating agent, resolve mode and arguments, then hand off to owned assets (a presentation `.txt`, optional `-auto.yaml` / `-confirm.yaml`, or scripts). It carries no inline dashboards, prompts, or result templates.\n\n**Detection signature.** The validator treats a command as a router when any of:\n\n- a `render-command-contract` marker is present (the compiled-stub variant, which has no authored section requirements), or\n- a `Presentation Boundary` section is present, or\n- two or more of `{Router Contract, Owned Assets, Mode Routing, Execution Targets}` co-occur.\n\n**Minimal core vs recommended.** A router must include the blocking core only: `Owned Assets` and `Presentation Boundary`. The remaining canonical sections (`Router Contract`, `Mode Routing`, `Execution Targets`, `Workflow Summary`) are recommended and surface as non-blocking warnings when absent. Author the full shape for new routers. The minimal core lets incremental migrations land without failing.\n\n**Canonical vocabulary (numbered `## N.`, full integers).** Use exactly these H2 names, in this order, for a fully-shaped router:\n\n```text\n## 1. ROUTER CONTRACT\n## 2. OWNED ASSETS\n## 3. MODE ROUTING\n## 4. EXECUTION TARGETS\n## 5. PRESENTATION BOUNDARY\n## 6. WORKFLOW SUMMARY\n```\n\nDo not invent divergent synonyms (`Routing Assets`, `Workflow Routing`, `Execution Order`). The validator alias-normalizes those as a safety net, but the authored end state is the canonical names above.\n\n**Ownership boundary.** The router owns: the mandatory input gate or Phase 0, the owned-assets table, mode resolution, argument routing, execution-target selection, the presentation boundary, and a short workflow summary. The presentation asset owns: startup prompts and consolidated setup questions, auto fail-fast display text, dashboard and checkpoint layouts, success and failure result templates, and next-step suggestions. The router must not contain inline startup-question wording, dashboard templates, result templates, or next-step wording when a presentation asset exists. The split is behavior-preserving: move display content, do not change routing semantics.\n\n**Variants (one type, differing only by hand-off, not by required sections). Each maps to the contract's `topology` field:**\n\n- Workflow-YAML-backed (`topology: mode-pair`): routes execution into `-auto.yaml` / `-confirm.yaml` workflow assets. EXECUTION TARGETS is the `| Mode | Target |` table.\n- Direct-dispatch-script (`topology: direct-dispatch`): dispatches directly to tools or scripts, no workflow YAML. The mode table is not required.\n- Subaction route-manifest (`topology: subaction-route-manifest`): a direct-dispatch router that resolves sub-actions through an owned `_routes.yaml` manifest.\n- Compiled-stub: a generated stub carrying the `render-command-contract` marker whose contract is rendered at invocation. It is exempt from authored section requirements (retained variant, no command currently uses it).\n\nWhich family uses which topology is defined by the machine-readable command contract (`assets/command-contract.json`, validated by `assets/command-contract.schema.json`). Consult it rather than a hand-maintained family list. Use `assets/command-router-template.md` for the canonical numbered router skeleton, and `assets/command-presentation-template.md` for the full presentation asset skeleton.\n\n**Template self-sufficiency.** Each router variant must be authorable from its template alone: `command-router-template.md` plus the family's `command-contract.json` entry carry every section, vocabulary, and asset-path shape a new router needs. If a required shape is not derivable from the template and the contract, the template is incomplete: fix the template rather than copying a sibling command. This keeps the contract the single source and lets `generate-command-routers.cjs --check` detect drift instead of it hiding in hand-copied prose.\n\n### Step 12: Add Destructive-Action Safety\n\nFor commands that delete data or make irreversible changes, include:\n\n- Frontmatter that makes destructive intent visible when appropriate.\n- Confirmation by default.\n- `--confirm` only when explicitly designed to skip the prompt.\n- Affected-state display before execution.\n- Clear list of items that will be deleted or changed.\n- Execution logging.\n- Completion verification.\n- Recovery or rebuild guidance.\n- `STATUS=CANCELLED ACTION=cancelled` when the user aborts.\n\nDo not ship destructive commands without confirmation and recovery design.\n\n### Step 13: Validate Before Delivery\n\nBefore publishing or claiming the command is valid, verify:\n\n- `description` exists, is action-oriented, and is single-line.\n- `argument-hint` exists when arguments are expected.\n- `allowed-tools` lists only tools actually used.\n- Required `<arguments>` have a mandatory gate after the H1 and its purpose line, before any workflow step.\n- The gate forbids inference and waits for explicit input.\n- Section numbering uses full integers only.\n- H2 headers follow `## N. SECTION-NAME`.\n- Instructions are actionable.\n- Examples cover two or three likely invocations.\n- Status output uses a structured pattern.\n- Thin routers contain no presentation templates when a presentation asset exists.\n- Router commands carry the blocking core (`OWNED ASSETS` + `PRESENTATION BOUNDARY`) and use the canonical numbered vocabulary from Step 11. The remaining router sections are present or intentionally left as warnings.\n\nRun shared validators when available:\n\n```bash\npython3 ../shared/scripts/check_authored_name_kebab.py <command-file.md>\npython3 ../shared/scripts/validate_document.py <command-file.md> --type command\npython3 ../shared/scripts/extract_structure.py <command-file.md>\n```\n\nExit code `0` from the authored-name checker and `validate_document.py` is required before stating that the command document is structurally valid. If validation cannot be run, say that explicitly.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\nAlways:\n\n1. Read existing target files before editing.\n2. Use the smallest command type that fits the workflow.\n3. Put executable workflow steps in the command, not only in references.\n4. Use `argument-hint` for expected user input.\n5. Add a mandatory gate for required arguments.\n6. Keep `description` concise, single-line, and invocation-oriented.\n7. Keep `allowed-tools` least-privilege and accurate.\n8. Use fully qualified MCP tool IDs in `allowed-tools`.\n9. Keep presentation text in the presentation asset when using a split.\n10. Validate with shared create-quality-control scripts before delivery.\n11. Keep this nested packet free of `graph-metadata.json`.\n\nNever:\n\n1. Never create a command for one-off work that does not need reuse.\n2. Never skip mandatory gates for required arguments.\n3. Never infer missing required input from context or conversation history.\n4. Never use broad `allowed-tools` just in case.\n5. Never put dashboards, startup prompts, or result templates inside a thin router when a presentation asset exists.\n6. Never omit confirmation gates for destructive or irreversible actions.\n7. Never turn a command into long reference documentation.\n8. Never add advisor identity metadata inside this nested packet.\n9. Never claim structural validity without running validation or stating it was not run.\n\nEscalate if:\n\n1. The command name, namespace, or invocation contract is unclear.\n2. Required arguments cannot be safely defaulted.\n3. The command would perform destructive work without explicit confirmation requirements.\n4. Tool permissions are broader than the workflow appears to need.\n5. Router logic and presentation wording cannot be separated without changing behavior.\n6. The request belongs to a skill, agent, or one-off task instead of a slash command.\n\n---\n\n## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\nA command produced through this packet is complete when:\n\n- The correct component type was chosen: the workflow genuinely warrants a slash command rather than a skill, agent, or one-off task.\n- Frontmatter is well-formed: a single-line, action-oriented `description`, an `argument-hint` whenever user input is expected, and a least-privilege `allowed-tools` list using fully qualified MCP tool IDs.\n- Every required `<argument>` has a mandatory input gate after the H1 and its purpose line, before any workflow step, that forbids inference and waits for explicit input.\n- The body is executable and instruction-oriented, with full-integer `## N. SECTION-NAME` headings, actionable steps, two or three example invocations, and structured status output.\n- Router commands keep the blocking core (`OWNED ASSETS` plus `PRESENTATION BOUNDARY`), use the canonical numbered vocabulary, and hold no presentation templates when a presentation asset exists.\n- Shared validation was run: `validate_document.py` exits `0`, or its absence is stated explicitly rather than assumed.\n\n---\n\n## 6. OPERATIONAL MODES — IN-CLI (PRIMARY) + EXTERNAL-CLI (SECONDARY)\n\nThe council is **primarily an IN-CLI capability**. When invoked from inside an active runtime (OpenCode, Claude Code, OpenCode), the council deliberates using THAT runtime's own models and reasoning lenses as seats. No external dispatch is required for the common case — the active CLI's own model bench (e.g. Opus + Sonnet + Haiku on Claude Code; gpt-5.5 + gpt-5.5-pro + gpt-5.5-xhigh on OpenCode; direct DeepSeek and OpenAI provider models plus MiMo through LLM Gateway on OpenCode) supplies the seat diversity for a round.\n\n**External-CLI dispatch is a SECONDARY, optional mode** for cases where a different AI vantage adds value (e.g. DeepSeek/Kimi via cli-opencode from inside another runtime). The council resolver accepts `native`, `cli-opencode`, `cli-cursor`, `cli-devin`, `cli-pi`, and the `opencode` alias; it rejects `cli-codex` and `cli-claude-code`. External dispatch is invoked via the supported `cli-*` skill family, never directly from this skill.\n\n**Both modes obey the one-CLI-per-round invariant** (§5 ALWAYS rule 6):\n- In-CLI round: all seats use the current runtime's models.\n- External-CLI round: all seats use ONE supported external CLI (e.g. all `cli-opencode` seats with different reasoning levels, or all `cli-cursor`, `cli-devin`, `cli-pi`, or `cli-hermes` seats with different models).\n- Cross-CLI deliberation is staged as MULTIPLE rounds (one in-CLI + one external, or two different externals) — never folded into the same round.\n\nThe default and most common council run is a single in-CLI round. Add external rounds only when the active runtime cannot supply the required vantage or when explicit cross-AI validation is requested.\n\n---\n\n## 2. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Council Workflow Overview\n\nThe skill guides planning-only council runs from packet resolution through deliberation, persistence, and handoff. It keeps council artifacts under `ai-council/**` and leaves implementation to the caller or implementation agents.\n\n**Process Flow**:\n\n```text\nSTEP 1: Resolve And Prepare\n       |-- Resolve target spec folder before any persistence\n       |-- Load packet context and needed evidence\n       |-- Select 2-3 distinct seats\n       v\nSTEP 2: Deliberate And Converge\n       |-- Run independent proposals\n       |-- Run adversarial cross-seat critique\n       |-- Apply two-of-three convergence or emit non-converged status\n       v\nSTEP 3: Persist And Hand Off\n       |-- Produce required report sections\n       |-- Persist packet-local artifacts when caller has write context\n       |-- Verify completion and hand planning to implementation agents\n```\n\n### Six-Step Operational Flow\n\n1. Resolve the target spec folder before any council execution.\n2. Select two or three distinct council seats with different reasoning lenses and, when real executors are available, different AI vantage targets.\n3. Deliberate across independent proposals, adversarial critique, and convergence reconciliation.\n4. Return a council report with required sections from `references/structure/output-schema.md`.\n5. Persist packet-local artifacts with `scripts/persist-artifacts.cjs` when the caller owns a write-capable context.\n6. Verify completion with `scripts/advise-council-completion.cjs` and the append-only state rules in `references/structure/state-format.md`.\n\n### Resource Usage Pattern\n\n**Scripts**:\n\n```bash\nnode .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-ai-council/scripts/persist-artifacts.cjs <packet> --input-file <report>\nnode .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-ai-council/scripts/advise-council-completion.cjs <packet>\n```\n\n**References**: load `quick-reference.md` first, then intent-specific references through Section 3. Load `output-schema.md` before persistence or report validation.\n\n**Manual testing**: load `manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md` only for operator validation and release checks.\n\n---\n\n## 5. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. **ALWAYS keep council writes scoped to packet-local `ai-council/**` artifacts**\n   - This preserves the planning-only boundary and avoids mutating implementation or spec-doc surfaces.\n\n2. **ALWAYS preserve the planning-only boundary**\n   - Implementation remains with implementation agents, commands, or the top-level caller after handoff.\n\n3. **ALWAYS use distinct strategy lenses**\n   - Label simulated vantages honestly when an external AI system did not actually run.\n\n4. **ALWAYS append a `council_complete` event for completed persisted runs**\n   - State is append-only and completion must be auditable.\n\n5. **ALWAYS treat council graph support as a derived projection**\n   - The graph is rebuilt from packet-local `ai-council/**` artifacts and must not replace append-only council state.\n\n6. **ALWAYS run a single CLI per round (one-CLI-per-round invariant)**\n   - All seats within ONE deliberation round MUST be dispatched through the SAME supported CLI executor (for example all seats from `cli-opencode`, `cli-cursor`, `cli-devin`, `cli-pi`, or `cli-hermes`). Seat diversity WITHIN a round comes from different models/reasoning lenses on the same CLI (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --variant high` + `llmgateway/mimo-v2.6-pro`).\n   - Mixing executors within one round (e.g. one seat via OpenCode + one seat via OpenCode + one seat via Claude Code) is FORBIDDEN — it conflates orchestration boundaries, complicates rollback, and produces noisy convergence signals because per-CLI guarantees (sandbox, runtime, tool surface, output schema) differ.\n   - When MULTIPLE CLIs are appropriate for a deliberation, each additional CLI is a NEW DEDICATED ROUND with its own state event, its own seats, and its own convergence pass — never folded into the same round.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. **NEVER write application code, authored spec docs, or files outside `ai-council/**` as part of a council run**\n   - The council recommends; it does not implement.\n\n2. **NEVER add backward-compatible old-name shims without concrete active-consumer evidence**\n   - Rename support should follow real consumers, not speculation.\n\n3. **NEVER claim an external CLI or AI system participated unless it actually ran**\n   - Simulated perspectives must be explicitly labeled.\n\n4. **NEVER rewrite historical state rows**\n   - State evolution is additive-only; append new events instead.\n\n5. **NEVER mix CLI executors across seats within a single round**\n   - See ALWAYS rule 6. A round is defined by its CLI; a CLI change is a round boundary, not a seat boundary.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. **ESCALATE IF no packet/spec folder can be resolved for artifact persistence**\n   - Ask for the destination before dispatching seats or writing artifacts.\n\n2. **ESCALATE IF required report sections are missing and persistence would be lossy**\n   - Fix the report or fail before writes.\n\n3. **ESCALATE IF a caller still depends on the old `ai-council` runtime name and cannot be renamed**\n   - Compatibility requires explicit user direction.\n\n4. **ESCALATE IF a caller asks the council agent itself to mutate graph storage**\n   - Graph updates belong to caller-owned `runtime/` CLI reducers, not seat deliberation.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Run this check once per session, cache the result, and re-run it only if a dispatch's output text (not its exit code) shows an authentication error.\n\n```bash\n# One-shot pre-flight: capture account auth status for routing\nCURSOR_ABOUT=$(cursor-agent about 2>&1)\necho \"$CURSOR_ABOUT\" | grep -qi \"not logged in\" && CURSOR_AUTH_OK=0 || CURSOR_AUTH_OK=1\n```\n\n**Decision tree** (apply in order — first match wins):\n\n| State | CURSOR_AUTH_OK | Action |\n|-------|-----------------|--------|\n| Authenticated | 1 | Proceed with `cursor-agent -p \"<prompt>\" --output-format text --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |\n| Not logged in | 0 | **ASK user** to run `cursor-agent login` — surface the command, do NOT dispatch. Never substitute an unrelated CLI. |\n\n**User prompt template — not logged in:**\n\n```\nCursor CLI is not authenticated on this machine. cli-cursor uses Cursor account OAuth\n(or CURSOR_API_KEY for headless auth). Run `cursor-agent login`\n(browser flow), then confirm when login finishes — the skill will retry the original dispatch.\n```\n\n**Error-recovery contract.** If a dispatch's output text shows an auth error after pre-flight passed (session expired or revoked), invalidate the cache, re-run the pre-flight, and re-check before retrying. Never substitute a model the user didn't approve.\n\n### Default Invocation (Skill Default)\n\n**Default model + approval**: `composer-2.5` (Cursor's own native model) · `auto-review` approval (Smart Auto). `auto` (Cursor's own router) is NOT used — it can silently resolve to a model outside the enforced allowlist below, which defeats the point of enforcing one.\n\n> **Fan-out fallback:** a deep-loop lineage that pins no model runs **Composer**. The family is named here on purpose, without a version or an effort tier, so this line does not go stale when the family ships a point release; the runner resolves the current id. Model stays on `composer-2.5` unless the user explicitly names a different ALLOWED model.\n\n### Model Selection — Enforced Allowlist\n\n**cli-cursor dispatch is scoped to exactly 29 ids — never dispatch a model outside the allowlist (including `auto`), and never substitute the closest-sounding allowed model without telling the user.** Default `composer-2.5`; pick a Gemini 3.8 Flash High / GLM 5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / Grok (4.5, 4.6 or 4.7) tier only when the task or user explicitly names that family. Cursor has no `--reasoning-effort` flag and rejects parameterized model brackets outright — effort tiers must be selected through exact enumerated ids.\n\nThe enforced allowlist (29 ids) and the per-task rationale table live inline in [references/cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) §5 and [references/providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §2. Enforced at the runtime layer (`CURSOR_SUPPORTED_MODELS` in `executor-config.ts`, checked by `fanout-run.cjs` and `dispatch-model.cjs` before any command is constructed) and at this skill layer. If a task seems to need a model outside the allowlist, escalate to the user rather than fabricating a substitute or falling back to `auto`.\n\n### Cursor Agent Delegation\n\nThe calling AI is the conductor; Cursor's own skill system at `~/.cursor/skills-cursor/` (observed live: `automate`, `babysit`, `canvas`, `create-hook`, `create-rule`, `create-skill`, `create-subagent`, `loop`, `migrate-to-skills`, `sdk`, `shell`, `split-to-prs`, `statusline`, `update-cli-config`, `update-cursor-settings`) confirms Cursor supports subagents natively, but these are Cursor-editor-side conventions, not a `-p <profile>` flag like Codex's. Gotchas that silently break a dispatch and must be honored at routing time:\n\n- **The exit code is never an availability signal.** `cursor-agent -p` without auth exits `0` and prints an error to stdout/stderr instead. Every guard and pre-flight in this packet checks output text, never exit code.\n- **The canonical binary is `cursor-agent`, never the bare `agent` alias.** `agent` is a symlink to the same binary; using it in a process-ancestry match risks colliding with an unrelated `agent` command.\n- **Cursor shares its entire config surface with the Cursor editor** (`.cursor/`/`~/.cursor/`: `mcp.json`, `hooks.json`, `rules/`, `cli-config.json`). A dispatched `cursor-agent` silently inherits the operator's shared hooks/MCP/rules unless a workspace/config-isolation flag is used — see [shared-editor-config.md](./references/shared-editor-config.md).\n- **No `model[effort=...]` bracket support.** Unlike some sibling CLIs' parameterized model syntax, `cursor-agent --model 'cursor-grok-4.6[effort=high]'` is rejected outright (\"Cannot use this model\") — effort tiers must be selected via an exact enumerated id (`cursor-grok-4.6-high`), never a bracket.\n- **`--auto-review`/`--force` are the write-capable escalation, not `--sandbox`.** `--sandbox enabled|disabled` toggles the OS-level sandbox; the approval decision (whether unattended actions run without a human) is `--auto-review` (Smart Auto) or `--force`/`--yolo` (Run Everything) — omitting both leaves Cursor's own prompt-and-block default in place, which cannot proceed unattended.\n- **Project-scoped MCP servers show `not loaded (needs approval)`** until trusted. For a non-interactive dispatch that needs MCP tools, add `--approve-mcps` to the `cursor-agent -p` command (auto-approves configured MCP servers for that run); for a persistent operator grant use `cursor-agent mcp enable <server>` (a trust mutation the automation itself must never run).\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. Verify Cursor CLI is installed before first invocation (`command -v cursor-agent`).\n2. Delegate research and review lineages to `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` with executor kind `cli-cursor`. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5. Never build a second adapter in this packet.\n3. Use `--mode plan` or `--mode ask` for read-only exploration/analysis/research; use the default agent mode with `--auto-review` or `--force` for code generation/file modification.\n4. Validate Cursor-generated code (XSS, injection, eval, syntax checks via `node --check`, `tsc --noEmit`, etc.) before applying.\n5. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) so errors surface; check output TEXT for auth/availability failures, never the exit code (always `0`).\n6. **Redirect cursor-agent stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch** — not only inside a `while read` loop, which is the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped, mirroring the family-wide convention: `cursor-agent -p \"$PROMPT\" > \"$LOG\" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Live-verified: a real `cursor-agent -p ... </dev/null` dispatch completes normally with no hang.\n7. **Specify model and approval mode explicitly** — never rely on caller environment. Default: `--model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled`. Honor user overrides verbatim, but ONLY within the enforced allowlist (§3 Model Selection) — never `auto`, never a model outside the 29 allowed ids.\n8. Route to `--mode plan`/`--mode ask`/default agent per the task type (see Section 3 routing table).\n9. **Pass the spec folder to the delegated agent** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating — the delegated agent cannot answer Gate 3 in `--force`/non-interactive mode.\n10. **Prompt construction & model-craft (cli-* family precedence).** Compose every dispatch prompt via the 2-tier rule canonical in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`:\n   1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.\n   2. **Deep path (escalation).** Dispatch `@prompt-improver` via the Task tool (never load full `sk-prompt` inline) when any canonical **Tier 2** trigger applies — the trigger list lives in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` under \"Tier 2 — Deep path\"; do not re-enumerate it here.\n11. **Never inject user-level voice/personalization content into AI-orchestrated Cursor delegations.** Cursor CLI reads rules from `.cursor/rules`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and legacy `.cursorrules` automatically. When an AI delegates via `cursor-agent -p`, the calling AI's own voice rules govern the response — keep delegations focused on task/model/approval/(spec-folder pre-approval).\n12. **Code Standards Loading (surface-aware contract)** — When dispatching for code review or code generation, instruct the dispatched session to: (1) load `sk-code`; (2) let `sk-code` emit a surface tag matching the detected stack from markers and target files; (3) load the selected surface resources and run its verification commands; (4) add `code-review` only for formal findings-first review output. Fallback: if the surface cannot be determined confidently, ask for the runtime surface and verification command set. NEVER hardcode obsolete sibling code skills in dispatch prompts.\n13. **Design Standards Loading (measured-reference contract)** — When dispatching for design or UI work, instruct the dispatched session to: (1) load `sk-design-md-generator`; (2) extract a measured Style Reference DESIGN.md (named color tokens, type scale, components, Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind) from the live source before building UI; (3) build against those measured tokens and run the extraction's validate step to confirm hex/section fidelity. Fallback: if there is no live source to measure, ask for the reference URL or the exact tokens to build against. NEVER treat `mcp-figma` or `sk-design-md-generator` as a taste, visual-direction, or critique authority — the extraction measures real CSS, it does not judge design.\n14. **Pass the design reference manifest to the dispatched session** — when dispatching design or UI work, inline a `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST v1` block in the prompt (the child cannot resolve skill paths, so the manifest travels in the payload, not by reference): `styleReferenceExtracted` true, the live `source` that was measured, the measured design tokens / type scale / components the child must build against, `loadedFiles`, and `proofDemandBack`. If the manifest cannot be assembled — no Style Reference extracted, or no live source to measure — ASK before launching the child rather than starting a silent design dispatch. The child returns the demanded proof; the parent reconciles it on the return path.\n15. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped)** — Default: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family. Wait for the dispatched agent's work to return, verify outputs exist, then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started: capture its PID at launch (`cursor-agent -p ... & CURSOR_PID=$!`) and kill that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 \"$CURSOR_PID\" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P \"$CURSOR_PID\" 2>/dev/null`). **Never use a blanket `pkill -9 -f \"cursor-agent\"` pattern** — that matches and kills EVERY running `cursor-agent` process on the machine, including the operator's unrelated Cursor sessions (and the operator's own Cursor editor, since the CLI shares the binary family). Only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped. **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole multi-iteration session at start — iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt. **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently — but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.\n16. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env AND state the exemption in the prompt.** The variable makes the waiver true; it does not make it observable. The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable, so a child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question and writes nothing, at exit code zero. Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt. when sessions may be launched through the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`). A dispatched `cursor-agent -p` is an orchestrated sub-session, not a new top-level session, so it must SHARE the parent's worktree rather than allocate its own (distinct from Cursor's own native `-w` worktree flag, which this packet's default dispatch never passes). Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 cursor-agent -p ... </dev/null`. Harmless when the wrapper is not in use. See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → \"Worktree session isolation\".\n\n17. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).** Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}` — never a bare task. Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9 (`.cursor/agents/<name>.md`, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, `.skilled/agents/<name>.md`, etc. — never hardcode one runtime), and map each subtask to the RIGHT agent (`code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, docs→`markdown`), not one default. **Cursor has a native file-convention subagent surface:** `.cursor/agents/*.md` + `.claude/agents/*.md` mirror all 13 canonical agents — dispatch by naming the resolved subagent, which satisfies the rule. On a bare `cursor-agent -p` that names no subagent, **INLINE** the persona block into the payload using the same in-payload pattern as the `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 14) — the child cannot resolve agent paths by reference. A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant, silently dropping the agent's tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract. Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` \"Persona Injection\"; native precedent: `orchestrate.md` \"Agent Loading Protocol\". Rare exceptions (native surface used, focused summary for a small-context model, pure-mechanical command) are declared at the dispatch site.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. Pass `-w`/`--worktree` or dispatch `cursor-agent worker` from orchestrated fan-out without explicit user approval — these are opt-in escape hatches documented in `references/cursor-tools.md`, not this packet's default dispatch behavior.\n2. Trust Cursor output blindly for security-sensitive code, send sensitive data (API keys, passwords, credentials) in prompts, or hammer the CLI with rapid sequential calls.\n3. Use Cursor for tasks where context is already loaded — direct action by the calling AI is faster.\n4. Assume Cursor output is correct without verification — cross-reference codebase and project standards.\n5. Build or maintain a packet-local Cursor execution adapter; the deep-loop runtime is the execution authority.\n6. Treat a `0` exit code as proof of a successful, authenticated dispatch — always inspect output text.\n7. Dispatch a `--model` value outside the enforced 29-id allowlist (§3 Model Selection) — including `auto` — or silently substitute the closest-sounding allowed model instead of asking the user. Enforced at the runtime layer (`CURSOR_SUPPORTED_MODELS`/`isCursorModelAllowed` in `executor-config.ts`; a hard-rejecting check in `fanout-run.cjs`'s `buildCursorLineageCommand` and `dispatch-model.cjs`'s cli-cursor case) — this rule states the same constraint for any advisory/manual dispatch the runtime layer cannot see.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. Cursor CLI is not installed and user has not acknowledged (provide `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash`).\n2. `cursor-agent about` reports \"Not logged in\" and the user has not acknowledged running `cursor-agent login`.\n3. Generic \"design\", \"UI\", or \"screen\" phrasing is not a Mobbin signal; measured live-site extraction belongs to `sk-design-md-generator`, Refero references to `mcp-refero`, Figma work to `mcp-figma`, and browser work to `mcp-chrome-devtools`.\n\n```bash\n# Signal detection (pseudo)\necho \"$REQUEST\" | grep -qiE 'mobbin' && ROUTE=\"MCP_MOBBIN\"\necho \"$REQUEST\" | grep -qiE 'app design research|real app (screenshots|screens)|ux flow reference' && ROUTE=\"MCP_MOBBIN\"\n# generic design/UI phrasing WITHOUT these signals -> not this packet (measured extraction -> sk-design-md-generator)\n```\n\n### Phase Detection\n\n```text\nTASK CONTEXT\n    |\n    +- STEP 0: Verify wiring state (mobbin manual registered; presence expected — absence is a failure to escalate)\n    +- STEP 1: Score intent -> APPS | SCREENS | FLOWS | ELEMENTS | WIRING_AUTH | TROUBLESHOOT\n    +- Phase 1: Measured Style Reference also wanted? -> pair sk-design-md-generator (extracted design tokens); retrieval stays here\n    +- Phase 2: Discovery (list_tools / tool_info confirms the callable name)   [MANDATORY; needs a fresh Code Mode session]\n    +- Phase 3: Retrieval (search_screens with intent-shaped query; limit 5; platform ios|web)\n    +- Phase 4: Verify (evidence cited by mobbin_url; failed[] reported; unknowns preserved; no invented tools)\n```\n\n### Resource Domains\n\nThe router discovers markdown resources recursively from `references/` and `assets/`, then applies intent scoring. This skill uses a **flat intent router**: no keyed `references/<key>/` subdirectories. References are the primary loaded resources; the single asset is the registered manual's reference shape.\n\n```text\nreferences/tool-surface.md      # the one-tool surface, args, response shape, workflows, plan gating\nreferences/mcp-wiring.md        # registered manual, mcp-remote bridge, OAuth/DCR/PKCE, naming, discovery\nreferences/troubleshooting.md   # failure modes + fixes\nassets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md    # Registered manual's reference shape + post-registration checklist\n```\n\n### Resource Loading Levels\n\n| Level | When to Load | Resources |\n| ----- | ------------ | --------- |\n| CONDITIONAL | Research intent (apps/screens/flows/elements) | `references/tool-surface.md` (tool contract + workflow baseline) |\n| CONDITIONAL | Wiring / auth intent | `references/mcp-wiring.md`, `assets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md` |\n| CONDITIONAL | Setup / error intent | `references/troubleshooting.md` |\n| FALLBACK | Zero-score routes only | `references/tool-surface.md` suggested (never auto-loaded) |\n| PAIR (measured reference) | A measured Style Reference of extracted tokens is also wanted | `sk-design-md-generator`, the measured-extraction companion |\n\n### Smart Router Pseudocode\n\n> Resilience pattern: see [sk-doc smart-router template](../../sk-doc/sk-create-skill/assets/skill/skill-smart-router.md). Guard paths, discover at runtime, score intents, and fall back when unsure. Because this skill has no keyed resource subdirectories, intent selects from the flat resource inventory below.\n\n```python\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nRESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / \"references\", SKILL_ROOT / \"assets\")\nDEFAULT_RESOURCE = \"references/tool-surface.md\"\n# Fallback-only: DEFAULT_RESOURCE is a defer-time suggestion, never unioned\n# into a route's loaded set. Scored routes load exactly RESOURCE_MAP[intent];\n# zero-score routes load nothing and ask for disambiguation instead.\nDEFAULT_RESOURCE_SEMANTICS = \"fallback-only\"\nMIN_CONFIDENCE = 1\nAMBIGUITY_DELTA = 1\n\nINTENT_MODEL = {\n    \"APPS\":         {\"keywords\": [(\"app design research\", 4), (\"app research\", 4), (\"competitor\", 3), (\"app comparison\", 3), (\"banking apps\", 2), (\"category\", 2), (\"how do apps\", 2), (\"real apps\", 3)]},\n    \"SCREENS\":      {\"keywords\": [(\"screen\", 4), (\"screen examples\", 4), (\"ui pattern\", 3), (\"empty state\", 3), (\"first open\", 3), (\"onboarding screen\", 3), (\"component example\", 3), (\"screenshot\", 3), (\"paywall\", 2), (\"settings\", 2), (\"dashboard\", 2)]},\n    \"FLOWS\":        {\"keywords\": [(\"flow\", 4), (\"ux flow\", 4), (\"user flow\", 4), (\"journey\", 4), (\"start to finish\", 3), (\"multi-step\", 3), (\"progression\", 2), (\"forgot password\", 2), (\"checkout\", 2), (\"signup process\", 2)]},\n    \"ELEMENTS\":     {\"keywords\": [(\"element\", 4), (\"bottom sheet\", 3), (\"inline validation\", 3), (\"component behavior\", 3), (\"button state\", 2), (\"tab bar\", 2), (\"modal\", 2), (\"confirmation dialog\", 2)]},\n    \"WIRING_AUTH\":  {\"keywords\": [(\"wiring\", 4), (\"utcp\", 4), (\"oauth\", 4), (\"mcp-remote\", 4), (\"authenticate\", 4), (\"pkce\", 3), (\"manual\", 3), (\"register\", 3), (\"token\", 3), (\"plan\", 2), (\"install\", 2), (\"setup\", 2)]},\n    \"TROUBLESHOOT\": {\"keywords\": [(\"error\", 4), (\"failed\", 4), (\"401\", 4), (\"not working\", 4), (\"not resolving\", 4), (\"429\", 3), (\"rate limit\", 3), (\"timeout\", 3), (\"unauthorized\", 3), (\"denied\", 3)]},\n}\n\n# Mirror of INTENT_MODEL in the standard {weight, keywords} shape that\n# INTENT_SIGNALS parsers read (the tuple form above parses to zero intents\n# there). Runtime scoring uses INTENT_MODEL; this block changes no routing.\n# Per-intent weight = the MAX per-keyword weight in INTENT_MODEL for that intent\n# (all six resolve to 4). Keys and keywords MUST stay identical to INTENT_MODEL;\n# keep the two blocks in sync whenever either one is edited.\nINTENT_SIGNALS = {\n    \"APPS\":         {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"app design research\", \"app research\", \"competitor\", \"app comparison\", \"banking apps\", \"category\", \"how do apps\", \"real apps\"]},\n    \"SCREENS\":      {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"screen\", \"screen examples\", \"ui pattern\", \"empty state\", \"first open\", \"onboarding screen\", \"component example\", \"screenshot\", \"paywall\", \"settings\", \"dashboard\"]},\n    \"FLOWS\":        {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"flow\", \"ux flow\", \"user flow\", \"journey\", \"start to finish\", \"multi-step\", \"progression\", \"forgot password\", \"checkout\", \"signup process\"]},\n    \"ELEMENTS\":     {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"element\", \"bottom sheet\", \"inline validation\", \"component behavior\", \"button state\", \"tab bar\", \"modal\", \"confirmation dialog\"]},\n    \"WIRING_AUTH\":  {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"wiring\", \"utcp\", \"oauth\", \"mcp-remote\", \"authenticate\", \"pkce\", \"manual\", \"register\", \"token\", \"plan\", \"install\", \"setup\"]},\n    \"TROUBLESHOOT\": {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"error\", \"failed\", \"401\", \"not working\", \"not resolving\", \"429\", \"rate limit\", \"timeout\", \"unauthorized\", \"denied\"]},\n}\n\nRESOURCE_MAP = {\n    \"APPS\":         [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"SCREENS\":      [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"FLOWS\":        [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"ELEMENTS\":     [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"WIRING_AUTH\":  [\"references/mcp-wiring.md\", \"assets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md\"],\n    \"TROUBLESHOOT\": [\"references/troubleshooting.md\", \"references/mcp-wiring.md\"],\n}\n\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [\n    \"Confirm the research intent: apps, screens, flows, or elements (all are query intents over search_screens)\",\n    \"Confirm the mobbin manual's registration state (registered; absence is a failure symptom to escalate, never repair)\",\n    \"Confirm the account has a paid plan (Pro, Team, or Enterprise); Free has no MCP access\",\n    \"If a measured Style Reference of extracted design tokens is also wanted, pair sk-design-md-generator; this transport only retrieves Mobbin screenshot evidence\",\n]\n\ndef _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:\n    resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()\n    resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)               # raises if path escapes the skill\n    if resolved.suffix.lower() != \".md\":\n        raise ValueError(f\"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}\")\n    return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()\n\ndef discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:\n    docs = []\n    for base in RESOURCE_BASES:\n        if base.exists():\n            docs.extend(p for p in base.rglob(\"*.md\") if p.is_file())\n    return {d.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for d in docs}\n\ndef classify_intents(request: str):\n    text = (request or \"\").lower()\n    scores = {i: 0 for i in INTENT_MODEL}\n    for intent, cfg in INTENT_MODEL.items():\n        for kw, w in cfg[\"keywords\"]:\n            if kw in text:\n                scores[intent] += w\n    ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True)\n    primary, top = ranked[0]\n    if top == 0:\n        return (None, None, scores)   # unrouted -> no intent selected; fallback branch disambiguates\n    secondary, second = ranked[1]\n    if second > 0 and (top - second) <= AMBIGUITY_DELTA:\n        return (primary, secondary, scores)\n    return (primary, None, scores)\n\ndef route_mobbin_resources(request: str):\n    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()\n    primary, secondary, scores = classify_intents(request)\n    intents = [i for i in (primary, secondary) if i]\n    loaded, seen, notices = [], set(), []\n\n    def load_if_available(rel: str) -> bool:\n        guarded = _guard_in_skill(rel)\n        if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:\n            load(guarded); loaded.append(guarded); seen.add(guarded)\n            return True\n        if guarded not in inventory:\n            notices.append(f\"Resource not found in inventory: {guarded}\")\n        return False\n\n    if max(scores.values() or [0]) < MIN_CONFIDENCE:\n        # Fallback-only: nothing is loaded on a zero-score route; the default\n        # reference is offered as a suggestion beside the disambiguation ask.\n        return {\"intents\": intents, \"load_level\": \"UNKNOWN_FALLBACK\", \"needs_disambiguation\": True,\n                \"disambiguation_checklist\": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST,\n                \"suggested_fallback\": DEFAULT_RESOURCE, \"resources\": loaded, \"notices\": notices}\n    for intent in intents:\n        for rel in RESOURCE_MAP.get(intent, []):\n            load_if_available(rel)\n    return {\"intents\": intents, \"intent_scores\": scores, \"resources\": loaded, \"notices\": notices}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### First Step (Always): report the wiring state honestly\n\nThe `mobbin` manual **is registered** in this repo's `.utcp_config.json` (registered 2026-07-16 by an operator, never by this packet). `scripts/doctor.sh` reports the state read-only: manual presence is the healthy result, and **absence is now an ERROR** (a broken or reverted registration to escalate, never repair). Because manuals load at Code Mode startup and OAuth is still pending, discovery through a fresh Code Mode session is mandatory before any call:\n\n```typescript\n// Live-confirmed dotted discovery names (2026-07-16 fixture):\n//   mobbin.mobbin.search_screens · mobbin.mobbin.search_flows · mobbin.mobbin.search_sections\nconst all = await list_tools();\n// MANDATORY per session: confirm the exact callable + schema before relying on any name\nconst info = await tool_info({ tool_name: \"mobbin.mobbin_search_screens\" });\n```\n\nBoth the dotted discovery names and the callable form are **CONFIRMED by live discovery 2026-07-16** (`references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`; the convention-derived prediction held exactly). Discovery ran **pre-auth** — `tools/list` and schemas needed no OAuth; authenticated CALLS remain operator-gated. If a future discovery shows different names, missing tools, unexpected new tools, or a mutation-capable tool, **fail closed**: report the drift; a changed provider surface requires a reviewed packet update, not an improvised call.\n\n### The live three-tool surface (supersedes the one-tool baseline, 2026-07-16)\n\nThe research's **one publicly documented tool** baseline is superseded: live pre-auth discovery on 2026-07-16 listed **three** read-only search tools. All three passed the mutation-refusal check (no mutation-capable tool in the listing). Full fixture schemas and the completeness boundary: [`references/tool-surface.md`](references/tool-surface.md).\n\n| Tool | Posture | Required inputs (fixture schema) | Optional inputs (fixture schema) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `search_screens` | Read/search | `query`; `platform` `\"ios\"`\\|`\"web\"` | `mode` `\"deep\"`\\|`\"standard\"`\\|`\"fast\"` (deprecated alias); `limit`; `exclude_screen_ids[]`; `image_format` `\"webp\"`\\|`\"jpg\"` |\n| `search_flows` | Read/search | `query` (one journey); `platform` `\"ios\"`\\|`\"web\"` | `limit`; `page` (max 20); `image_format` |\n| `search_sections` | Read/search | `query` (one website section) | `limit`; `page`; `image_format` |\n\nDeclared `search_screens` output (fixture): `{ query, screens: [{ id, image_url, mobbin_url, app_name, platform }] }` — the research-documented `index`/`failed[]` fields do not appear in the declared schema; verify the actual response shape on the first authenticated call. **The `deep` conflict is RESOLVED**: search mode is a client-settable input on `search_screens` (`\"deep\"` = AI-powered relevance pipeline for nuanced queries; `\"standard\"` = low latency; `\"fast\"` = deprecated alias for standard). Never invent `search_apps`, `search_elements`, or any detail/image-download/mutation tool beyond the discovered inventory.\n\n### Calling through Code Mode\n\n> **Callable-name status.** The callable is confirmed by live discovery 2026-07-16 (`references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`): registry name `mobbin.mobbin.search_screens`, TS callable `mobbin.mobbin_search_screens(args)`. The call below quotes the confirmed form; the live RESPONSE behavior is still unexercised (authenticated calls pend operator OAuth), so re-confirm with `tool_info` per session.\n\n```typescript\ncall_tool_chain({\n  code: `\n    const result = await mobbin.mobbin_search_screens({\n      query: \"iOS banking app onboarding identity verification\",\n      platform: \"ios\",\n      limit: 5\n    });\n    return { success: true, data: result, errors: [], timestamp: new Date().toISOString() };\n  `\n});\n```\n\nMandatory discovery-first sequence: `list_tools()` or `search_tools({ task_description: \"Mobbin screen design research\", limit: 10 })` -> filter to the `mobbin` manual -> `tool_info()` on the exact dotted name -> only then `call_tool_chain({ code })`. Cite every selected reference by its `mobbin_url`.\n\n### Research workflows (query intents over the three live tools)\n\nApp, screen, and element research remain intent-specific query designs over `search_screens`; flow and website-section research now have dedicated live-discovered tools (2026-07-16):\n\n1. **App research** — name the app/company/category and comparison goal (\"banking apps onboarding identity verification\"); compare `app_name`, platform, structure, visible patterns.\n2. **Screen research** — name the concrete screen/state/job (\"iOS subscription cancellation confirmation\", \"web empty-state dashboard\"); start at 5 results; cite each `mobbin_url` used.\n3. **Flow research** — use `search_flows`: describe one user journey (\"onboarding with personalization steps\"); it returns ordered flow objects (`screens[].position`, `actions[]`, `screen_count`), superseding the old screens-only reconstruction guidance. Label anything beyond the returned ordering as inference.\n4. **Element research** — name component + context/state (\"bottom-sheet destructive confirmation\", \"inline validation on signup\"); analyze element behavior within returned screens; never fabricate an element-detail tool.\n5. **Website-section research** — use `search_sections`: describe one section (\"pricing page with plan comparison table\"); results carry `site_name` and section images.\n\nOfficial skill operating sequence: derive query terms from the user's actual words -> infer `ios` vs `web` from app context (unclear -> ask) -> announce a short search plan -> call `search_screens` in the same turn -> visually inspect returned references (observe content, structure, styling, interaction; compare repeats and meaningful differences; synthesize principles) -> answer from evidence tied to returned screens. The official skill's optional evidence-board writer is **excluded** from this transport (read-only boundary).\n\nContext discipline: start `limit: 5`; ask before widening materially (do not exceed ~15 just for variety); report `failed[]` entries and missing images as partial success, never silently discard; retain `mobbin_url` as provenance for every selected reference.\n\n### Auth, plans, and limits\n\n- **Auth**: browser OAuth only — protected-resource discovery, Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), authorization-code + PKCE S256, `openid` scope. **No static Mobbin API key exists for MCP**; the API-key Bearer model belongs to the separate Team/Enterprise REST API and must never be conflated with MCP. Client access is revocable from Mobbin Account Settings -> MCP. Adapter auth state persists under `~/.mcp-auth` (or `MCP_REMOTE_CONFIG_DIR`) and is **operator-owned**: never inspect, clear, or repair it. A live unauthenticated probe returned HTTP 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` pointer to the protected-resource metadata — a pre-authorization 401 is the **expected** challenge, not a missing-key error. End-to-end OAuth through the local Code Mode + `mcp-remote` bridge is **Inferred**, not verified: no operator has completed the flow in this repo's record.\n- **Plans**: MCP on **Pro, Team, and Enterprise; Free is excluded** (state \"MCP starts at Pro\"; the exact Free denial status/payload/UX is UNVERIFIED — do not guess failure semantics). No reviewed source documents different MCP tool sets per paid tier — do not invent per-tool tier gates. Per-plan usage caps within eligible tiers are undocumented; Finance+ is a separate paid add-on whose MCP result coverage is unestablished.\n- **Rate limit**: **60 requests per 60 seconds per user**; on 429 honor `Retry-After`, then exponential backoff with jitter.\n- **Transport**: the provider itself is a hosted remote server over **Streamable HTTP** at `https://api.mobbin.com/mcp` — there is no local package to install; the official repo is metadata-only. The local bridge is `npx -y mcp-remote` over stdio (HTTP-first, SSE fallback only on HTTP 404; experimental, externally versioned; Node 18+ and working `npx` are prerequisites).\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. **ALWAYS confirm callables with `tool_info` before first use.** The `mobbin.mobbin_search_screens` form is **CONFIRMED by live discovery 2026-07-16** (fixture `references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`; registry names are dotted `mobbin.mobbin.<tool>`). Fail closed on any drift from the live three-tool baseline (`search_screens`, `search_flows`, `search_sections`).\n2. **ALWAYS route measured-extraction needs to `sk-design-md-generator`, and pair it when a measured Style Reference is also wanted.** This packet is the transport; `sk-design-md-generator` is its cross-hub measured-extraction companion, turning a live site's real CSS into a Style Reference DESIGN.md of named design tokens. Transport output is Mobbin screenshot evidence and never a design-token set or Style Reference by itself.\n3. **ALWAYS report the manual's registration state honestly.** The `mobbin` manual is registered in `.utcp_config.json`: presence means verify read-only and proceed to discovery; absence is a **failure symptom** (a broken or reverted registration) to escalate to the operator, never to repair from this packet.\n4. **ALWAYS follow the documented input contract**: `query` from the user's actual words, `platform` `ios`|`web` (infer from context; unclear -> ask), `limit` starting at 5 and never exceeding ~15 without asking. Preserve unknown response fields untouched.\n5. **ALWAYS cite evidence by `mobbin_url`** and report `failed[]` entries and missing images as partial success, never silently discarding them.\n6. **ALWAYS treat this packet as read-only against this repo** (`mutatesWorkspace: false`). All reads happen against the external Mobbin service; Write, Edit, and Task are forbidden tools for this transport.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. **NEVER use Write, Edit, or Task through this packet.** It is a TRANSPORT: it retrieves external evidence and changes nothing in this workspace. Hand file changes to the owning workflow skill.\n2. **NEVER edit, re-draft, or re-add the `mobbin` manual in `.utcp_config.json`.** The registered entry is operator-owned. The reference shape in [`assets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md`](assets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md) exists for verification and escalation, not for this packet to apply or repair.\n3. **NEVER invent an API key or auth env var.** No `MOBBIN_API_KEY` or any MCP auth env var exists — the manual's `env` stays empty, and the auth env-var question is answered in the negative, not open. No `search_apps`, `search_elements`, detail, image-download, or mutation tools exist to call. The `deep` question is resolved — `mode: \"deep\" | \"standard\" | \"fast\"` is a real client input on `search_screens` — but do not assume undeclared parameters on any tool.\n6. **NEVER target `docs.mobbin.com/mcp`.** That is a separate Mintlify docs-search MCP; the design-reference server this packet owns is `api.mobbin.com/mcp` only. Likewise never conflate the OAuth MCP with the separate API-key REST API.\n7. **NEVER treat search rank or image appeal as a taste verdict**, never average strong references into a generic middle, and never copy or cache third-party reference content (screenshots, images) into this repo.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. **ESCALATE IF authentication is required** (HTTP 401 beyond the expected pre-auth challenge, OAuth prompt, browser round-trip). Completing browser OAuth is **operator-only**; surface the step and wait. Headless sessions need an operator-visible escalation, never a workaround.\n2. **ESCALATE IF discovery shows catalog drift**: a different callable name than the inferred form, unexpected new tools, or any mutation-capable tool. Refuse mutation-capable tools outright; a provider-surface change requires a reviewed packet update.\n3. **ESCALATE IF the account is Free-tier or rate-limited** (entitlement denial or 429 beyond the `Retry-After` + backoff protocol), reporting the provider's message verbatim without guessing denial semantics.\n4. **ESCALATE IF the manual is missing or malformed in `.utcp_config.json`.** The registered entry is operator-owned; a broken or reverted registration is reported with the reference shape in the asset, and any config change stops with the operator.\n5. **ESCALATE IF retrieved Mobbin evidence conflicts with a `sk-design-md-generator` Style Reference (its extracted design tokens)**, asking which source prevails before any conclusion is drawn.\n\n---\n\n## 5. INTEGRATION POINTS\n\n### Tool Usage Guidelines\n\n- **Code Mode** (`mcp__code_mode__call_tool_chain`) owns every Mobbin call, including discovery (`list_tools`, `search_tools`, `tool_info`) — the registered manual resolves in a fresh Code Mode session (manuals load at startup).\n- **Read/Grep/Glob** load references and check the manual's registration state in `.utcp_config.json` read-only.\n- **Bash** runs only the read-only `scripts/doctor.sh` diagnostics; this transport has no other shell role (Code Mode owns the stdio process launch, so the packet never runs `npx` itself).\n\n### Cross-Workflow Contracts\n\n- **`sk-design-md-generator`** is the cross-hub measured-extraction companion: it turns a live website's real CSS into a Style Reference DESIGN.md of named design tokens (type scale, components, Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind). The pairing: this packet retrieves cited Mobbin screens through Code Mode as reference evidence, and `sk-design-md-generator` produces the measured Style Reference of extracted tokens from an actual live site. The transport issues no design tokens or Style Reference of its own; pure setup/doctor or factual tool-surface reporting stays purely retrieval.\n- **`mcp-code-mode`** is the substrate: manuals, `{manual}.{manual}_{tool}` naming, discovery, and the error-envelope discipline all come from it. The current local config surface documents `stdio`/`sse` manual shapes, which is why the registered manual bridges through `mcp-remote` rather than declaring direct Streamable HTTP.\n- **`mcp-refero`** is the closest sibling: another remote-MCP-via-`mcp-remote`, read-only, OAuth-gated design-research transport in this hub. **`mcp-figma`** is the hub's original Figma transport. Neither overlaps this packet's Mobbin surface.\n\n### External Tools\n\n- **Mobbin MCP** (`https://api.mobbin.com/mcp`): the external, paid, hosted design-research service (manifest identity `com.mobbin/mobbin` v1.0.1; provider transport Streamable HTTP). Not vendored, not mirrored, no local package exists.\n- **mcp-remote** (npm, experimental, externally versioned): the stdio-to-HTTP bridge Code Mode launches via `npx` from the registered manual. WHEN TO USE\n\n### Activation Triggers\n\n**Use when** the user wants to:\n- Drive Figma Desktop from the terminal: create/render frames, components, icons, layouts, or images.\n- Work a design system in Figma: tokens, variables, collections, `var:name` binding, shadcn primitives.\n- Inspect or export from Figma: `extract` to DESIGN.md, export PNG/SVG/JSX/CSS/Tailwind/Storybook, screenshots, a11y audits.\n- Import a design system INTO Figma: from Tailwind config, CSS variables, `tokens.json`, or Storybook.\n- Set up or troubleshoot the figma-cli connection or daemon (safe plugin vs yolo patch, daemon health).\n- Optionally pull design context FROM Figma into the agent via a Figma MCP (Framelink `figma`) through Code Mode.\n\n**Keyword Triggers**: \"figma cli\", \"figma-ds-cli\", \"figma desktop\", \"render in figma\", \"figma tokens/variables\", \"extract DESIGN.md\", \"export from figma\", \"connect to figma\", \"figma daemon\", \"figma mcp\".\n\n### Use Cases\n\n**Connect / setup (CLI).** Verify the binary, choose a connect mode (safe plugin vs yolo patch), bring up the daemon, confirm health.\n\n**Inspect / export (CLI, read-only).** List/find nodes, get properties, `extract` a DESIGN.md, export assets/CSS/Tailwind/JSX/Storybook, run a11y audits, none of which change the Figma document.\n\n**Author / modify (CLI, gated).** Render JSX, create frames/components/icons, set properties, bind variables, generate variants. Every one changes the document and is gated, and every one is design-affecting: pair with `sk-design-md-generator` for a measured Style Reference (extracted design tokens) BEFORE authoring — this transport moves and renders, it does not produce the measured reference itself.\n\n**Design-system / tokens (CLI, gated).** Create token collections, import from Tailwind/CSS/tokens/Storybook, bind `var:name`. Ground token and variable choices in a measured reference: the `sk-design-md-generator` pairing (a measured Style Reference of extracted design tokens) applies before any token authoring, same as author/modify.\n\n**Optional MCP context pull (Code Mode).** When the agent needs Figma design context as model input (design data, variables, screenshots), call the Framelink `figma` manual through Code Mode.\n\n### When NOT to Use\n\n**Skip this skill when:**\n- The work is generic app coding with no Figma input: use `sk-code`.\n- The work is extracting a measured Style Reference (design tokens) from a live website's real CSS. That is `sk-design-md-generator`, and this skill is the Figma transport.\n- The task is browser debugging or visual preview of a built page. That is `mcp-chrome-devtools`.\n- Figma Desktop is not installed or not open. The CLI drives the live Desktop session and cannot work without it.\n\n---\n\n## 2. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### First Step (Always): verify the binary + Figma Desktop\n\n```bash\n# Canonical binary = figma-ds-cli. The npm package 'figma-cli' is an UNRELATED tool (unic/figma-cli).\nBIN=\"\"\ncommand -v figma-ds-cli >/dev/null && BIN=\"figma-ds-cli\"\n[ -z \"$BIN\" ] && command -v figma-cli >/dev/null && BIN=\"figma-cli\"   # only if installed from silships repo\n[ -z \"$BIN\" ] && { echo \"figma-ds-cli not found, see INSTALL-GUIDE.md (do NOT 'npm i -g figma-cli')\"; exit 1; }\n\"$BIN\" --version; \"$BIN\" --help | head -1\n```\n\nFigma Desktop must be **open with a file**, since figma-cli drives the live Desktop session (no Figma API key). Node `>=18`. macOS is the supported baseline.\n\n### Connect modes + daemon\n\n- **Safe (default): `figma-ds-cli connect --safe`** runs the FigCli plugin bridge, with **no patch**. Import `plugin/manifest.json` once, then keep `Plugins → Development → FigCli` open each session.\n- **Yolo (gated): `figma-ds-cli connect`** patches Figma Desktop `app.asar`, codesigns on macOS, restarts Figma with CDP on port `9222`. May need Full Disk Access/admin and **breaks when Figma updates**. **Never run without explicit consent + a stated rollback** (`figma-ds-cli unpatch`).\n- **Daemon**: local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:3456` (not a socket), auth via `X-Daemon-Token` at `~/.figma-ds-cli/.daemon-token`, PID `~/.figma-cli-daemon.pid`, idle ~60 min, not reboot-persistent. Verbs: `daemon status | diagnose | start | stop | restart | reconnect`. \"Unauthorized\" → `daemon diagnose` then `daemon restart` (never auto-delete the token).\n\n### Command classes (gating)\n\nThe full per-command taxonomy lives in [`references/tool-surface.md`](references/tool-surface.md). Summary:\n- **READ-ONLY** (safe default): `status`, `var list/find`, `get`, `find`, `inspect`, `node tree`, `extract`, `export*`, `export-jsx`, `export-storybook`, `analyze*`, `a11y*`, `files`, `--dry-run` variants. (Local exports still write files, so require an explicit output path, never silently overwrite.)\n- **MUTATING** (gate): all `create*`/`render*`/`tokens *`/`var create|bind|set|rename|visualize`, `bind *`, `set *`, layout verbs, `duplicate`, `use/theme`, `node to-component`, `slot/sizes/variants/combos`, `shadcn add`, `import`, `lint --fix`, `screenshot-url`, `recreate-url`, `gradient mesh`. App-level: `connect`, `unpatch`, `daemon start/stop/restart`, `config set`, `init-agent`. Design-affecting MUTATING verbs (authoring, tokens, binding, variants — everything except the app-level connection/daemon/config verbs) additionally carry the `sk-design-md-generator` pairing precondition: a measured Style Reference (extracted design tokens) grounds them first, then they are executed here.\n- **DESTRUCTIVE** (confirm + explicit target + rollback): `var delete-all`, `var delete-batch`, `delete/remove`, `node delete`, `undo`, `unwrap`, `fj delete`, `plugins uninstall`, `dev unlink`, `component prop delete`, `grid clear`, `annotate clear`.\n- **ARBITRARY** (treat as mutating, review first): `eval`, `raw`, `run`.\n\n### Optional Figma MCP via Code Mode (opt-in)\n\nThe skill works **fully with the CLI alone**. When the agent must pull design context FROM Figma, use the **Framelink `figma` manual already registered in Code Mode** (`figma-developer-mcp`, stdio, needs a Figma personal token). Calls go through `call_tool_chain()` with naming `figma.figma_<tool>`. The token must be in `.env` as `figma_FIGMA_API_KEY` (Code Mode prefixes the manual name). Always discover first with `search_tools()` / `tool_info()` before invoking. Full detail + the snippet: [`references/mcp-wiring.md`](references/mcp-wiring.md).\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. **ALWAYS verify the binary first.** Prefer `figma-ds-cli`, and only use `figma-cli` if it resolves to the silships tool (`--version`/`--help`), since the npm `figma-cli` package is unrelated.
