They organize capabilities by category, summarize current behavior in a root catalog, and link to per-feature files that carry implementation anchors, tests, and metadata.\n\nCore principle: use the root catalog for stable inventory and navigation, and use per-feature files for implementation truth and traceable source anchors.\n\nThis packet owns `/create:feature-catalog`, its `references/` set (indexed by `references/README.md`), and `assets/`. It consumes shared sk-doc validation and writing standards from `../shared/`.\n\n---\n\n## 1. WHEN TO USE\n\n### Activation Triggers\n\nUse this workflow when the request involves:\n\n- Creating a canonical feature inventory for a skill, system, MCP surface, CLI surface, or documentation family.\n- Splitting a large feature surface into a root catalog plus per-feature files.\n- Documenting shipped behavior with source-file anchors, validation anchors, and stable feature slugs.\n- Creating or updating `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md`.\n- Creating category folders such as `retrieval/` or `mutation/`.\n- Creating per-feature files such as `unified-context-retrieval.md` under category folders.\n- Linking manual testing playbooks, README summaries, or operator docs back to a stable feature reference.\n\nKeyword triggers: `feature catalog`, `feature inventory`, `catalog package`, `per-feature files`, `source anchors`, `root catalog`, `capability inventory`, `capabilities`, `/create:feature-catalog`.\n\n### When NOT to Use\n\nUse another `sk-doc` packet when:\n\n- The system has only a small feature list that fits accurately in a README.\n- The user needs manual validation scenarios. Use `create-manual-testing-playbook`.\n- The user needs a README. Use `create-readme`.\n- The user needs a changelog, benchmark package, command, agent, skill, or flowchart. Use `create-changelog`, `create-benchmark`, `create-command`, `create-agent`, `create-skill`, or `create-flowchart`.\n- The requested catalog would describe planned behavior rather than current shipped behavior.\n- The task is only document quality review of an existing catalog. Use `create-quality-control`.\n\n---\n\n## 2. SMART ROUTING\n\n### Creation Decision\n\nCreate a feature catalog when the system needs a canonical capability inventory.\n\nStrong signals:\n\n- The feature surface is too large for a trustworthy README-only summary.\n- Multiple docs need a stable source of truth for feature names and links.\n- Reviewers or operators need one place to see what the system does now.\n- Manual playbooks or specs need a canonical feature list to cross-reference.\n\nUse a lighter alternative when:\n\n- The system has only a handful of features.\n- A README already provides a complete and stable inventory.\n- The product is too volatile for a maintained catalog to stay accurate.\n\nDecision rule:\n\n```text\nNeed a stable, reviewable current-state inventory?\n  YES -> Create a feature catalog package\n  NO  -> Keep capability summary in README or install guide\n```\n\n### Family Boundary\n\nThis is a nested workflow packet under `sk-doc`. It carries its own `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `references/`, `assets/`, and `changelog/`, but it must not define a packet-local `graph-metadata.json`; advisor identity lives at the `sk-doc` hub root.\n\n### Router Resilience\n\nThis packet routes by whether the target needs a stable, reviewable current-state feature inventory. It does not use runtime keyed resource discovery through `references/<key>/` because its references are flat.\n\n- Load optional markdown resources only after resolving them under this packet and confirming they exist.\n- Treat `references/README.md` as the fallback route map when catalog necessity or target feature scope is unclear.\n- Ask for the missing target system, feature scope, or inventory requirements instead of silently loading no resources.\n- Do not add a full `references/<key>/` or `assets/<key>/` runtime-key router unless this packet gains real keyed resource subdirectories.\n\n### Smart Router Pseudocode\n\nFor this flat-reference packet, the canonical resilient router discovers resources at call\ntime, guards and loads only what exists, scores the root-catalog vs per-feature-file intent,\nand returns a disambiguation checklist rather than silently loading nothing:\n\n```python\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nRESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / \"references\", SKILL_ROOT / \"assets\")\nDEFAULT_RESOURCE = \"references/README.md\"\n\n# Two routing targets; keywords come from this packet's activation triggers.\nINTENT_MODEL = {\n    \"root_catalog\": {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"root catalog\", \"feature catalog\", \"capability inventory\", \"catalog package\"]},\n    \"per_feature_file\": {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"per-feature files\", \"source anchors\", \"feature inventory\", \"/create:feature-catalog\"]},\n}\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [\n    \"Confirm the target system, skill, or surface the catalog should cover\",\n    \"Confirm whether the request needs the root catalog, per-feature files, or the full package\",\n    \"Confirm where implementation source anchors and validation/test anchors live for the claimed features\",\n]\n\ndef discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:\n    docs = []\n    for base in RESOURCE_BASES:\n        if base.exists():\n            docs.extend(path for path in base.rglob(\"*.md\") if path.is_file())\n    return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}\n\ndef _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:\n    resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()\n    resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)\n    if resolved.suffix.lower() != \".md\":\n        raise ValueError(f\"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}\")\n    return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()\n\ndef load_if_available(relative_path, inventory, loaded, seen) -> None:\n    guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)\n    if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:\n        load(guarded)\n        loaded.append(guarded)\n        seen.add(guarded)\n\ndef score_intents(request) -> dict:\n    text = request.text.lower()\n    scores = {intent: 0 for intent in INTENT_MODEL}\n    for intent, cfg in INTENT_MODEL.items():\n        for kw in cfg[\"keywords\"]:\n            if kw in text:\n                scores[intent] += cfg[\"weight\"]\n    return scores\n\ndef route_feature_catalog_request(request):\n    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()\n    loaded, seen = [], set()\n    scores = score_intents(request)\n\n    if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 4:                      # Tier 1: low confidence\n        load_if_available(DEFAULT_RESOURCE, inventory, loaded, seen)\n        return {\n            \"load_level\": \"UNKNOWN_FALLBACK\",\n            \"needs_disambiguation\": True,\n            \"disambiguation_checklist\": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST,\n            \"resources\": loaded,\n        }\n\n    intent = max(scores, key=scores.get)                      # Tier 2: happy path\n    # Flat resource topology: no references/<key>/ subdirectories. The intent selects the\n    # root-catalog or per-feature template already documented below, not a keyed subtree.\n    for path in sorted(inventory):\n        load_if_available(path, inventory, loaded, seen)\n    return {\"intent\": intent, \"resources\": loaded}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. PACKAGE CONTRACT\n\n### Canonical Shape\n\n```text\nfeature-catalog/\n├── feature-catalog.md\n├── category-name/\n│   ├── feature-name.md\n│   └── another-feature-name.md\n└── another-category/\n    └── feature-name.md\n```\n\nInvariants:\n\n- Root file is always `feature-catalog.md` in lowercase.\n- Category directories use descriptive kebab-case names such as `category-name` (no numeric prefix).\n- Per-feature files use kebab-case names such as `feature-name.md` without numeric prefixes.\n- One root entry maps to exactly one per-feature file.\n- Slugs should remain stable after publication.\n- Display order is owned by the root catalog index (`feature-catalog.md`), not the folder name.\n- Per-feature snippet order is defined by the root catalog listing order; filenames do not encode order.\n\n### Required Resources\n\nUse these packet resources while authoring:\n\n- `assets/feature-catalog-template.md` for the root catalog scaffold.\n- `assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` for each per-feature file.\n- `../shared/references/quick-reference.md` and `../shared/references/validation.md` before delivery.\n- `../sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md` when checking frontmatter version fields.\n- `references/README.md` to route the reference overflow — [`examples.md`](references/examples.md) (worked live-catalog walkthrough) and [`common-pitfalls.md`](references/common-pitfalls.md) (deep-dive pitfalls, template-versus-reference split) — only for depth beyond this inline workflow.\n\nThe source assets keep the filenames `feature-catalog-template.md` and `feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` until their separate source-file migration. Those filenames are authoring inputs, not emitted package names.\n\n---\n\n## 4. HOW IT WORKS: CREATION WORKFLOW\n\nFollow this workflow in order.\n\n1. Read the target system docs, source files, command surfaces, MCP tool lists, tests, and existing README material before drafting the catalog.\n2. Decide whether a catalog is warranted; use a README summary instead when the feature surface is small, complete, stable, or too volatile for a maintained catalog.\n3. Decide the category taxonomy before writing prose.\n4. Stabilize category names, feature names, and feature slugs before polishing descriptions.\n5. Create `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md` from `assets/feature-catalog-template.md`.\n6. Create one category folder per root section using a descriptive kebab-case slug such as `category-name`; the root catalog listing defines display order.\n7. Create one per-feature file for each root entry using `assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md`.\n8. Write concise root summaries and link each feature to its per-feature file.\n9. Fill each per-feature `## 2. HOW IT WORKS` section with current behavior.\n10. Use plain prose for short `HOW IT WORKS` sections and H3 subheadings for sections longer than three paragraphs.\n11. Fill implementation source tables and validation or test anchor tables for every feature claim.\n12. Fill `## 4. SOURCE METADATA`, including group, canonical file path, and related references.\n13. Validate the root catalog and each per-feature leaf file with shared validation (see §7).\n14. Manually verify feature-file links, root-entry parity, source anchors, and current-state wording.\n\nAuthoring order matters:\n\n- Stabilize names and slugs before polishing prose.\n- Finish root taxonomy before expanding file-level detail.\n- Use implementation and test anchors to justify every feature summary.\n\n---\n\n## 5. ROOT CATALOG REQUIREMENTS\n\nThe root catalog is the top-level inventory and navigation layer.\n\nIt owns:\n\n- Frontmatter with title, description, trigger phrases, last updated date, and four-part version.\n- A short H1 intro describing the current feature surface.\n- `## 1. OVERVIEW`.\n- Numbered H2 capability sections by category.\n- H3 feature entries with concise descriptions.\n- Current-reality summaries.\n- Explicit links to per-feature files.\n\nRoot summaries should answer:\n\n- What this feature does.\n- What its current reality is.\n- Where to find source-file and test detail.\n\nPackage highlights for root catalogs:\n\n- Use frontmatter, including `trigger_phrases`.\n- Include a short H1 intro.\n- Do not include a Table of Contents.\n- Do not use `<!-- ANCHOR -->` navigation comments.\n- Start numbered H2 sections with `## 1. OVERVIEW`.\n\nDo not overload the root catalog with:\n\n- Exhaustive source-file tables.\n- Full scenario matrices.\n- Speculative future-state design.\n- Long implementation explanations.\n- Roadmap detail.\n\nThat information belongs in per-feature files, playbooks, or specs.\n\n---\n\n## 6. PER-FEATURE FILE REQUIREMENTS\n\nEach per-feature file is the detailed reference entry for one catalog item.\n\nRequired structure:\n\n1. `## 1. OVERVIEW`\n2. `## 2. HOW IT WORKS`\n3. `## 3. SOURCE FILES`\n4. `## 4. SOURCE METADATA`\n\nEach per-feature file must include:\n\n- Frontmatter with stable `title`, one-line `description`, `trigger_phrases`, and a four-part `version`.\n- At least three trigger phrases matching the H3 heading in the root catalog.\n- An H1 matching the feature, with a tool or command name in parentheses when relevant.\n- A concise overview of the feature.\n- A behavior-focused `HOW IT WORKS` section.\n- Implementation source tables with `File | Layer | Role` columns.\n- Validation or test anchors with `File | Type | Role` columns.\n- Metadata including group, canonical file path, and related references.\n\n`HOW IT WORKS` subheading rule:\n\n- Use plain prose when the section is three paragraphs or fewer.\n- Add H3 subheadings when the section exceeds three paragraphs.\n- Preferred H3 examples include `### Core Behavior`, `### Quality Gates`, `### Configuration`, `### Edge Cases`, and `### Async & Safety`.\n- Describe behavior from the caller or operator perspective, not the implementation perspective.\n\nContent rule:\n\n- Describe behavior that exists now.\n- If a rollout or compatibility layer is documented, label it explicitly.\n- Avoid roadmap or speculative wording unless the feature itself is a documented compatibility or feature-flag surface.\n\n---\n\n## 7. PLAYBOOK AND VALIDATION BOUNDARY\n\nFeature catalogs and manual testing playbooks serve different purposes.\n\n| Document | Primary Question |\n|---|---|\n| Feature catalog | What does the system do today? |\n| Manual testing playbook | How do we validate that behavior manually? |\n\nCross-reference rule:\n\n- Playbooks should link back to the matching catalog entry when one exists.\n- Catalogs should stay focused on current behavior, not test execution detail.\n- Manual execution scenario matrices belong in playbooks, not catalogs.\n\nValidation workflow — run from the repo root so the validator resolves the `feature_catalog` doc type on per-feature leaves (leaf detection accepts the canonical `feature-catalog/<category>/` path during the bounded compatibility window):\n\n```bash\n# New-content naming guard. The staging root must contain only the newly authored\n# canonical feature-catalog package, never an ancestor with shipped legacy roots.\npython3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/check_no_hyphenated_catalog_content.py <new-content-staging-root>\n\n# Root catalog (detected as the readme doc type)\npython3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py <target-skill>/feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md\npython3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/extract_structure.py <target-skill>/feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md\n\n# Each per-feature leaf (detected as the feature_catalog doc type; validates the Validation And Tests table taxonomy)\npython3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py <target-skill>/feature-catalog/<category-name>/feature-name.md\n```\n\nThe staging scope is mandatory until shipped underscore roots are migrated. Do not run this guard against `.skilled/skills` or another ancestor containing legacy `feature_catalog/` or `manual_testing_playbook/` trees.\n\nThe validator machine-checks the root-catalog structure and each leaf's Validation And Tests table, but not cross-file link targets or source-anchor accuracy. Manually verify:\n\n- Every root entry links to an existing per-feature file.\n- Every per-feature file is represented in the root catalog.\n- Source-file tables reference real, stable paths.\n- Validation or test tables reference real, stable paths.\n- Catalog claims describe shipped behavior, not speculative roadmap.\n- Cross-file links resolve.\n- Runtime docs avoid mutable spec or phase packet history.\n\n### Package Validator Enforcement\n\n`scripts/validate_catalog_package.py` is the package-level enforcement surface. Discovery is presence-based: every canonical `feature-catalog/` directory below `.skilled/skills/` is a package, keyed by its path relative to that root. The measured starting corpus is 26 packages and 804 leaves. The validator carries explicit runtime-data exclusion rulings for any root that could gain a same-named directory without a skill contract.\n\nThe validator compares root filenames and root-link targets case-insensitively. This preserves the `mcp-click-up` package's uppercase `FEATURE-CATALOG.md` without counting the root itself as an orphan.\n\nThe initial enforcement ladder is staged. Promoted packages fail closed immediately. The explicit WARN tier is `system-spec-kit`, `mcp-tooling/mcp-refero`, `mcp-tooling/mcp-click-up`, and `system-deep-loop/deep-research`, the four packages carrying the measured 104-orphan backlog. Repair children remove a package from the map when it is repaired; a clean package reports a promoted PASS. Use `--report-only` for advisory output; `--strict` remains an alias for the default.\n\nThe enforced roster is:\n\n- root/leaf bijection and discovery coverage;\n- SOURCE FILES path existence and Validation And Tests taxonomy;\n- sk-doc workflow-mode parity;\n- phantom root-row detection and repo-relative prose-path checking;\n- root-H3-to-leaf-title parity and normalized description parity;\n- packet-history metadata rejection;\n- dark-vs-shipped labeling; and\n- volatile measurement-snapshot rejection.\n\nCatalog prose may describe structural rosters derived from links or source tables, but it must not freeze measured counts or dated snapshots. The validator reports those snapshots so the catalog stays current-state evidence rather than stale census data.\n\nValidator boundary:\n\n- `validate_document.py` checks root-catalog structure and, for per-feature leaves reached by a repo-root path, the Validation And Tests table taxonomy.\n- Cross-file link resolution is enforced in CI by `check-markdown-links.cjs`.\n- Per-feature link correctness and source-anchor accuracy still require manual review.\n\n---\n\n## 8. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. Use `assets/feature-catalog-template.md` for the root catalog scaffold.\n2. Use `assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` for per-feature files.\n3. Preserve the canonical root path `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md`.\n4. Name category folders with a descriptive kebab-case slug such as `category-name`; let the root catalog index own display order.\n5. Keep per-feature filenames stable after publication.\n6. Keep per-feature filenames free of numeric prefixes.\n7. Include source-file and validation anchors for every feature claim.\n8. Describe current shipped behavior from the caller or operator perspective.\n9. Keep the root catalog inventory-first and navigation-focused.\n10. Put implementation truth in per-feature files.\n11. Run shared validation on the root catalog and per-feature leaves before delivery.\n12. Manually verify cross-file links, source anchors, and root-entry to feature-file parity.\n13. Consume global standards and validators from `../shared/` instead of duplicating them here.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. Never add a packet-local `graph-metadata.json`.\n2. Never use a feature catalog as a roadmap unless future-state material is explicitly labeled.\n3. Never split one feature across multiple files without a clear category boundary.\n4. Never leave root entries without matching per-feature files.\n5. Never leave per-feature files unlinked from the root catalog.\n6. Never cite mutable packet numbers where current source paths, commands, or feature names should be used.\n7. Never use numeric prefixes on per-feature filenames.\n8. Never add numeric prefixes to category folder names; the root catalog index owns display order.\n9. Never use underscores in category folder or per-feature filename path segments.\n10. Never put manual execution scenario matrices in the catalog.\n11. Never omit source anchors for feature claims.\n12. Never leave long `HOW IT WORKS` sections as unbroken walls of prose.\n13. Never omit `trigger_phrases` from per-feature frontmatter.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. The category taxonomy is unclear after reading the target system.\n2. Source anchors cannot be found for a claimed feature.\n3. The requested catalog mixes shipped behavior with planned behavior.\n4. Existing docs conflict about feature names or current reality.\n5. Validation fails in `../shared/scripts/validate_document.py` and the safe fix is not obvious.\n6. Published category or feature slugs would need to change without a deliberate rename migration.\n\n---\n\n## 9. COMMON MISTAKES\n\n| Mistake | Why It Breaks | Correct Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| Treating the catalog like a roadmap | Readers cannot trust current-state claims | Keep speculative material out or label it explicitly |\n| Unstable renaming of category or feature slugs | Breaks links from playbooks and other docs | Keep published slugs stable unless there is a deliberate rename migration |\n| Missing source anchors | Catalog claims become hard to audit | Add implementation and validation file references in the per-feature file |\n| Writing execution-heavy scenario detail in the catalog | Blurs the boundary with playbooks | Keep execution matrices in playbooks, not the catalog |\n| Playbook cross-references drifting from catalog names | Inventory and validation no longer match | Update catalog and playbook links together when a feature name changes |\n| Wall of prose in `HOW IT WORKS` | Long unbroken sections lose scannability and navigation anchors | Add H3 subheadings whenever the section exceeds three paragraphs |\n| Missing `trigger_phrases` in frontmatter | Feature is invisible to doc-trigger routing | Add at least three trigger phrases matching the H3 heading in the root catalog |\n\n---\n\n## 10. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\nThe catalog package is complete when:\n\n- The root catalog exists at `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md` and was built from the packet template.\n- Category folders use descriptive kebab-case slugs with no numeric prefixes, and display order is owned by the root catalog index.\n- Every root entry links to exactly one per-feature file, and every per-feature file is represented in the root catalog.\n- Each per-feature file carries frontmatter with a stable title, description, at least three `trigger_phrases`, and a four-part version, plus source-file and validation or test anchors for every feature claim.\n- Prose describes current shipped behavior from the caller or operator perspective, with any rollout or compatibility layer labeled explicitly.\n- Shared validation ran clean on the root catalog and each per-feature leaf, and cross-file links, source anchors, and root-entry-to-feature-file parity were verified by hand.\n\n---\n\n## 11. REFERENCES\n\nThe primary contract is this `SKILL.md`. Load the resources below only for overflow depth, worked examples, or schema checks beyond the inline workflow.\n\n- `references/README.md` - route map for the packet reference set.\n- `references/examples.md` - annotated walkthrough of a shipped feature-catalog package.\n- `references/common-pitfalls.md` - deep-dive pitfalls with before/after fixes and the template-versus-reference split.\n- `assets/feature-catalog-template.md` - root catalog scaffold.\n- `assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` - per-feature file scaffold.\n- `../shared/references/quick-reference.md` - condensed commands and file locations.\n- `../shared/references/validation.md` - shared validation and quality-scoring workflow.\n- `../sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md` - four-part version field rules.\n"

SURFACE STANDARDS (the non-negotiables)\n\nThese are measured facts about how this plugin proves correctness. A workflow bundling this surface\nMUST honor them:\n\n- **Never invent a `.db-*` class.** `src/views/screenshot-fixtures.test.ts` walks every class named by a\n  fixture and fails any that appears in neither `styles.css` nor `src/`. A capture of an invented class\n  photographs unstyled markup while looking like a successful screenshot.\n- **A capture succeeding is not proof.** `npm run screenshots:verify` only checks that a capture's\n  sources have not changed since it was taken; it does not check what the PNG shows. A capture can\n  succeed and still photograph an empty box. Look at the changed PNG.\n- **Captures are fixture markup, not the real renderers.** `tools/screenshots/` renders hand-written\n  fixture markup against the shipped `styles.css` in headless Chrome via `playwright-core`; the real\n  renderers need a live Obsidian `App`, vault, and metadata cache that the harness does not construct.\n  Markup drift shows up as a stale screenshot, not a capture error. `theme.css` and `runtime-vars.css`\n  stand in for what Obsidian supplies at runtime — a surface that looks wrong in a capture may be a gap\n  in those stand-ins rather than a plugin defect.\n- **Phone captures need the `is-phone` body class.** Obsidian marks phone layouts with it, and a large\n  part of the responsive CSS keys off it; without the class a narrow viewport is only a cramped desktop.\n- **The verification gate is real and partly red.** `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and\n  `npx vitest run` (386 passing across 49 files) must stay clean, and `npm run screenshots:verify` must\n  stay at its current entry count (180) or grow with new scenarios. `npm run lint` carries a **known\n  baseline of 115 problems** (100 errors, 15 warnings) — record it, never imply it is clean, and never\n  claim a change reduced it without rerunning the count.\n- **`styles.css` is the one stylesheet.** There are no component-scoped styles anywhere in this plugin;\n  every `.db-*` rule lives in that single file, 18,931 lines, 1,196 distinct classes measured, of which\n  769 are referenced by no fixture.\n- **Six recorded P0/P1 items and roughly 145 unphotographed surfaces are evidence, not a backlog this\n  surface clears.** They are named in `specs/public/HANDOVER.md` in the plugin repository; a bundled\n  workflow honors them as known state, never silently \"fixes\" them as a side effect of an unrelated\n  change.\n- **Never put a spec path, requirement id, task id, or checklist id in a code comment.** Record the\n  durable reason a thing is the way it is instead (`AGENTS.md`, plugin repository root).\n\n---\n\n## 3b. SOURCE TREE CONVENTIONS (the shipped grammar)\n\nThis section states the plugin's real, measured tree first, then the target conventions a later phase\nadopts — each labeled honestly, because most of them are not shipped yet.\n\n### The real, shipped tree (current state)\n\n- **`src/data/`** (128 `.ts` files) holds models, query, formulas, and filters — for example\n  `DataSource.ts`, `RowPipeline.ts`, `ColumnTypes.ts`, `ComputedEvaluator.ts`, `Aggregate.ts`.\n- **`src/views/`** (91 `.ts` files) holds renderers — the `*Renderer.ts` family covers every view type:\n  `TableRenderer.ts`, `BoardRenderer.ts`, `GalleryRenderer.ts`, `ListRenderer.ts`, `CalendarRenderer.ts`,\n  `CalendarTimelineRenderer.ts`, and `ChartRenderer.ts`.\n- **`src/views/modals/`** (17 `.ts` files) holds every modal dialog — `AddDatabaseModal.ts`,\n  `FormulaModal.ts`, `CreatePropertyModal.ts`, `DeleteDatabaseModal.ts`, `StatusOptionsModal.ts`, and\n  twelve more. No scanner enforces either\n  form yet.\n- **No folder carries a `README.md` or `CODE.md`.** Zero exist across the tree today.\n- **No file opens with a `MODULE:` banner or a numbered box-drawing section.** Zero of 249 source files\n  carry one; four contain some box-drawing rule for other reasons. `styles.css` itself opens with a\n  Chinese-language CSS-property cheat sheet (312 CJK comment lines measured) and 65 `===` banners — a\n  pre-existing convention, not the target grammar below.\n\n### The target conventions (not yet adopted — say so plainly)\n\n- **Kebab-case filenames** across `src/` and `tools/`, replacing the PascalCase-dominant tree above. A\n  manifest-driven rename executes this in a later phase; this packet documents the target, not a\n  completed migration.\n- **A `MODULE:` banner plus numbered, upper-case box-drawing sections** at the top of every source file,\n  applied here once a later phase lands it, not present in the shipped tree today.\n- **Paired `README.md`/`CODE.md` folder documents** at the three-or-more-direct-source-files (or any\n  child source folder) threshold. Measured\n  against the current tree, these folders owe both documents: `src`, `src/data`, `src/views`,\n  `src/views/modals`, `tools`, `tools/screenshots`, `tools/screenshots/scenarios`. The two `__tests__`\n  folders owe nothing, because the next rule removes them.\n- **A top-level `tests/` tree** holding every test, fixture and helper, flat while file names stay\n  unique and grouped by area only when a group holds several files, with no\n  double-underscore folder names. This is the universal rule in\n  [code-style-guide.md](../shared/references/universal/code-style-guide.md) §3 \"Folders and tests\".\n  Moving the 49 co-located test files and both `__tests__` folders is a migration in the plugin repo,\n  not yet done.\n- **Numbered box-drawing section grammar in `styles.css`**, replacing or supplementing the existing\n  CJK cheat-sheet preamble, over all 18,931 lines — an operator decision on whether the file stays one\n  section-annotated file or is split, since a split changes the load order the tests and the capture\n  harness depend on.\n\n---\n\n## 4. scores, \"resources\": loaded}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Workspace Choice Enforcement\n\n**MANDATORY**: The AI must NEVER autonomously choose between a git worktree and the current branch, and must NEVER create a branch directly with `git branch`, `git checkout` plus `-b`, or `git switch` plus `-c`.\n\nWhen a git workspace trigger fires, the AI MUST ask the user to explicitly choose:\n\n| Option                        | Description                              | Best For                        |\n| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |\n| **A) Create a git worktree**  | Isolated workspace in separate directory | Parallel work, complex features |\n| **B) Work on current branch** | No new worktree created                  | Trivial changes, exploration    |\n\n**AI Behavior**: ASK before proceeding, WAIT for explicit selection (A/B), NEVER assume, RESPECT choice for the session unless the user requests a change. Create any needed branch only through `git worktree add -b ...`.\n\n### Launch-Wrapper Worktrees vs the In-Session Ask-First Rule\n\nThe ask-first rule above governs **in-session** decisions: once running, an AI must not autonomously create a worktree. `.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`, a **launch wrapper** the operator opts into at the shell, is different: it runs *before* the AI starts, placing each top-level session in its own worktree + branch + isolated MCP databases (orchestrated children with `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1`, or already inside a linked worktree, exec in place), acting pre-session at operator opt-in, so it doesn't violate the ask-first rule.\n\n**Deliberate per-session deps override.** The wrapper **symlinks** the shared `node_modules`/`dist` into each worktree and gives each its own MCP DBs (via `SPEC_KIT_DB_DIR` / `SPECKIT_IPC_SOCKET_DIR`), rather than paying an install per session. Strict-validate and metadata regeneration run on `main` only.\n\n> **Known gap.** Those links are wholesale, so a wrapper session does not yet satisfy the ALWAYS #8 invariant: it reads the main checkout's first-party code however much it edits its own, and a generator run inside one exits 0 without writing. That is the real reason the line above sends strict-validate and metadata regeneration to `main`. Treat it as a constraint to work within, not a property of worktrees. The deep-loop lane provisioner performs the same sharing correctly, by splitting the link and recreating each self-link relative to the lane.\n\n### Continuous Integration: the always-current live branch\n\nWorktree isolation keeps concurrent, multi-runtime sessions safe but hides each session's work from the operator's IDE. The **continuous-integration workflow** fixes this: each launch-wrapper session **autosyncs** every commit to one shared **live branch** (whatever branch the primary checkout is on), fast-forward-followed by the IDE. The operator sees what's active seconds behind each commit. The wrapper exports `SPECKIT_LIVE_BRANCH` + `SPECKIT_AUTOSYNC`. The `post-commit` hook publishes via `git-sync.sh` (fetch → fast-forward-or-rebase-abort → non-force push), commit-granularity only. Full model: [continuous-integration.md](references/continuous-integration.md).\n\n### Remote Push Permission Enforcement\n\n**MANDATORY**: The AI must NEVER push a branch to `origin` outside the remote allowlist without a fresh, explicit go-ahead for THAT push. A prior approval doesn't carry forward to the next push.\n\nThe remote allowlist is `main`, `skilled/v*` release branches, plus anything in [remote-branch-allowlist.txt](scripts/remote-branch-allowlist.txt). Everything else needs an ask before every push to origin.\n\n\"Explicit go-ahead\" is either an in-turn instruction that already names the push (e.g. \"push this branch\": do NOT ask again), or a direct question the AI asks that the operator answers yes to.\n\nOnce granted, set `SPECKIT_ALLOW_REMOTE_PUSH=1` for that one `git push` only, never the session. The [pre-push hook](../../scripts/git-hooks/pre-push) backstops this, blocking any push to a non-allowlisted branch unless that env var is set. An unasked push fails instead of landing silently. Full contract: [remote-branch-policy.md](references/remote-branch-policy.md).\n\n**Continuous-integration exception**: the launch-wrapper's autosync publish (ALWAYS #16) targets only `$SPECKIT_LIVE_BRANCH` (chosen before the session started) and is exempt because `git-sync.sh` never blocks mid-hook (see [continuous-integration.md](references/continuous-integration.md)). Autosync to any OTHER branch still asks.\n\n### Preflight Advisory: the rules reach you at command time\n\nThe rules in `hard-rules.json` beside this file are executed, not just documentation: a preflight\nadvisory hook evaluates every visible `git` command against those rules and live repository state,\nfiring only on the specific risky state, never a bare verb match, and prints the matching rule\nas typed. It advises and never blocks. Enforcement stays with the pre-commit, commit-msg, and\npre-push hooks.\n\nSeven AI runtimes share it: Claude/Codex/Devin use `PreToolUse`, Cursor uses a Shell proxy,\nOpenCode uses its plugin, Pi uses its extension and Hermes uses the `repo-guards` plugin. Full\ndocs: [scripts/hooks/README.md](scripts/hooks/README.md) (registration, delivery,\nfail-open), [scripts/lib/README.md](scripts/lib/README.md) (rule engine, tests), and\n[manual-testing-playbook/](manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md) (operator scenario).\n\nSuppression: `SKGIT_ADVISORY=0` (global), `SKGIT_ADVISORY_SKIP=<rule-id>` (one rule), or a\n`SKGIT_ADVISORY_SKIP=commit`-style prefix (a family).\n\n### Repository Settings: /doctor:git\n\nA repository adapts sk-git through git config and `.sk-git/`, never by editing this skill.\n`/doctor:git` (`.skilled/commands/doctor/git.md`) changes and checks those settings:\n\n- `hooks` switches an optional pre-commit or pre-push gate on or off.\n- `standards` copies the commit, PR and branch rule templates into `.sk-git/` and edits them.\n- `setup` runs eleven read-only checks and names one repair per failure.\n\nWhen asked whether sk-git is set up or why a rule is not enforced, run `/doctor:git setup` before reading config by hand.\n\n### Git Development Lifecycle Map\n\nGit development flows through 3 phases:\n\n| Phase | Goal | Prevents | Output | See |\n|-------|------|----------|--------|-----|\n| **1. Workspace Setup** | Isolate work in a short-lived temp branch | Branch juggling, stash chaos | Clean, focused workspace | [worktree-workflows.md](./references/worktree-workflows.md) |\n| **2. Work & Commit** | Analyze changes, filter artifacts, write Conventional Commits | Bad commits, unclear history | Clean commit history | [commit-workflows.md](./references/commit-workflows.md) |\n| **3. Complete & Integrate** | Merge, create a PR, or discard work (tests-gated) | Untested code merged | Work integrated or discarded | [finish-workflows.md](./references/finish-workflows.md) |\n\n### Phase Transitions\nSetup (worktree created) → Work → Complete (committed, tests passing) → back to Setup (integrated).\n\n### Workflow Selection Guide\n- New feature/fix → Phase 1. Quick fix → Phase 2.\n- Ready to commit → Phase 2. No changes yet → keep coding.\n- Tests pass → Phase 3. Failing → return to Phase 2.\n\n### Common Workflow Patterns\n\n- **Full**: all 3 phases.\n- **Quick fix**: skip Phase 1.\n- **Parallel**: repeat Phases 1-2 per feature, then Phase 3 for each.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. **Use deterministic conventional commit format** - All authored commits follow `type(scope): summary`. Preserve the explicitly exempt Git-generated subjects defined below\n2. **Create worktree for parallel work** - Never work on multiple features in the same worktree\n3. **Verify branch is up-to-date** - Pull latest changes before creating PR\n4. **Name worktree-created branches with the numbered-worktree grammar** - `worktrees/{NNN}-{slug}` for a worktree-backed branch, `branches/{NNN}-{slug}` for a dedicated branch with none. Each namespace counts 001..999 independently, sequential, never skipped or reused. Never hand-compute `{NNN}`: allocate through `.skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh` (`create`, `create-branch` or `allocate`), which locks and seeds each counter from its high-water mark plus every matching ref. The script header carries the full grammar, the relocatable `{base}` rule and the reserved `skilled/v*`, `main` and `backup/` lanes. Distinct from the launch wrapper's unnumbered `work/{runtime}/{slug}` lane (see above).\n5. **Reference the spec packet in a `Spec:` trailer** - Put the packet path in a `Spec:` trailer shaped `Spec: <track>/<packet>[/<phase>...]`: the packet's path below `specs/`, with nested phases included and without the `specs/` segment itself. The packet query is anchored on that line, `git log -E --grep='^Spec: sk-git/028'`, so a leading `specs/` makes every commit for that packet unfindable. Omit the line when the commit is not packet work. `Refs:` is for external links only: issues, pull requests and URLs.\n6. **Clean up after merge** - Delete local and remote feature branches after successful merge\n7. **Squash commits for clean history** - Use squash merge for feature branches with many WIP commits\n8. **Provision a worktree before you trust anything it reports** - Every dependency tree here is gitignored, so a fresh worktree has none of them and fails in ways that read as broken code: a build can exit 0 having compiled nothing, and a hub-conformance check that copies a skill into a temp directory loses that skill's dependencies and reports a correct hub broken. `worktree-naming.sh create` now installs them (`--no-provision` opts out), and `worktree-naming.sh provision [dir]` fixes a worktree made another way. Both are idempotent. Provisioning **installs** by default, but what binds is narrower than the technique: **no path shared into a worktree may resolve a repository-internal reference back to the source checkout.** Two mechanisms break that, and each has its own remedy. A package's `node_modules` carries relative workspace self-links that re-anchor through wherever the link physically sits, so a wholesale link leaves the worktree reading the source checkout's code however much it edits its own. Share such a tree by linking its third-party entries individually and recreating each self-link relative to the worktree's own copy. Separately, a compiled entry point reached through a link compares the path it was invoked with against the location it derives from its own file, finds them different, and exits 0 having done nothing. Invoke such a script by its canonical path, or give the worktree its own build. A dependency tree that does neither may be linked wholesale. `worktree-naming.sh provision` installs, which satisfies the invariant the blunt way. On a large reorg, still do file/`git mv` ops in the worktree and run the spec-kit toolchain and ALL metadata regeneration on `main` after merge. See [large-reorg-playbook.md](references/large-reorg-playbook.md).\n9. **Scan for gitignored leftovers after a rename wave** - After `git mv` + merge, detect dirs with disk files but 0 tracked files (`git ls-files <dir>` empty, `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` clean) and `rm -rf` them, stale cruft left by `git mv`.\n10. **Verify rename history is preserved** - After a rename wave confirm `R`-status (not delete+add) before commit, and after merge confirm the tree has no old+new duplicate folders.\n11. **GitHub release bodies never start with an H1** - The release title field already renders `vX.X.X.X — Title`, so a body-leading `# vX.X.X.X` duplicates it. The H1 belongs ONLY to the repo's changelog md. When publishing from a changelog, strip the leading H1 (and blank lines) into a temp notes file before `gh release create/edit --notes-file`. Full mechanics: [finish-workflows.md](references/finish-workflows.md) Step 6.\n12. **Route GitKraken MCP's local-mutation tools back to Bash** - GitKraken MCP (`gitkraken.gitkraken_*`) exposes `git_add_or_commit`, `git_push`, `git_pull`, `git_fetch`, `git_checkout`, `git_branch`, `git_worktree`, and `git_stash`, duplicates of mutations already gated by NEVER #2, ALWAYS #4, and the commit-message logic. Never call these as a Bash substitute. Reserve it for GitLens AI workflows and cross-platform issue/PR/repository ops with no local equivalent. Full detail: [gitkraken-mcp-integration.md](references/gitkraken-mcp-integration.md) §2.\n13. **Honor an authorized operator's explicit direct-push directive on a protected branch** - Protected-branch rules primarily gate EXTERNAL contributors. When the operator holds bypass rights and explicitly asks for one, do it, do NOT default to a PR detour, re-ask, or frame the bypass as a problem. Still apply full commit hygiene (scope to intended files, never blind `git add -A`, and use Conventional Commits) and report plainly the push bypassed protection. Bypass authority lives in operator memory, not this codebase-agnostic skill.\n14. **Commit substantial work before an autostash-prone operation** - `git merge|pull|rebase --autostash` (or `pull.rebase=true`/`rebase.autoStash=true`) stashes the tree, runs the operation, then re-applies it, but a re-apply CONFLICT strands the changeset behind an easily-missed warning, one `git stash drop`/`clear`/gc from permanent loss. Before merging/pulling/rebasing a large or shared-branch changeset, COMMIT it (or stash and pop it yourself) instead of `--autostash`. The `post-merge`/`post-rewrite` guard ([git-hooks/lib/autostash-orphan-guard.sh](../../scripts/git-hooks/lib/autostash-orphan-guard.sh)) is a safety net, not a substitute: it anchors autostashes under `refs/autostash-rescue/<sha>` and alerts visibly if not re-applied. Recover with `git stash pop` and commit immediately, before any `git stash drop/clear`.\n15. **Reconcile the primary checkout after pushing a detached/worktree HEAD to a shared branch** - `git push origin HEAD:<branch>` from a detached HEAD or a worktree advances the remote but not the primary checkout's local ref, so the work is safe on origin yet invisible there. Say so plainly and hand over the safe sync recipe. Never stash, rebase or reset a primary tree that is dirty, diverged or concurrently owned. See [finish-workflows.md](references/finish-workflows.md) Step 5b.\n16. **Let launch-wrapper sessions autosync, and never hand-roll the publish** - Under the continuous-integration model, autosync publishes every commit to the live branch through `git-sync.sh`. Never `git push origin HEAD:<live>` or rebase onto the live branch by hand: that risks the invariants the sync protects. If autosync prints a conflict, resolve per its message and never force it. The primary checkout follows fast-forward-only and is never worked in. Full contract: [continuous-integration.md](references/continuous-integration.md).\n17. **Reap worktrees before branches, and only the exempt wrapper lane** - Remove a finished worktree's directory (`git worktree remove`) before deleting its branch, because a checked-out branch cannot be deleted. `.skilled/bin/worktree-reaper.sh` auto-reaps only `work/{runtime}/{slug}` pairs that are clean, merged into the live integration tip and proven inactive by a dead session marker. Everything else stays report-only: absence of proof is never proof of absence. Naming is enforced by a migration-tolerant pre-push hook on new remote branches only, never `skilled/v*`.\n18. **Ask before every push to a branch outside the remote allowlist** - See [Remote Push Permission Enforcement](#remote-push-permission-enforcement) above for mechanics. A prior approval never carries forward to the next push. Allowlist: [remote-branch-policy.md](references/remote-branch-policy.md).\n\n### Commit Message Logic (Human-Clear and AI-Deterministic)\n\nUse this logic whenever an AI writes or rewrites a commit message: the subject explains the\noutcome in `git log --oneline`, and the body explains the reason without packet knowledge or\njargon. The hooks enforce structure, not clarity. The structure they enforce is the \"Enforced\nrules\" JSON block in [commit-message-template.md](assets/commit-message-template.md) §7, read by\n[validate-message.mjs](scripts/validate-message.mjs) at commit time, at push time, in the agent\ngate and in CI. PR descriptions follow the block in [pr-template.md](assets/pr-template.md) and\nnew branch names the block in [worktree-checklist.md](assets/worktree-checklist.md). Each repository\nsupplies its own copies (`.sk-git/` or git config `skgit.contractDir`). A repository with no rules\nblock is not checked. There is no bypass: when a rule is wrong, change the template.\n\n#### 1. Classify Special Git Messages\n\nPreserve Git-generated subjects unchanged when they begin with `Merge `, `Revert \"`, `fixup! `,\n`squash! `, or `amend! `. Intentional checkpoints are not exempt: write them as\n`chore(wip): checkpoint <specific state>`.\n\n#### 2. Authored Subject Contract\n\nFormat:\n\n```text\ntype(scope)[!]: imperative summary\n```\n\nHard requirements:\n\n- Type and scope are required. Scope is lowercase kebab-case, a stable subsystem name, never a\n  packet, phase, task, or other numeric-only identifier.\n- Summary starts with a lowercase imperative verb, names the changed behavior or artifact (not\n  the work process), ends without punctuation, has no repeated spaces, and is specific enough to\n  distinguish this commit from adjacent work.\n- Subject has an 80-character target (`subject.length-target`, warning) and a 100-character hard limit (`subject.max-length`).\n- A `!` requires a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.\n\nDo not use vague summaries like `update`, `changes`, `cleanup`, or `work in progress`.\n\nMove process metadata (packet numbers, phases, waves, lanes, task counts, model names, review\nrounds, remediation labels, verification claims) to the body or `Refs:` line unless part of the\nbehavior being changed.\n\n#### 3. Type Selection Order\n\nUse first match:\n\n1. `release`: publishing a release.\n2. `docs`: every substantive path is documentation.\n3. `fix`: existing behavior was incorrect, unsafe, or failing.\n4. `feat`: adds new usable behavior or support.\n5. `perf`: measured performance improves, behavior unchanged.\n6. `refactor`: structure changes without behavior changes.\n7. `test`: only tests or fixtures change.\n8. `ci`: only CI workflow behavior changes.\n9. `build`: only build or dependency mechanics change.\n10. `style`: only formatting changes.\n11. `revert`/`merge`: authored revert or merge messages.\n12. `chore`: no more specific type applies.\n\nTests and documentation shipped with a feature or fix inherit that feature or fix type. Do not\nchoose `chore` merely because the commit touches many files.\n\n#### 4. Scope Selection Order\n\nFirst match, by logical owner:\n\n1. `.skilled/skills/<name>/...` -> `<name>`.\n2. `.skilled/scripts/git-hooks/...` or installer -> `git-hooks`.\n3. `AGENTS.md` or runtime agent definitions -> `agents`.\n4. `.skilled/commands/...` -> `commands`.\n5. `opencode.json`, `.utcp_config.json`, or equivalent config -> `config`.\n6. Root `README.md` only -> `readme`.\n7. Spec-doc or generated packet-metadata maintenance only -> `specs`.\n8. Documentation spanning multiple owners -> `docs`.\n9. A dominant top-level component -> its lowercase name.\n10. Inseparable cross-repository change -> `repo`.\n\nUse the full skill folder name as the canonical scope. For example, `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/...` uses `system-spec-kit`. Files in `.skilled/repo-rules/` use `repo-rules`. The template's `subject.scope-alias` rule rejects short forms listed in its `scopeAliases` map.\n\nIf two independent owners remain, split the commit instead of inventing a combined scope.\n\n#### 5. Summary Construction\n\nApply this sequence:\n\n1. State the primary outcome of the staged diff.\n2. Start with a precise imperative action (`add`, `remove`, `route`, `clarify`, etc.) naming the\n   affected behavior or artifact.\n3. Add the visible effect when the object alone is ambiguous.\n4. Remove chronology, review claims, and duplicate Conventional Commit prefixes.\n5. Read only the subject and ask: \"Would a maintainer understand what changed without opening\n   the packet?\" If not, rewrite it.\n\n#### 6. Body Contract\n\nEvery authored commit carries a body: at least one prose line, separated from the subject by a\nblank line, that says why the change exists. The number of staged paths never excuses a missing\nbody, because a later search reads the body to learn the reason, and a one-path commit is\nsearched as often as a large one. Trailers such as `Spec:` and `Commit-Id:` are machine data and\ndo not count as a body. Only the Git-generated subjects in §1 are exempt.\n\nUse the full structure below when any condition applies:\n\n- The change fixes a regression, failure, race, security issue, or data risk, or it is breaking or has migration requirements. A breaking commit MUST carry the `Context`, `Changes` and `Verification` sections below. They are required, not preferred.\n- The reason or tradeoff is not obvious from the subject.\n- The commit spans code plus generated metadata or multiple repository areas.\n\nRequired structure for breaking commits. Recommended for the other cases above:\n\n```text\nContext: <plain-language problem or reason>\n\nChanges:\n- <observable change>\n- <observable change>\n\nVerification:\n- `<command>` -> <observed result>\n\nSpec: <track>/<packet>[/<phase>...]\nCommit-Id: NNNNNNN\nRefs: <issue, PR or URL>\n```\n\nThe trailer paragraph is the commit's final paragraph, contiguous and separated from the prose\nabove it by a blank line. The `Commit-Id:` ordinal is stamped by the `prepare-commit-msg` hook\nand never typed by hand. An amend keeps its id, unless the message is replaced with `-m`, which mints a fresh one. A cherry-pick re-mints a fresh one. A rebase keeps the id, and the commit it replaced is recognised as a copy by its author email and author date.\n\nUse only sections that carry useful information, explain internal terms on first use, and state\nin verification what actually ran and its result.\n\n#### 7. Deterministic Self-Check\n\nBefore committing, verify message format (§1-2), type (§3), scope (§4), summary (§5), body\n(§6) and the final trailer paragraph satisfy their rule, and that the same staged diff would\nproduce the same subject again.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. **Force push to main/master** - Protected branches must never receive force pushes\n2. **Never create branches directly** - Via `git worktree add -b ...`. Never `git branch`, `git checkout` plus `-b`, or `git switch` plus `-c`\n3. **Commit directly to protected branches WITHOUT operator authorization** - Default to feature branches + PRs, except when the operator has bypass authority and explicitly directs a direct commit/push (see ALWAYS #13). Don't force a PR detour.\n4. **Leave worktrees uncleaned** - Remove worktree directories after merge\n5. **Commit secrets or credentials** - Use environment variables or secret management\n6. **Create PRs without description** - Always include context, changes, and testing notes\n7. **Merge without CI passing** - Wait for all checks to complete\n8. **Rebase public/shared branches** - Only rebase local, unpushed commits\n9. **Bypass a git hook with `--no-verify`** - Never skip commit-msg, pre-commit, or pre-push validation this way. If a message rule is genuinely wrong, change the rules block in the template. `--no-verify` only defers the block to pre-push and CI\n10. **Amend a commit that has already been pushed or merged** - Rewriting published history breaks other clones and any autosynced live branch. Commit a new change (or `git revert`) instead once it's left the local repo\n11. **Hand-write or edit a `Commit-Id:` value** - The `prepare-commit-msg` hook stamps the ordinal from the allocator. A typed or edited id collides with history, so the commit-msg hook refuses it\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. **Merge conflicts cannot be auto-resolved** - Needs a human decision on which changes to keep\n2. **GitHub MCP returns authentication errors** - Token may be expired or permissions insufficient\n3. **Worktree directory is locked or corrupted** - May require manual cleanup with `git worktree prune`\n4. **Force push to protected branch is requested** - Requires explicit approval and understanding of consequences\n5. **CI/CD pipeline fails repeatedly** - May indicate infrastructure issues beyond code problems\n6. **Branch divergence exceeds 50 commits** - Suggests an incremental merging strategy\n7. **Submodule conflicts detected** - Updates require careful coordination\n8. **Strict-validate run inside a bare worktree** - Its exit code is meaningless (ALWAYS #8: missing gitignored deps). Re-run on `main` post-merge before trusting any result. See [large-reorg-playbook.md](references/large-reorg-playbook.md).\n\n---\n\n## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\n### Workspace Setup Complete\n- Workspace prepared in the selected mode (`git worktree` or current branch), user-confirmed\n- Any worktree lives in the correct directory (`.worktrees/` or user-specified), branch named per convention (`worktrees/{NNN}-{slug}` or `branches/{NNN}-{slug}`)\n\n### Commit Complete\n- All changes reviewed, categorized, and artifact-filtered (build files, coverage, etc.). Only public-value files staged\n- Commit message follows Conventional Commits format\n\n### Integration Complete\n- Tests pass and branch up-to-date before merge/PR\n- PR description includes context, changes, and testing notes\n- Worktree cleaned up and local/remote feature branches deleted after merge (if used)\n\n### Quality Gates\n\n| Gate | Criteria | Blocking |\n|------|----------|----------|\n| **Pre-commit** | Artifacts excluded and staged-content gates pass | Yes |\n| **Commit-msg** | Message structure passes. Clarity warnings reviewed | Structure only |\n| **Pre-merge** | Tests pass, branch up-to-date | Yes |\n| **Pre-PR** | Description complete, CI passing | Yes |\n| **Post-merge** | Worktree removed, branches cleaned | No |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Guard paths, discover at runtime, score intents, and fall back when unsure. Because this skill has no keyed resource subdirectories, intent selects from the flat resource inventory below.\n\n```python\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nRESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / \"references\", SKILL_ROOT / \"assets\")\nDEFAULT_RESOURCE = \"references/tool-surface.md\"\n# Fallback-only: DEFAULT_RESOURCE is a defer-time suggestion, never unioned\n# into a route's loaded set. Runtime scoring uses INTENT_MODEL; this block changes no routing.\n# Per-intent weight = the MAX per-keyword weight in INTENT_MODEL for that intent\n# (all five resolve to 4). Keys and keywords MUST stay identical to INTENT_MODEL;\n# keep the two blocks in sync whenever either one is edited.\nINTENT_SIGNALS = {\n    \"STYLES\":       {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"style\", \"visual direction\", \"design reference\", \"aesthetic\", \"look and feel\", \"design language\", \"landing page\", \"typography reference\", \"palette reference\"]},\n    \"SCREENS\":      {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"screen\", \"ui pattern\", \"similar screens\", \"real app\", \"empty state\", \"component example\", \"screenshot\", \"modal\", \"dashboard\", \"onboarding\", \"settings\", \"ui element\"]},\n    \"FLOWS\":        {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"flow\", \"user flow\", \"journey\", \"multi-step\", \"steps\", \"checkout\", \"cancel subscription\", \"signup process\"]},\n    \"WIRING_AUTH\":  {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"wiring\", \"utcp\", \"oauth\", \"bearer\", \"mcp-remote\", \"authenticate\", \"manual\", \"token\", \"register\", \"plan\", \"subscription\", \"install\", \"setup\"]},\n    \"TROUBLESHOOT\": {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"error\", \"failed\", \"401\", \"connection closed\", \"not resolving\", \"not working\", \"sigsegv\", \"429\", \"quota\", \"timeout\", \"broken\", \"unauthorized\"]},\n}\n\nRESOURCE_MAP = {\n    \"STYLES\":       [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"SCREENS\":      [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"FLOWS\":        [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"WIRING_AUTH\":  [\"references/mcp-wiring.md\", \"assets/utcp-refero-manual.md\"],\n    \"TROUBLESHOOT\": [\"references/troubleshooting.md\", \"references/mcp-wiring.md\"],\n}\n\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [\n    \"Confirm the layer: styles (visual direction), screens (UI patterns), or flows (journeys)\",\n    \"Confirm the refero manual is registered and discovery (tool_info) confirms the doubled-prefix callables\",\n    \"Confirm the account has a Pro (or higher) plan; Free has no MCP access at all\",\n    \"If the evidence will influence a design decision, pair with sk-design-md-generator for a measured Style Reference (extracted design tokens); this transport never decides taste\",\n]\n\ndef _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:\n    resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()\n    resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)               # raises if path escapes the skill\n    if resolved.suffix.lower() != \".md\":\n        raise ValueError(f\"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}\")\n    return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()\n\ndef discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:\n    docs = []\n    for base in RESOURCE_BASES:\n        if base.exists():\n            docs.extend(p for p in base.rglob(\"*.md\") if p.is_file())\n    return {d.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for d in docs}\n\ndef classify_intents(request: str):\n    text = (request or \"\").lower()\n    scores = {i: 0 for i in INTENT_MODEL}\n    for intent, cfg in INTENT_MODEL.items():\n        for kw, w in cfg[\"keywords\"]:\n            if kw in text:\n                scores[intent] += w\n    ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True)\n    primary, top = ranked[0]\n    if top == 0:\n        return (None, None, scores)   # unrouted -> no intent selected; fallback branch disambiguates\n    secondary, second = ranked[1]\n    if second > 0 and (top - second) <= AMBIGUITY_DELTA:\n        return (primary, secondary, scores)\n    return (primary, None, scores)\n\ndef route_refero_resources(request: str):\n    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()\n    primary, secondary, scores = classify_intents(request)\n    intents = [i for i in (primary, secondary) if i]\n    loaded, seen, notices = [], set(), []\n\n    def load_if_available(rel: str) -> bool:\n        guarded = _guard_in_skill(rel)\n        if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:\n            load(guarded); loaded.append(guarded); seen.add(guarded)\n            return True\n        if guarded not in inventory:\n            notices.append(f\"Resource not found in inventory: {guarded}\")\n        return False\n\n    if max(scores.values() or [0]) < MIN_CONFIDENCE:\n        # Fallback-only: nothing is loaded on a zero-score route; the default\n        # reference is offered as a suggestion beside the disambiguation ask.\n        return {\"intents\": intents, \"load_level\": \"UNKNOWN_FALLBACK\", \"needs_disambiguation\": True,\n                \"disambiguation_checklist\": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST,\n                \"suggested_fallback\": DEFAULT_RESOURCE, \"resources\": loaded, \"notices\": notices}\n    for intent in intents:\n        for rel in RESOURCE_MAP.get(intent, []):\n            load_if_available(rel)\n    return {\"intents\": intents, \"intent_scores\": scores, \"resources\": loaded, \"notices\": notices}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### First Step (Always): confirm wiring, then discover\n\nThe `refero` manual is **already registered** in this repo's `.utcp_config.json` (`npx -y mcp-remote https://api.refero.design/mcp`, stdio, empty env). Verify it is present (read-only grep, or `scripts/doctor.sh`), never re-add it, and never edit it. Then discover the live callables through Code Mode before any call:\n\n```typescript\n// Discovery names appear dotted: refero.refero.refero_search_styles\nconst all = await list_tools();\n// MANDATORY: confirm the exact callable + schema before relying on any name\nconst info = await tool_info({ tool_name: \"refero.refero_refero_search_styles\" });\n```\n\nThe doubled-prefix callable form (`refero.refero_refero_<tool>`) is **confirmed by live registry evidence** (2026-07-16 discovery fixture, `references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`): all eight tools were live-listed pre-auth as `refero.refero.refero_{search_styles,search_screens,get_style,get_similar_screens,get_screen_image,get_screen,search_flows,get_flow}`, resolving the research record's conflicting derivations — the single-prefix derivation is dead. Discovery is pre-auth; authenticated CALLS remain operator-gated. The per-session `tool_info` confirmation step is still not optional. If discovery shows the eight tools missing, renamed, or expanded, **fail closed**: report the drift; a changed provider surface requires a reviewed packet update, not an improvised call.\n\n### The 8-tool surface (three layers)\n\nThe expected contract (authoritative docs baseline; `tool_info` is the final live schema). Full args, bounds, and result shapes: [`references/tool-surface.md`](references/tool-surface.md).\n\n| Layer | Tool | Required args | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Styles | `refero_search_styles` | `query` | `page` (default 1) pagination |\n| Styles | `refero_get_style` | exactly one of `style_id` \\| `style_ids[]` | Full styles are ~10-15k chars each; batch 3-4 |\n| Screens | `refero_search_screens` | `query`, `platform: \"web\"\\|\"ios\"` | Returns UUID records with `site`, `ux_patterns`, `ui_elements` |\n| Screens | `refero_get_screen` | exactly one of `screen_id` \\| `screen_ids[]` | Never pass `image_size` or `include_similar` here |\n| Screens | `refero_get_similar_screens` | `screen_id` | `limit` 1-20, default 10 (the only tool with `limit`) |\n| Screens | `refero_get_screen_image` | `screen_id` | `image_size: \"thumbnail\"\\|\"full\"` (default thumbnail); returns raw image |\n| Flows | `refero_search_flows` | `query`, `platform: \"web\"\\|\"ios\"` | Returns **numeric** flow IDs |\n| Flows | `refero_get_flow` | exactly one of `flow_id` \\| `flow_ids[]` (numbers) | Ordered steps: goal, action, system response |\n\nHard constraints: styles and screens use **UUID strings**, flows use **numeric IDs**; the two are not interchangeable. Search pagination uses `page`, never legacy `limit`/`offset`. There are **no** `search_apps`/`get_app`/`search_elements`/`get_element` tools; apps and elements are query facets, inspected through `site` and `ui_elements` in results. `response_format` is documented on the **seven text-returning tools** and must **never** be passed to `refero_get_screen_image`; treat per-tool availability as a `tool_info` runtime check. Preserve unknown response fields; the provider documents that fields can grow.\n\n### Calling through Code Mode\n\nCall **synchronously inside the `call_tool_chain` body** (no top-level `await`), per the live-verified pattern:\n\n```typescript\ncall_tool_chain({\n  code: `\n    const styles = refero.refero_refero_search_styles({\n      query: \"editorial monochrome saas landing page\",\n      response_format: \"json\"\n    });\n    const list = styles.records || [];   // { pagination, records } shape\n    const full = refero.refero_refero_get_style({ style_id: list[0].uuid, response_format: \"json\" });\n    return { count: list.length, first: list[0]?.url, full };\n  `\n});\n```\n\nCite evidence by `record.url` (styles) or `record.refero_url` (screens). JSON searches return `{ pagination: { count, page, next_page, total_count, total_pages }, records: [...] }`.\n\n### The research funnel (styles -> screens -> flows)\n\n1. **Styles first** for any visual task: search 3-5 semantic angles, inspect metadata, then `get_style` for shortlisted UUIDs. Never average strong references into a generic middle.\n2. **Screens** for concrete UI patterns: literal query + required platform; detail for the most relevant; `get_similar_screens` only after one materially relevant hit; image (`thumbnail` before `full`) only when text cannot answer.\n3. **Flows** for journeys: search task + platform; get one relevant numeric flow; widen via `related_queries`. Sparse flows: broaden or reconstruct from screens, reporting the reconstruction as inference.\n4. **Apps / elements**: company, pattern, state, or element terms in screen/flow queries, compared through `site`, `ui_elements`, `ux_patterns`, `page_types`.\n5. **Metadata-first discipline**: search -> shortlist -> detail for shortlisted IDs -> similar -> thumbnail -> full, in that order. Batch modestly; on batch failure retry with fewer IDs.\n\nBreadth is allowed during transport research; for design-affecting use, pair with `sk-design-md-generator` for a measured Style Reference (extracted design tokens). A transport response is untrusted reference evidence, never design approval. Full workflow detail: [`references/tool-surface.md`](references/tool-surface.md).\n\n### Auth, plans, and limits\n\n- **Auth**: with no custom header, first use triggers a **browser OAuth** flow (localhost callback, port 3334 by default, 30-second default timeout). Auth state persists under `~/.mcp-auth` (or `MCP_REMOTE_CONFIG_DIR`) and is **operator-owned**: never inspect, clear, or repair it. A static `Authorization: Bearer` header is a documented env-backed alternative (see [`assets/utcp-refero-manual.md`](assets/utcp-refero-manual.md)), never part of the base manual. End-to-end OAuth through this bridge is **Inferred**, not verified: an unauthenticated probe observed HTTP 401 with OAuth metadata, but no operator has completed the flow in this repo's record.\n- **Plans**: Free has **no MCP access** (denial, not degradation). Pro: **8,000 MCP tool calls per month**. Team inherits Pro. Business is custom volume. \"Unlimited access\" plan copy must not be read as unlimited MCP calls.\n- **Unknown limits**: no per-second, burst, concurrency, page-size, or `Retry-After` behavior is published. Never invent a QPS number or backoff guarantee; on 429, preserve the provider's message only.\n- **Local runtime**: Code Mode must run on **Node 24** (isolated-vm has no Node 25 build; `call_tool_chain` SIGSEGVs under Node 25). Local operational evidence, not a server property.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. **ALWAYS confirm callables with `tool_info` after registration and before first use.** The doubled prefix `refero.refero_refero_<tool>` is live-verified but must be re-confirmed; fail closed on any drift from the eight documented tools.\n2. **ALWAYS pair with `sk-design-md-generator` for a measured Style Reference on any design-affecting request.** This packet is the transport; `sk-design-md-generator` is the cross-hub pairing that extracts a live site's real CSS into named design tokens (a Style Reference DESIGN.md). Transport output can never satisfy taste, accessibility, responsiveness, or readiness gates by itself.\n3. **ALWAYS validate documented unions, enums, and bounds before calling**: exactly-one-of ID unions, UUID vs numeric ID typing, the `platform` enum, `page >= 1`, similar-screens `limit` 1-20, and the image-size enum. Pass unknown response fields through untouched.\n4. **ALWAYS follow the metadata-first funnel**: search and shortlist on metadata, fetch detail only for shortlisted IDs, similar screens only after one relevant hit, images last (`thumbnail` before `full`).\n5. **ALWAYS call synchronously inside the `call_tool_chain` body** (no top-level `await`) and cite results by their source URL (`url` / `refero_url`).\n6. **ALWAYS treat this packet as read-only against this repo** (`mutatesWorkspace: false`). Reads and writes happen against the external Refero service only; Write, Edit, and Task are forbidden tools for this transport.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. **NEVER use Write, Edit, or Task through this packet.** It is a TRANSPORT: it retrieves external evidence and changes nothing in this workspace. Hand file changes to the owning workflow skill.\n2. **NEVER edit `.utcp_config.json`'s `refero` manual.** It is validated as-is (verify, do not re-add, do not modify), and never add a second Refero manual or a Bearer token to the base manual.\n3. **NEVER claim OAuth works end-to-end.** It is **Inferred** pending an operator-completed authorization; report it as such. Never inspect, clear, or repair `~/.mcp-auth` / `MCP_REMOTE_CONFIG_DIR`, and never accept, print, or cache credentials.\n4. **NEVER invent rate limits, page sizes, retry contracts, or backoff numbers.** Only the monthly Pro quota (8,000 calls) is published; on 429, relay the provider's own message.\n5. **NEVER pass `response_format` to `refero_get_screen_image`**, and never use the deprecated legacy surface: `_tool`-suffixed names, `get_design_guidance`, numeric screen IDs, `limit`/`offset` search pagination, or `image_size`/`include_similar` on `refero_get_screen`.\n6. **NEVER treat search rank or similarity as a taste verdict**, never average strong references into a generic middle, and never copy or cache third-party reference content into this repo.\n7. **NEVER model Free-plan access as a reduced tool set.** Free has no MCP access at all; report the entitlement denial and stop.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. **ESCALATE IF authentication is required** (HTTP 401, OAuth prompt, token needs). Completing browser OAuth or obtaining a Bearer token is **operator-only**; surface the step and wait.\n2. **ESCALATE IF discovery shows catalog drift**: a documented tool missing or renamed, unexpected new tools, or schemas that contradict [`references/tool-surface.md`](references/tool-surface.md). A provider-surface change requires a reviewed packet update.\n3. **ESCALATE IF the account is Free-tier or quota-limited** (entitlement denial, 429, or quota exhaustion), reporting the provider's message verbatim.\n4. **ESCALATE IF `call_tool_chain` drops the connection** (`-32000 Connection closed`), which locally indicates a Node 25 runtime; the Node 24 pin is an operator-side fix.\n5. **ESCALATE IF retrieved evidence conflicts with a `sk-design-md-generator` Style Reference (its extracted design tokens)**, asking which source prevails before any design conclusion is drawn.\n\n---\n\n## 5.
