    "content": "\n<!-- Keywords: manual testing playbook, testing playbook, deterministic scenario, evidence collection, operator validation, multi-agent execution, release readiness, create:manual-testing-playbook -->\n\n# Manual Testing Playbook Creation\n\n`create-manual-testing-playbook` is the manual-validation package workflow for the `sk-doc` family. It authors `manual-testing-playbook/` packages for skills and systems that need reproducible operator-facing scenarios, evidence capture, release-readiness review, and realistic orchestration or multi-agent execution planning.\n\nCore principle: keep shared rules in the root playbook, keep execution truth in per-feature files, and make every scenario deterministic enough that another operator can reproduce the verdict.\n\n---\n\n## 1. WHEN TO USE\n\n### Activation Triggers\n\nUse this workflow when the request involves:\n\n- `/create:manual-testing-playbook`.\n- Creating `manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md`.\n- Building one-file-per-feature manual test scenarios.\n- Designing deterministic prompts, command sequences, expected signals, evidence, pass/fail criteria, and failure triage.\n- Planning manual validation across multiple operators, agents, CLIs, MCP tools, or runtime surfaces.\n- Converting an ad hoc release checklist into a reusable evidence-driven playbook package.\n- Aligning a manual testing playbook with a feature catalog.\n\nKeyword triggers: `manual testing playbook`, `/create:manual-testing-playbook`, `testing playbook`, `playbook system`, `deterministic scenario`, `evidence collection`, `operator validation`, `multi-agent execution`, `release readiness`.\n\nStrong signals that a playbook is warranted:\n\n- 5+ distinct features need manual validation.\n- Release decisions depend on structured evidence.\n- Realistic orchestration behavior matters.\n- Multiple operators or agents will execute the same scenarios.\n- Automated tests cover internals but not operator-visible behavior.\n\n### When NOT to Use\n\nUse another `sk-doc` packet when:\n\n- Test steps fit cleanly in a spec folder checklist.\n- The feature is one-off or experimental.\n- The system has only a few manually testable behaviors.\n- Automated tests already cover the only meaningful acceptance criteria.\n- The user asks for a feature catalog rather than executable validation scenarios. Use `create-feature-catalog`.\n- The user asks for a README, skill, agent, command, benchmark package, flowchart, or changelog. Use `create-readme`, `create-skill`, `create-agent`, `create-command`, `create-benchmark`, `create-flowchart`, or `create-changelog`.\n- The task audits, validates, scores, or optimizes an existing playbook without creating or extending the package. Use `create-quality-control`.\n\n---\n\n## 2. SMART ROUTING\n\n### Decision Rule\n\nDecision rule:\n\n```text\nNeed reusable manual validation with captured evidence?\nYES -> Create a playbook package\nNO  -> Keep test steps in spec/checklist docs\n```\n\n### Family Boundary\n\nThis packet owns manual testing playbook packages only. It consumes shared `sk-doc` standards from `../shared`, but the advisor identity lives at the `sk-doc` hub root. Do not add a packet-local `graph-metadata.json`.\n\n### Smart Router Pseudocode\n\nFor this flat-reference packet, the canonical resilient router discovers resources at call\ntime, guards and loads only what exists, scores the two authoring scopes, and returns a\ndisambiguation checklist rather than silently loading nothing:\n\n```python\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nRESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / \"references\", SKILL_ROOT / \"assets\")\nDEFAULT_RESOURCE = \"references/README.md\"\n\n# Two authoring scopes; keywords come from this packet's activation triggers.\nINTENT_MODEL = {\n    \"root_playbook\": {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"manual testing playbook\", \"/create:manual-testing-playbook\", \"testing playbook\", \"release readiness\"]},\n    \"per_feature_scenario\": {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"deterministic scenario\", \"evidence collection\", \"operator validation\", \"multi-agent execution\"]},\n}\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [\n    \"Confirm the target skill or system and the feature set under test\",\n    \"Confirm root playbook index scope vs per-feature scenario file scope\",\n    \"Confirm the evidence and pass/fail validation expectations\",\n]\n\ndef discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:\n    docs = []\n    for base in RESOURCE_BASES:\n        if base.exists():\n            docs.extend(path for path in base.rglob(\"*.md\") if path.is_file())\n    return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}\n\ndef _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:\n    resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()\n    resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)\n    if resolved.suffix.lower() != \".md\":\n        raise ValueError(f\"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}\")\n    return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()\n\ndef load_if_available(relative_path, inventory, loaded, seen) -> None:\n    guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)\n    if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:\n        load(guarded)\n        loaded.append(guarded)\n        seen.add(guarded)\n\ndef score_intents(request) -> dict:\n    text = request.text.lower()\n    scores = {intent: 0 for intent in INTENT_MODEL}\n    for intent, cfg in INTENT_MODEL.items():\n        for kw in cfg[\"keywords\"]:\n            if kw in text:\n                scores[intent] += cfg[\"weight\"]\n    return scores\n\ndef route_manual_testing_playbook_request(request):\n    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()\n    loaded, seen = [], set()\n    scores = score_intents(request)\n\n    if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 4:                      # Tier 1: unclear scope\n        load_if_available(DEFAULT_RESOURCE, inventory, loaded, seen)\n        return {\n            \"load_level\": \"UNKNOWN_FALLBACK\",\n            \"needs_disambiguation\": True,\n            \"disambiguation_checklist\": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST,\n            \"resources\": loaded,\n        }\n\n    scope = max(scores, key=scores.get)                       # Tier 2: happy path\n    # Flat resource topology: no references/<key>/ subdirectories. The scope selects the\n    # authoring target documented above, not a keyed subtree; load the flat refs that exist.\n    for path in sorted(inventory):\n        load_if_available(path, inventory, loaded, seen)\n    return {\"scope\": scope, \"resources\": loaded}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. OUTPUT PACKAGE CONTRACT\n\n### Canonical Package Shape\n\nAuthor this layout:\n\n```text\nmanual-testing-playbook/\n|-- manual-testing-playbook.md\n|-- category-name/\n|   |-- feature-name.md\n|   `-- another-feature-name.md\n`-- another-category/\n    `-- feature-name.md\n```\n\nPackage invariants:\n\n- The root file is always `manual-testing-playbook.md`.\n- Per-feature files live in root-level category folders.\n- Category directories use descriptive kebab-case names such as `category-name` (no numeric prefix).\n- Per-feature files use stable kebab-case slugs such as `feature-name.md`; no numeric file prefix.\n- Per-feature snippet order is defined by the root playbook listing order.\n- Display order is owned by the root playbook index (`manual-testing-playbook.md`), not the folder name.\n- Benchmark tier is owned by the per-feature file's optional `stage:` frontmatter field (`routing` default, or `holdout`/`negative`), not by a filename token.\n- Every feature ID maps to exactly one per-feature file.\n\nTwo runtimes, where a system ships as both a skill and a hosted assistant:\n\n- Write two scenario sets, never one system tested twice. Category folders carry a\n  prefix naming the runtime, and every per-feature file carries a matching\n  `- Runtime:` line in `SOURCE METADATA`.\n- Each set opens with one identity handover scenario, named as a precondition by\n  every other scenario in that set. It passes only when the reply carries a\n  verbatim string present in that runtime's own instructions and absent from the\n  other's, plus the delivery contract only that runtime can honour. A reply that\n  could have come from either runtime is a FAIL.\n- A handover string is proved against each runtime's whole load surface, not\n  against its top-level instruction file alone. A skill runtime loads that file\n  and everything the file sends it to. A hosted runtime loads its own\n  instructions and every document attached to it. A string absent from one file\n  and present three directories away has not been proved.\n- Read the string at run time where it can move. Grading on a literal version\n  line fails the next time that version is bumped, which makes a version check\n  wearing an identity check's clothes.\n\nContract boundary:\n\n- The operator-scenario contract is the five-section, execution-evidence contract\n  defined here and checked by `scripts/validate-playbook-package.cjs`.\n- The routing-gold contract is the compact typed-routing schema checked by\n  `sk-create-skill/scripts/validate-playbook-topology.cjs`.\n- `playbook-corpus-manifest.json` is an explicit whole-tree override map consumed only\n  by the operator validator. A listed routing-gold tree is excluded from operator\n  checks; for every other file, a non-empty `expected_workflow_mode` plus at least one\n  `expected_leaf_resources` pair in frontmatter classifies that file as routing gold.\n  Files without that signature are operator-scenario files. The topology gate does not\n  read this manifest and keeps its existing boundary.\n\nDo not create:\n\n- A `snippets/` subtree for canonical per-feature files.\n- Separate canonical `review_protocol.md`.\n- Separate canonical `subagent_utilization_ledger.md`.\n- Duplicated scenario truth across multiple sidecar files.\n\n### Root Playbook Responsibilities\n\n`manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md` is the package directory and review surface. It owns:\n\n- Frontmatter and H1 intro.\n- Global overview and coverage note.\n- Global preconditions.\n- Global evidence requirements.\n- Deterministic command notation rules.\n- Integrated review protocol and release-readiness rules.\n- Integrated orchestration and wave-planning guidance.\n- Category sections with short per-feature summaries.\n- Automated test cross-reference section.\n- Feature catalog cross-reference index.\n\nRoot summaries should be concise but useful:\n\n- Provide enough context to understand what each scenario covers.\n- Preview operator intent and prompt shape.\n- Do not duplicate the full execution matrix from the per-feature file.\n\nRoot-to-feature rule: the root document explains package-level policy; per-feature files carry scenario-specific execution truth.\n\n### Per-Feature File Responsibilities\n\nEach per-feature file is the canonical scenario contract for one feature ID.\n\nRequired per-feature section order:\n\n1. `## 1. OVERVIEW`\n2. `## 2. SCENARIO CONTRACT`\n3. `## 3. TEST EXECUTION`\n4. `## 4. REFERENCES` or `## 4. SOURCE FILES`\n5. `## 5. SOURCE METADATA`\n\nEach per-feature file must include:\n\n- Frontmatter with `title`, `description`, and a 4-part `version`.\n- Realistic user request when it clarifies user intent.\n- Operator prompt or orchestrator prompt.\n- Exact prompt in the scenario table when a table is used.\n- Exact command sequence.\n- Expected signals.\n- Evidence requirements.\n- Pass/fail criteria.\n- Failure triage.\n- Root playbook link.\n- Feature catalog link when applicable.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RESULTS STORAGE CONTRACT\n\nA playbook is a corpus. Running it produces evidence, and that evidence has a home: the same\n`benchmark/` tree that holds every other measurement of the skill. Without this rule a run leaves\nnothing behind, and the next person has no way to know the playbook was ever executed.\n\n### Where A Run Lands\n\n```text\n<skill>/\n|-- manual-testing-playbook/          # the corpus, an input, never rewritten by a run\n`-- benchmark/\n    `-- reports/\n        |-- README.md                 # the run index, one row per folder\n        `-- 2026-07-29--manual-testing-playbook--goal-hook/\n            |-- README.md\n            |-- skill-benchmark-report.json\n            |-- skill-benchmark-report.md\n            |-- results.csv\n            |-- failed-runs.md\n            |-- findings-and-recommendations.md\n            `-- source.md\n```\n\nRun folders are named `<YYYY-MM-DD>--<subject>--<variant>`, dated by execution. When a run is\n**feature-scoped** — a hand-derived validation of one feature or scenario group rather than a full-corpus\nharness sweep — name the `<variant>` for the feature (e.g. `goal-hook`) and record the model/executor\ninside the report, so the folder stays legible across models. `create-benchmark` owns the grammar in full;\nsee its naming convention section for the field vocabulary and the one carve-out.\n\n### Manual scenario completion\n\n<!-- MANUAL_PLAYBOOK_RESULT_PERSISTENCE_CONTRACT -->\nA manual scenario is incomplete until its `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `SKIP` outcome, its reason and its evidence paths are\nrecorded in the skill's `benchmark/reports/<dated-run-label>/` folder. The wrapper that once persisted them\nwas retired with the Lane C harness, so the record is written by hand until a replacement exists.\n\n### Rules\n\n- The corpus is an input. A run never edits `manual-testing-playbook/`, and gold that needs to change\n  gets a corpus revision rather than a rewritten scenario.\n- Curated summaries and result tables live in the run folder. Raw transcripts and copied artifacts stay\n  in the spec packet that produced them, named in `source.md`.\n- A run whose result changes gets a new folder. A prior run is never overwritten.\n- Every file in the folder derives from the run record. A field the run did not capture reads as not\n  recorded; it is never filled in from inference.\n\n---\n\n## 5. HOW IT WORKS - AUTHORING WORKFLOW\n\nFollow this sequence:\n\n1. Confirm the target skill or system, package owner, feature set, and whether a feature catalog already exists.\n2. Decide whether a manual testing playbook is appropriate using the decision rule in this skill.\n3. Define category directories using a descriptive kebab-case slug such as `category-name`.\n4. Define stable feature IDs using a consistent `{PREFIX}-{NNN}` pattern.\n5. Create the root `manual-testing-playbook/` directory.\n6. Create `manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md` from `assets/manual-testing-playbook-template.md`.\n7. Create one per-feature file for each feature ID from `assets/manual-testing-playbook-snippet-template.md`.\n8. Write root package policy before writing scenario-specific exceptions.\n9. Write each per-feature prompt and execution truth before polishing root summary prose.\n10. Fill each scenario contract with the nine display fields: Feature ID, Feature Name, Scenario Objective, Exact Prompt, Exact Command Sequence, Expected Signals, Evidence, Pass/Fail Criteria, Failure Triage. The operator validator's eight unconditional checks cover Feature ID plus the seven execution/link fields; realistic user request, table prompt, and feature-catalog link are conditional checks.\n11. Write root category summaries and link every per-feature file.\n12. Add automated-test anchors when they exist.\n13. Add feature-catalog cross-references when a catalog exists.\n14. Explicitly note when a scenario has no dedicated catalog entry.\n15. Review destructive scenarios and isolate them in root preconditions and recovery guidance.\n16. Validate the root document with shared validators.\n17. Manually spot-check per-feature structure, prompt synchronization, feature ID counts, and local links.\n18. Report any remaining manual validation scope honestly.\n\nAuthoring sequence matters:\n\n- Decide categories and IDs before writing summaries.\n- Write root package policy before scenario exceptions.\n- Write execution truth before root prose.\n- Keep scenario-specific execution truth in per-feature files.\n\n---\n\n## 6. SCENARIO DESIGN RULES\n\n### Determinism\n\nEach scenario must be reproducible by another operator. Include exact prompts, exact command sequences, observable expected signals, captured evidence, and binary pass/fail criteria.\n\nExecution status is limited to:\n\n- `PASS`\n- `FAIL`\n- `SKIP` with a specific sandbox blocker\n\nDo not classify scenarios outside the `PASS` / `FAIL` / `SKIP` enum. A `SKIP` must name a specific sandbox or runtime blocker.\n\n### Prompt Quality\n\nPrompts should be:\n\n- Realistic, not bare command paraphrases.\n- Deterministic enough to produce stable evidence.\n- Explicit about what to capture.\n- Explicit about the user-facing verdict or outcome.\n- Compact enough for a 9-column table cell.\n\nWeak prompt:\n\n```text\nTest search\n```\n\nAcceptable prompt:\n\n```text\nUse advisor_recommend for the flaky routing-threshold issue, capture the returned recommendation set, and return a concise pass/fail verdict with the main reason.\n```\n\n### Natural-Human vs RCAF Voice\n\nThe canonical `Prompt:` field defaults to natural-human voice. Match how a real user would phrase the request to an AI in conversation.\n\nUse the RCAF wrapper only when the actor is an AI orchestrator:\n\n```text\nAs a {ROLE}, {ACTION} against {TARGET}. Verify {EXPECTED_OUTCOME}. Return {OUTPUT_FORMAT}.\n```\n\nUse natural-human voice when:\n\n- A human asks the AI directly in conversation.\n- The scenario is a code review, commit/git workflow, bug fix, code question, or preference question.\n- The scenario could plausibly originate from a Slack DM or terminal prompt.\n\nUse RCAF when:\n\n- The actor is an AI orchestrator delegating to another tool, AI, agent, CLI, or runtime.\n- Role context determines safety refusal behavior.\n- The validation contract treats the orchestrator as the operator.\n\nWhen in doubt, prefer natural-human voice. The `Real user request:` field is always natural-human and serves as the voice reference baseline.\n\n### Prompt Synchronization Gate\n\nThese fields must agree:\n\n- Structured prompt field in `SCENARIO CONTRACT`.\n- `Exact Prompt` column in the execution table.\n- Any root summary prompt text.\n- A conversation chain's Turn 1 input, when the scenario has one, because that is the copy a runner sends.\n\nDo not ship unsynchronized prompt fields. `scripts/validate-playbook-package.cjs` reports each copy that disagrees with the contract as a `PROMPT_UNSYNCED` warning. Quotes, backticks, emphasis and spacing are presentation and are ignored. Any difference in the words is reported.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Enumerating only the first\nlevel once left most of this corpus unscanned: a fleet run reported success while roots it had\nnever opened carried hundreds of violations. If you change discovery, re-check the scanned count\nagainst `find .skilled/skills -type d -name manual-testing-playbook | wc -l` — a root that is not\nscanned cannot fail, so absence looks exactly like success.\n\n**Make a clean package permanent.** When a package reaches zero violations, remove it from\n`warnPackages` in `playbook-corpus-manifest.json` in the same change, and add each of its roots to\n`playbook-failclosed-allowlist.txt`. Graduating is what converts a one-time cleanup into a standing\nguarantee: a warn-listed package reports its violations and ships anyway. The CI workflow\n`.github/workflows/playbook-operator-contract.yml` runs the fleet validator and separately asserts\nevery allowlisted root is still discovered, so a root cannot quietly leave enforcement by being\nrenamed or moved. Fix a failing package rather than removing its line.\n\nThe command validates the operator-scenario contract, not the routing-gold contract. It walks every non-excluded\nscenario tree and checks, per feature: five-section ordering; `title`, `description`, and four-part `version`\nfrontmatter; Feature ID; operator/orchestrator prompt; exact command sequence; expected signals; evidence;\npass/fail criteria; failure triage; root-playbook link; allowed verdicts; filename/category shape; unique IDs;\nroot-index bijection; local links; evergreen truth; and placeholder exclusion. Conditional checks cover a realistic\nuser request when user intent is explicitly being clarified, an exact prompt when a scenario table is present,\nand a feature-catalog link when catalog applicability is declared.\n\nThe validator derives scenario and category counts at run time. A root's hand-typed census is reported as a warning,\nincluding a mismatch, so documentation repair remains separate from enforcement. Existing measured packages are\nlisted in the validator's staged warning set for the first fleet run; clean packages and new playbooks fail closed.\nPromotion removes a package from that warning set only after a clean run.\n\nThe validator also checks the root playbook for the result-persistence completion marker and the complete `PASS` / `FAIL` / `SKIP`\nvocabulary as advisory warnings. Missing either item never creates a new fail-closed violation for an existing package.\nPrompt synchronization is advisory in the same way: a prompt copy that disagrees with the scenario contract is a\n`PROMPT_UNSYNCED` warning, never a violation.\n\nExit codes are direct: `0` means conforming or staged warning, `1` means a fail-closed contract violation, and `2`\nmeans a usage or boundary error. Strict mode is on by default; `--no-strict` is local triage only and must not be\nused by CI.\n\nThe existing `validate-playbook-topology.cjs` remains the routing-gold consumer and is intentionally unchanged.\nIt continues reading its current playbook paths without consulting the additive corpus manifest.\n\n---\n\n## 8. This is the primary path.\n\n**Validation-only.** The user already has a `DESIGN.md` + `tokens.json` pair (from a prior extraction or hand-edited) and wants to confirm fidelity. That is out of scope — this skill captures measured reality, it does not create new direction.\n- The task is **authoring a Style Reference from a brief alone** with no live site to measure. That is forward-authoring, and it is OUT OF SCOPE for this mode. This mode reports what is measurably there. A brief-only request that does not name this mode's artifact is a different contract, routed to the sibling authoring skill `sk-design`, never satisfied by loosening fidelity here. The line between measured values and a brief's stated intent is drawn in `references/authoring-boundary.md`.\n- The target is a **Figma file**, not a live website. Use `mcp-figma` to extract from Figma Desktop.\n- The user only wants a **screenshot or visual preview** of a page. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### The Three-Phase Pipeline\n\nEvery extraction runs as a sequential pipeline. No phase can be skipped in a full run, though VALIDATE and REPORT can be invoked standalone on an existing `DESIGN.md` + `tokens.json` pair.\n\n### Procedure Card Selection\n\nAfter the hub selects the public `md-generator` mode, select the private `procedures/design-system-extraction.md` card when the request involves measured extraction, token capture, CSS capture, `DESIGN.md` generation, source design systems, screenshots, brand references, gaps, inconsistencies, or grounding future work in an existing surface. Cite that card by relative path in the plan or proof line. The card supports this mode; it is not a public route.\n\nIf the card does not match, state `Procedure applied: none - baseline md-generator pipeline` and continue with phase detection (`EXTRACT_WRITE`, `VALIDATE`, `REPORT`, `STUDY`) plus the existing resource router.\n\n### Backend Boundary Preservation\n\nProcedure support does not replace or generalize the extraction backend. `design-md-generator` remains the only mutating `sk-design` mode, with `backendKind: playwright-extract`, Write/Edit/Bash permission, and the embedded TypeScript pipeline under `backend/scripts/`. The protected entrypoints are `extract.ts`, `build-write-prompt.ts`, `validate.ts`, `report-gen.ts`, `preview-gen.ts`, and `proof.ts`; package-level verification remains `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, and `npm test` from `backend/` when operator policy allows those commands.\n\nThe procedure card can shape planning and proof, but it must not flatten this skill into read-only guidance or alter its owned extract-write-validate write boundary.\n\n### Context, Proof, And Direct Fallback\n\nRecord the context basis before extraction or validation: public mode `md-generator`, selected procedure card or no-procedure fallback, pipeline phase, source type, target URL or artifact, output paths, tool-readiness state, loaded references, and value-origin risks. Before any completion claim, include proof naming the selected procedure card, backend entrypoint used, `tokens.json`/`DESIGN.md` provenance, validation result, and unresolved gaps.\n\nIf subagents are unavailable or disallowed, execute directly in the current session using this mode's normal backend boundary. Direct fallback does not weaken the pipeline: full extraction still requires extract, write, and validate; validation-only and report-only paths still use their dedicated backend entrypoints.\n\n**Process Flow:** `EXTRACT (Phase 1)` → `WRITE (Phase 2)` → `VALIDATE (Phase 3)` → `REPORT (Phase 4, optional)`\n\n- **EXTRACT** — Playwright crawls 5 viewports, collecting computed CSS (colors, typography, shadows, radii, spacing, CSS variables), measured image-edge outlines, nested/concentric radii, root font smoothing, and hit-target affordances when present, plus dark-mode/framework/icon/motion/a11y signals. Every token is tagged with a stability class (L1–L4, see below). Output: `tokens.json`.\n- **WRITE** — `build-write-prompt.ts` runs first: it pre-renders the value tables (Tokens — Colors, Spacing & Shapes, Surfaces, Quick Start) plus a FACTS block deterministically from tokens via `formatters-v3.ts` (doc-as-view, no AI on the value tables). Paste those sections unchanged; write prose only (intro, Typography role prose, Components, Do's/Don'ts, Elevation, Imagery, Layout, Agent Prompt Guide, Similar Brands) — voice per `references/writing-style-guide.md`. Elevation renders FLAT when there are 0 shadow tokens. Output: `DESIGN.md`.\n- **VALIDATE** — `validate.ts` checks hex accuracy, v3 section completeness, Quick-Start fidelity, and prose provenance (see \"What `validate.ts` traces\" below). Output: pass/fail with a dual score and per-finding messages.\n- **REPORT** (optional) — `report-gen.ts` and `preview-gen.ts` render visual artifacts (HTML report, preview) for human review.\n\nFull phase-by-phase actions and handoff: `references/extraction-workflow.md`.\n\n### Cardinal Fidelity Rule\n\n**Every hex code, pixel value, font weight, box shadow, border radius, and spacing value in `DESIGN.md` MUST be copied verbatim from `tokens.json`.** No estimation, no rounding, no invention, no \"close enough\" substitution. This is the single non-negotiable contract of the skill — it is what makes `DESIGN.md` a hallucination-proof reference.\n\n- **Hex codes** must use **6-digit lowercase** format (e.g., `#1a1a2e`, never `#1A1A2E` or `#1a1a2`).\n- **Stability gates**: only L1 (permanent/brand-level) and L2 (system/component-level) tokens belong in the main DESIGN.md sections. L3 (campaign-level, e.g., a seasonal accent color) may appear with an explicit \"Subject to change\" annotation. L4 (content-level, e.g., a hero image's dominant color) is excluded.\n- **Dark mode**: include a dark-mode section ONLY when the extractor detected a dark-mode palette. Do not fabricate a dark palette from the light one.\n- **What `validate.ts` traces**: validation hard-checks hex codes (against `tokens.colorTokens`) and the Quick Start values (every Quick Start hex traces to a token; `--page-max-width` matches `tokens.spacingSystem.maxContentWidth`). Non-hex values (pixel sizes, font weights, shadows, radii) are NOT re-traced by the validator — their fidelity is guaranteed upstream because the WRITE phase pre-renders the value tables from `formatters-v3.ts` and supplies the typography/component numbers verbatim in the FACTS block, so the AI never types them. Treat the cardinal rule as the binding contract for those values even though validation does not re-check each one.\n\n### Authoring Boundary\n\nThe cardinal rule stays enforceable by inspection because every value has a legible origin. A value is **measured** (read off the page and present in `tokens.json`), **brief-provided** (supplied by the user, not the page), **inferred** (a grounded characterization of a measured value) or **absent** (never captured). Only measured values enter the token tables, and they enter unlabeled, so an unlabeled value is a promise it was measured. Brief-provided values stay in prose as a stated intent and never sit in a value table. Inferred claims carry `[INFERRED]` and cite the measured token they rest on. Absent values are stamped or omitted rather than backfilled. This boundary adds no capability and relaxes the fidelity contract by not one digit. When a value's origin is unclear, or a request asks to author from a brief with no live site, load `references/authoring-boundary.md` for the full line and `assets/source-of-truth-router-card.md` to sort each value before writing. Authoring from a brief alone is forward-authoring and stays out of scope (Section 1, When NOT to Use).\n\n### Invocation\n\n> **Working directory.** One-time setup runs from `backend/`. Every pipeline script runs from the **repo root** with the full script path — `extract.ts` refuses any `--output` that resolves inside the skill, so a relative `specs/...` path only resolves correctly from there. Full phase-by-phase actions: `references/extraction-workflow.md`. Complete flag reference: `backend/README.md`.\n\n```bash\n# One-time setup\ncd .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend && npm install && npx playwright install chromium\n\n# Phase 1 — extract (writes tokens.json to --output)\nnpx ts-node .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend/scripts/extract.ts <url> --fast --output specs/<track>/<packet>/output\n\n# Phase 2 — pre-render value tables + FACTS block, then write DESIGN.md prose\nnpx ts-node .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend/scripts/build-write-prompt.ts specs/<track>/<packet>/output/tokens.json\n\n# Phase 3 — validate (DESIGN.md first, tokens.json second)\nnpx ts-node .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend/scripts/validate.ts <DESIGN.md> specs/<track>/<packet>/output/tokens.json\n```\n\nOptional Phase 4 (from the repo root, tokens.json first): `proof.ts <url> <tokens.json>`, `report-gen.ts <tokens.json> <dir> <DESIGN.md>`, `preview-gen.ts <tokens.json> <dir>`. Interaction capture is **default-on**; opt out with `--no-interaction` or `--fast-no-interaction`.\n\n### Token Stability Classes (L1–L4)\n\nEach token is classified L1 (Permanent/`infrastructure`) through L4 (Content/`content`) by the deterministic classifier in `backend/scripts/cluster.ts`. L1+L2 populate the main `DESIGN.md` sections, L3 gets a \"Subject to change\" annotation, L4 is excluded entirely. Boundary tokens take the higher (more restrictive) class. Full class table, the emitted `stability.layer` string mapping, and the coverage-election pre-gate: `references/extraction-workflow.md` (Section 3).\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. **ALWAYS read `references/design-md-format.md` and `references/writing-style-guide.md` before writing DESIGN.md.** These define the v3 Style Reference section specification and the voice/tone rules. No DESIGN.md is conformant without them.\n2. **ALWAYS copy every numeric CSS value verbatim from `tokens.json`.** Hex colors, pixel sizes, font weights, box shadows, border radii, spacing values — every number must match `tokens.json` exactly. This is the cardinal fidelity rule.\n3. **ALWAYS use 6-digit lowercase hex** for every color in DESIGN.md (e.g., `#1a1a2e`, never `#1A1A2E`, `#333`, `rgb()`, or `hsl()`).\n4. **ALWAYS apply stability gates:** L1 and L2 colours in the main token table; L3 colours in the \"Current Campaign Colors (Subject to change)\" sub-table; L4 tokens excluded entirely.\n5. **ALWAYS run `validate.ts` before claiming completion** of any extraction or DESIGN.md edit. Validation checks hex accuracy against `tokens.json`, v3 Style Reference section completeness, Quick-Start fidelity (every Quick Start hex traces to a token, `--page-max-width` matches `tokens.json`), and prose provenance — the gate passes only with zero hard failures in the `target`, `schema` and `provenance` categories, and `valuesScore` and `claimsScore` print as information.\n6. **ALWAYS include a dark-mode section ONLY when `tokens.json` contains a detected dark-mode palette.** Never infer, derive, or fabricate a dark palette from the light tokens.\n7. **ALWAYS include an accessibility section** drawn from the `tokens.json` a11y data (contrast ratios, focus ring styles, minimum touch-target sizes). If the extractor captured no a11y data, note the absence rather than inventing values.\n8. **ALWAYS confirm tool readiness** before any extract/validate/report invocation: `cd backend && npm install && npx playwright install chromium`. The embedded tool requires Node.js and a Playwright Chromium binary.\n9. **ALWAYS cite `procedures/design-system-extraction.md` or the no-procedure fallback** before substantial extraction planning, generation, validation, or report output.\n10. **ALWAYS, on a brief-only request with no live URL, STOP before producing any Style Reference content.** The entire response is text only: either (a) a request for the live URL to crawl, or (b) an explicit statement, citing `references/authoring-boundary.md` by path, that brief-only authoring is out of scope for this mode and naming where it routes instead (the sibling authoring skill `sk-design`). Cite both `references/authoring-boundary.md` and `assets/source-of-truth-router-card.md` by their file paths in the response text — reading them via a tool call is not a substitute for naming them in what the user sees. **NEVER produce a partial or full DESIGN.md artifact as a byproduct of this decision** — no Tokens table, no Surfaces, no Quick Start — even with a disclaimer sentence attached or brief values Origin-labeled. A labeled or disclaimed artifact is still forward-authoring; the boundary forbids the artifact itself, not just unlabeled values inside it. There is no third option and no \"boundary exception\" framing that produces output anyway.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. **NEVER estimate, round, or invent a hex, pixel, font-weight, shadow, or radius value in DESIGN.md.** Every value must trace back to a token in `tokens.json`. Even trivial-looking values like `1px` borders or `0.25rem` spacing must be confirmed.\n2. **NEVER include L4 (content) tokens in DESIGN.md.** These are image-derived or one-off values that do not represent the design system.\n3. **NEVER replace the v3 Style Reference format with a freeform structure.** The named sections (Tokens — Colors/Typography/Spacing & Shapes, Components, Do's and Don'ts, Surfaces, Elevation, Layout, Agent Prompt Guide, Similar Brands, Quick Start) are part of the contract that downstream consumers — `sk-code` and AI coding agents — depend on. Never assert a false system (gradient-as-depth, focus-consistent) the tokens contradict.\n4. **NEVER skip validation before claiming a DESIGN.md is complete.** An unvalidated DESIGN.md is a draft. Validation errors must be resolved before completion.\n5. **NEVER write DESIGN.md without reading `tokens.json` first.** The markdown exists only as a faithful rendering of the token data; writing without the source data guarantees hallucination.\n6. **NEVER produce any Tokens table (Colors, Typography, Spacing & Shapes, Border Radius, or any other) when the request is brief-only with no live URL to crawl** — not even with an Origin/brief-provided label or a disclaimer sentence attached. The correct response for that condition contains zero token tables: either a URL request or an explicit out-of-scope statement per ALWAYS rule #10. Outside that specific no-live-URL condition, a brief-provided value must never appear inside an actual Tokens table row, even when a separate Provenance/source-of-truth table also exists elsewhere in the response. A separate labeling table does not cure an unlabeled value sitting in the real Tokens table — brief-provided values stay in prose only, per `references/authoring-boundary.md`'s measured/brief-provided/inferred/absent line (Section 3, \"Only measured values enter the token tables, and they enter unlabeled\").\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. **ESCALATE IF the extract fails** (Playwright cannot reach the URL, JavaScript rendering times out, or the page emits no measurable CSS). Report the specific error, the URL, and whether the site requires authentication or blocks automated crawlers. Do not retry in a loop.\n2. **ESCALATE IF dark-mode detection is ambiguous** — the extractor found a `prefers-color-scheme` media query but could not capture the dark palette values. Ask whether to proceed with light-only output or to investigate a manual dark-mode toggle on the site.\n3. **ESCALATE IF a token straddles the L2/L3 boundary** and the classifier cannot disambiguate. Surface the token and its context and ask which class to assign.\n4. **ESCALATE IF validation reports hex mismatches** that appear to be extractor bugs rather than write-phase errors (e.g., `tokens.json` itself contains `#1A1A2E` — invalid case — where the live CSS was `#1a1a2e`). Ask whether to correct `tokens.json` before re-validating.\n5. **ESCALATE IF the user wants to edit DESIGN.md by hand after extraction** and remove or alter token-derived values. The DESIGN.md is a fidelity artifact; manual edits that deviate from `tokens.json` break validation. Offer to re-run extraction with different parameters instead.\n\n---\n\n## 5.     "content": "\n<!-- Keywords: magicpath, magicpath-ai, magicpath components, magicpath search components, magicpath inspect component, magicpath themes, magicpath design system, magicpath cli transport, magicpath canvas, magicpath share link -->\n\n# MagicPath (mcp-magicpath)\n\nLook up **MagicPath** components, projects, teams, design systems, and the live web canvas through the **`magicpath-ai` Node CLI** from an agent, via Code Mode's UTCP `cli` transport. MagicPath ships **no MCP server**; the bridge is the CLI, registered as the manual named `magicpath` in this repo's `.utcp_config.json`. The registered surface is **read-only on purpose**: fourteen tools that only read. The CLI can also write `.tsx` files into the calling project, install npm packages, and create remote projects and component revisions (`add`, `code`, `image`, `create-project`, `clone`), but those are deliberately **not registered**, so an agent cannot reach them through a tool call. Deep operational detail lives in [`references/tool-surface.md`](references/tool-surface.md), [`references/credential-setup.md`](references/credential-setup.md), [`references/mutation-boundary.md`](references/mutation-boundary.md), and [`references/design-authority.md`](references/design-authority.md).\n\n> **Design authority (read before any work).** Every MagicPath surface is a design surface: components, themes, CSS variables, fonts, canvas state. This packet therefore loads **`sk-design` unconditionally** and operates under the **design agent persona** resolved from the active runtime's agent directory. The transport retrieves; `sk-design` decides. Neither the persona nor the pairing widens this packet's authority — the transport's own tool surface stays narrower than the persona's and wins on every conflict. Full contract: [`references/design-authority.md`](references/design-authority.md).\n\n> **Transport shape (read first).** This is a `cli` transport manual, not an `mcp` one. The manual command (`node .skilled/bin/magicpath-utcp-manual.cjs`) emits the UTCP manual that lists the fourteen tools; each tool then runs through `node .skilled/bin/magicpath-utcp-exec.cjs`, which shells out to the `magicpath-ai` binary. Code Mode's naming convention is `{manual}.{tool}`, so the callable form is `magicpath.<tool>(...)` (for example `magicpath.search_components`), and discovery names appear dotted as `magicpath.<tool>`. The tool names have no `magicpath_` prefix of their own, so the prefix is applied once, not doubled. Confirm the exact callable with `tool_info` per session and fail closed on drift.\n\n> **Calling convention (hard).** Inside `call_tool_chain`, tools are **synchronous**. Call them directly. Do **not** use `await`, do **not** use top-level `await`, and do **not** return a Promise — a returned Promise silently marshals as `{}` with no error. Plain JavaScript only; TypeScript type annotations fail to parse. A failing command does **not** throw. It returns the error text or a JSON error object as an ordinary value, so callers must inspect the returned value rather than rely on `try`/`catch`.\n\n---\n\n## 1. WHEN TO USE\n\n### Activation Triggers\n\n**Use when** the user wants to:\n- Look up a MagicPath component by name across personal and team projects, or read a component's source, dependencies, and imports without installing it.\n- List the projects, components, teams, or members reachable to the signed-in MagicPath user.\n- Read a MagicPath design system (theme): its CSS variables, fonts, and styling prompt, to match generated UI to an existing brand rather than inventing values.\n- Inspect the live MagicPath web canvas: the components and images currently selected, and the projects the user has open.\n- List MagicPath components already installed in the current project directory.\n- Produce a shareable URL for a MagicPath component or project to surface in conversation.\n- Verify the `magicpath` manual wiring, the credential, and the CLI reachability.\n\n**Keyword Triggers**: \"magicpath\", \"magicpath-ai\", \"magicpath components\", \"magicpath search components\", \"magicpath inspect component\", \"magicpath themes\", \"magicpath design system\", \"magicpath canvas\", \"magicpath share link\".\n\n### Use Cases\n\n**Component lookup (read-only).** Search component names across every accessible project, then inspect a shortlisted component's source, dependencies, and imports without installing anything. `inspect_component` writes no files and needs no package manifest, so it is the safe way to read a component and the only way to read one into a non-React project.\n\n**Project and team inventory (read-only).** List projects across the personal workspace and every team, list the components inside one project (cursor-paginated), list the teams the user belongs to, and list the members of one team.\n\n**Design system lookup (read-only).** List the design systems (themes) available to the user or one team, then fetch a theme's CSS variables, fonts, and styling prompt.\n\n**Canvas and local state (read-only).** Read the components and images currently selected on the MagicPath web canvas, the projects open in the web app, and the MagicPath components already present in the current project directory.\n\n**Sharing (read-only).** Print a shareable URL for a component or project on stdout without opening a browser.\n\n**Wiring and credential verification.** Confirm the `magicpath` manual is registered, the CLI is reachable, and the credential is what the operator expects. Never repair auth state yourself.\n\n### When NOT to Use\n\n**Skip this skill when:**\n- The work is to *generate*, *install*, *add*, *code*, *image*, *create-project*, or *clone* through MagicPath. Those CLI commands are deliberately unregistered; this packet exposes no tool that performs them. Hand the request to the operator or to a workflow that runs the CLI directly outside a tool call.\n- The task is design judgment with no MagicPath surface in it at all (a palette for an unrelated app, a component this library does not hold). Go straight to `sk-design`; there is nothing here to retrieve. When the work *does* touch MagicPath, do not skip this packet to avoid the transport — the two run together, and this packet loads `sk-design` for you.\n- The task is design-reference search over real shipped UI from other apps. That is `mcp-refero`, a sibling transport in this hub; MagicPath is its own component library, not a reference corpus of third-party apps.\n- The task is Figma work (`mcp-figma`), Notion (`mcp-notion`), Obsidian (`mcp-obsidian`), or browser automation and preview (`mcp-chrome-devtools`).\n- The work is generic app coding with no MagicPath input: use `sk-code`.\n- The user asks to change this repo's files, the `.utcp_config.json` manual, or auth state. This transport forbids Write/Edit/Task and never mutates the workspace.\n\n---\n\n## 2. SMART ROUTING\n\n### Primary Detection Signal\n\nRoute on **MagicPath-specific signals only**. Generic \"component\", \"design system\", or \"theme\" phrasing is not a MagicPath signal; component-library work in Figma belongs to `mcp-figma`, and third-party UI reference search belongs to `mcp-refero`.\n\n```bash\n# Signal detection (pseudo)\necho \"$REQUEST\" | grep -qiE 'magicpath' && ROUTE=\"MCP_MAGICPATH\"\necho \"$REQUEST\" | grep -qiE 'magicpath-ai|magicpath (component|project|team|theme|design system|canvas|share)' && ROUTE=\"MCP_MAGICPATH\"\n# generic component/design/theme phrasing WITHOUT these signals -> not this packet\n```\n\n### Phase Detection\n\n```text\nTASK CONTEXT\n    |\n    +- STEP 0: Adopt the design agent persona and load sk-design                            [MANDATORY, UNCONDITIONAL]\n    +- STEP 1: Verify wiring (magicpath manual registered; Code Mode reachable; credential operator-confirmed)\n    +- STEP 2: Score intent -> SESSION | COMPONENTS | PROJECTS | TEAMS | THEMES | LOCAL_CANVAS | SHARING | WIRING_AUTH | TROUBLESHOOT\n    +- Phase 2: Discovery (list_tools / tool_info confirms the magicpath.<tool> callables)   [MANDATORY]\n    +- Phase 3: Read funnel (search/list -> inspect/get detail -> share last); inspect returned values, never try/catch\n    +- Phase 4: Verify (evidence cited by source; unknown fields preserved; no invented capability)\n```\n\n### Resource Domains\n\nThe router discovers markdown resources recursively from `references/` and `assets/`, then applies intent scoring. This skill uses a **flat intent router**: no keyed `references/<key>/` subdirectories. References are the primary loaded resources; the single asset is the registered manual snapshot.\n\n```text\nreferences/tool-surface.md       # the 14-tool surface, args/bounds, the read funnel\nreferences/credential-setup.md   # the credential, the .env wiring, the unauthenticated failure shape\nreferences/mutation-boundary.md  # what is registered (read-only) vs what the CLI can do but is unregistered\nreferences/design-authority.md   # the unconditional sk-design pairing and the persona's reconciled write boundary\nassets/utcp-magicpath-manual.md  # verified manual snapshot (already registered) + the env-var wiring\n```\n\n### Resource Loading Levels\n\n| Level | When to Load | Resources |\n| ----- | ------------ | --------- |\n| ALWAYS | Every invocation, before intent is scored and before the first tool call | `sk-design` (the decide skill) + the design agent persona; `references/design-authority.md` |\n| CONDITIONAL | Component, project, team, theme, canvas, or sharing intent | `references/tool-surface.md` (tool contract + read funnel) |\n| CONDITIONAL | Credential / auth intent | `references/credential-setup.md`, `assets/utcp-magicpath-manual.md` |\n| CONDITIONAL | Mutation-boundary intent (what the agent may and may not reach) | `references/mutation-boundary.md` |\n| FALLBACK | Zero-score routes only | `references/tool-surface.md` suggested (never auto-loaded) |\n\n### Smart Router Pseudocode\n\n> Resilience pattern: see [sk-doc smart-router template](../../sk-doc/sk-create-skill/assets/skill/skill-smart-router.md). Guard paths, discover at runtime, score intents, and fall back when unsure. Because this skill has no keyed resource subdirectories, intent selects from the flat resource inventory below.\n\n```python\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nRESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / \"references\", SKILL_ROOT / \"assets\")\nDEFAULT_RESOURCE = \"references/tool-surface.md\"\nDEFAULT_RESOURCE_SEMANTICS = \"fallback-only\"\nMIN_CONFIDENCE = 1\nAMBIGUITY_DELTA = 1\n\nINTENT_MODEL = {\n    \"SESSION\":       {\"keywords\": [(\"info\", 4), (\"whoami\", 4), (\"signed in\", 3), (\"cli version\", 3), (\"reachable\", 3), (\"set up\", 2)]},\n    \"COMPONENTS\":    {\"keywords\": [(\"component\", 4), (\"search components\", 4), (\"inspect component\", 4), (\"component source\", 3), (\"component dependencies\", 3), (\"list components\", 3), (\"generated name\", 2)]},\n    \"PROJECTS\":      {\"keywords\": [(\"project\", 4), (\"list projects\", 4), (\"active project\", 4), (\"open project\", 3), (\"magicpath project\", 3)]},\n    \"TEAMS\":         {\"keywords\": [(\"team\", 4), (\"teams\", 4), (\"member\", 3), (\"list teams\", 3), (\"team member\", 3), (\"role\", 2)]},\n    \"THEMES\":        {\"keywords\": [(\"theme\", 4), (\"design system\", 4), (\"css variables\", 3), (\"brand\", 3), (\"styling prompt\", 3), (\"fonts\", 2)]},\n    \"LOCAL_CANVAS\":  {\"keywords\": [(\"canvas\", 4), (\"selection\", 4), (\"installed\", 3), (\"list installed\", 3), (\"selected\", 2), (\"open in the web\", 2)]},\n    \"SHARING\":       {\"keywords\": [(\"share\", 4), (\"share link\", 4), (\"shareable url\", 3), (\"link to\", 2)]},\n    \"WIRING_AUTH\":   {\"keywords\": [(\"wiring\", 4), (\"utcp\", 4), (\"manual\", 4), (\"credential\", 4), (\"magicpath token\", 4), (\"authenticate\", 4), (\"login\", 3), (\"register\", 3), \"setup\", 2)]},\n    \"TROUBLESHOOT\":  {\"keywords\": [(\"error\", 4), (\"failed\", 4), (\"not authenticated\", 4), (\"not working\", 4), (\"cli unavailable\", 3), (\"missing argument\", 3), (\"not resolving\", 3)]},\n}\n\nINTENT_SIGNALS = {\n    \"SESSION\":       {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"info\", \"whoami\", \"signed in\", \"cli version\", \"reachable\", \"set up\"]},\n    \"COMPONENTS\":    {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"component\", \"search components\", \"inspect component\", \"component source\", \"component dependencies\", \"list components\", \"generated name\"]},\n    \"PROJECTS\":      {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"project\", \"list projects\", \"active project\", \"open project\", \"magicpath project\"]},\n    \"TEAMS\":         {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"team\", \"teams\", \"member\", \"list teams\", \"team member\", \"role\"]},\n    \"THEMES\":        {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"theme\", \"design system\", \"css variables\", \"brand\", \"styling prompt\", \"fonts\"]},\n    \"LOCAL_CANVAS\":  {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"canvas\", \"selection\", \"installed\", \"list installed\", \"selected\", \"open in the web\"]},\n    \"SHARING\":       {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"share\", \"share link\", \"shareable url\", \"link to\"]},\n    \"WIRING_AUTH\":   {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"wiring\", \"utcp\", \"manual\", \"credential\", \"magicpath token\", \"authenticate\", \"login\", \"register\", \"setup\"]},\n    \"TROUBLESHOOT\":  {\"weight\": 4, \"keywords\": [\"error\", \"failed\", \"not authenticated\", \"not working\", \"cli unavailable\", \"missing argument\", \"not resolving\"]},\n}\n\nRESOURCE_MAP = {\n    \"SESSION\":      [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"COMPONENTS\":   [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"PROJECTS\":     [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"TEAMS\":        [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"THEMES\":       [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"LOCAL_CANVAS\": [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"SHARING\":      [\"references/tool-surface.md\"],\n    \"WIRING_AUTH\":  [\"references/credential-setup.md\", \"assets/utcp-magicpath-manual.md\"],\n    \"TROUBLESHOOT\": [\"references/credential-setup.md\", \"references/mutation-boundary.md\"],\n}\n\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [\n    \"Confirm the layer: session, components, projects, teams, themes, local/canvas, or sharing\",\n    \"Confirm the magicpath manual is registered and discovery (tool_info) confirms the magicpath.<tool> callables\",\n    \"Confirm a credential is present (magicpath-ai login or MAGICPATH_TOKEN); info answers without credentials, most other tools do not\",\n    \"If the evidence will influence a design decision, remember this transport supplies read-only facts, never a taste verdict\",\n]\n\ndef _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:\n    resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()\n    resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)\n    if resolved.suffix.lower() != \".md\":\n        raise ValueError(f\"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}\")\n    return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()\n\ndef discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:\n    docs = []\n    for base in RESOURCE_BASES:\n        if base.exists():\n            docs.extend(p for p in base.rglob(\"*.md\") if p.is_file())\n    return {d.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for d in docs}\n\ndef classify_intents(request: str):\n    text = (request or \"\").lower()\n    scores = {i: 0 for i in INTENT_MODEL}\n    for intent, cfg in INTENT_MODEL.items():\n        for kw, w in cfg[\"keywords\"]:\n            if kw in text:\n                scores[intent] += w\n    ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True)\n    primary, top = ranked[0]\n    if top == 0:\n        return (None, None, scores)\n    secondary, second = ranked[1]\n    if second > 0 and (top - second) <= AMBIGUITY_DELTA:\n        return (primary, secondary, scores)\n    return (primary, None, scores)\n\ndef route_magicpath_resources(request: str):\n    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()\n    primary, secondary, scores = classify_intents(request)\n    intents = [i for i in (primary, secondary) if i]\n    loaded, seen, notices = [], set(), []\n\n    def load_if_available(rel: str) -> bool:\n        guarded = _guard_in_skill(rel)\n        if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:\n            load(guarded); loaded.append(guarded); seen.add(guarded)\n            return True\n        if guarded not in inventory:\n            notices.append(f\"Resource not found in inventory: {guarded}\")\n        return False\n\n    if max(scores.values() or [0]) < MIN_CONFIDENCE:\n        return {\"intents\": intents, \"load_level\": \"UNKNOWN_FALLBACK\", \"needs_disambiguation\": True,\n                \"disambiguation_checklist\": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST,\n                \"suggested_fallback\": DEFAULT_RESOURCE, \"resources\": loaded, \"notices\": notices}\n    for intent in intents:\n        for rel in RESOURCE_MAP.get(intent, []):\n            load_if_available(rel)\n    return {\"intents\": intents, \"intent_scores\": scores, \"resources\": loaded, \"notices\": notices}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### First Step (Always): confirm wiring, then discover\n\nThe `magicpath` manual is **already registered** in this repo's `.utcp_config.json` (`call_template_type: \"cli\"`; the manual command runs `node .skilled/bin/magicpath-utcp-manual.cjs`, which prints the UTCP manual; tool execution runs through `node .skilled/bin/magicpath-utcp-exec.cjs`, which shells out to `magicpath-ai`). Verify it is present (read-only grep), never re-add it, and never edit it. Then discover the live callables through Code Mode before any call:\n\n```javascript\n// Discovery and callable names are the same: magicpath.search_components\nconst all = list_tools();\n// MANDATORY: confirm the exact callable + schema before relying on any name\nconst info = tool_info({ tool_name: \"magicpath.search_components\" });\n```\n\nThe callable form `magicpath.<tool>` follows Code Mode's `{manual}.{tool}` convention applied once, because the tool names have no `magicpath_` prefix of their own. If discovery shows the fourteen tools missing, renamed, or expanded, **fail closed**: report the drift; a changed provider surface requires a reviewed packet update, not an improvised call.\n\n### The 14-tool surface (six themes)\n\nThe expected contract (authoritative baseline from the registered manual; `tool_info` is the final live schema). Full args, bounds, and result shapes: [`references/tool-surface.md`](references/tool-surface.md).\n\n| Theme | Tool | Required args | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Session | `info` | none | Answers without credentials; cheapest reachability check |\n| Session | `whoami` | none | Fails when no credential is present |\n| Components | `search_components` | `query` | `limit` (default 20), `team` optional |\n| Components | `inspect_component` | `generated_name` | Reads source/deps/imports; writes no files |\n| Components | `list_components` | `project_id` | `limit` (default 100), `after` cursor pagination |\n| Projects | `list_projects` | none | `team`, `limit` optional |\n| Projects | `active_project` | none | Projects open in the web app; lighter than `selection` |\n| Projects | `share_link` | `identifier` | Component generated name or numeric project id; prints a URL, opens no browser |\n| Teams | `list_teams` | none | Teams the user belongs to, with role |\n| Teams | `list_members` | `team` | Members of one team (name or id) |\n| Themes | `list_themes` | none | `team` optional |\n| Themes | `get_theme` | `theme` | `team` optional; CSS variables, fonts, styling prompt |\n| Local & canvas | `list_installed` | none | `path` optional; components already in the project directory |\n| Local & canvas | `selection` | none | Canvas selection + open projects; empty when nothing is selected, safe to call speculatively |\n\nHard constraints: every tool is read-only. `limit` is declared as a `string` in the registered schema, not a number. `list_components` paginates by cursor (`after` is the previous page's last id), not by page number. `share_link` takes a component generated name or a numeric project id in one `identifier` argument. `info` is the only tool that answers without a credential; `whoami` and the rest require one. Preserve unknown response fields; the provider surface can grow.\n\n### Calling through Code Mode\n\nCall **synchronously inside the `call_tool_chain` body** (no `await`, no top-level `await`, no returned Promise), per the established convention:\n\n```javascript\ncall_tool_chain({\n  code: `\n    var found = magicpath.search_components({\n      query: \"button\",\n      limit: \"5\"\n    });\n    var list = (found && found.records) ? found.records : [];\n    var first = list.length ? list[0] : null;\n    var detail = first\n      ? magicpath.inspect_component({ generated_name: first.generated_name })\n      : null;\n    return { count: list.length, first: first, detail: detail };\n  `\n});\n```\n\nInspect every returned value. A failing command does not throw; it returns the error text or a JSON error object as an ordinary value, so a caller that wraps the call in `try`/`catch` will miss the failure. Read the value, check for an `error`/`code` field, and only then use the result.\n\n### The read funnel\n\n1. **Start with reachability.** `info` answers without credentials and is the cheapest check that MagicPath is reachable and set up; it also reports the signed-in user, teams, projects, and CLI version.\n2. **Search before detail.** For components, `search_components` first, then `inspect_component` for a shortlisted generated name. For themes, `list_themes` first, then `get_theme`. For project contents, `list_projects` first, then `list_components` for one `project_id`, cursor-paginating with `after`.\n3. **Canvas and local state are safe to call speculatively.** `selection` returns empty collections when nothing is selected or no canvas is open; `active_project` is lighter than `selection` when only the project context is needed; `list_installed` scans the current project directory.\n4. **Share last.** `share_link` prints a URL for a component or project to surface in conversation; it opens no browser.\n\n### Auth, credential, and limits\n\n- **Credential**: `magicpath-ai login` (browser) or the `MAGICPATH_TOKEN` environment variable. Under Code Mode the env var is wired as `magicpath_MAGICPATH_TOKEN` in `.env`, which the manual maps to the CLI's `MAGICPATH_TOKEN`. See [`references/credential-setup.md`](references/credential-setup.md).\n- **Unauthenticated failure**: without a credential, a call returns structured JSON: `{\"error\":\"Not authenticated. Set MAGICPATH_TOKEN or run \\`magicpath-ai login\\`.\",\"code\":\"NOT_AUTHENTICATED\",\"suggestion\":\"...\"}`. `info` is the exception and answers without credentials.\n- **Stale surface warning**: `magicpath-ai info -o json` reports a `cli.commands` list that is **stale and under-reports** the real surface. `magicpath-ai --help` is authoritative. The registered manual is the source of truth for what an agent can call; do not infer the tool set from `info`'s `cli.commands`.\n- **Unknown limits**: no per-second, burst, concurrency, page-size, or retry contract is published for the CLI. Never invent a QPS number or backoff guarantee; on a failure, preserve the CLI's own message.\n- **Local runtime**: Code Mode must run on **Node 24** (isolated-vm has no Node 25 build; `call_tool_chain` SIGSEGVs under Node 25). Local operational evidence, not a server property.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ALWAYS\n\n1. **ALWAYS load `sk-design` and adopt the design agent persona before anything else**, on every invocation, without waiting for the request to look design-shaped. Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory (`.skilled/agents/design.md`, `.claude/agents/design.md`, and the sibling runtime paths) rather than hardcoding one runtime. Loading is not citing: a route named but not read does not satisfy this. A packet already in context is not re-read.\n2. **ALWAYS confirm callables with `tool_info` after registration and before first use.** The `magicpath.<tool>` form is the documented convention; fail closed on any drift from the fourteen documented tools.\n3. **ALWAYS call synchronously inside the `call_tool_chain` body** (no `await`, no top-level `await`, no returned Promise) and use plain JavaScript only; TypeScript type annotations fail to parse.\n4. **ALWAYS inspect the returned value instead of relying on `try`/`catch`.** A failing command returns the error text or a JSON error object as an ordinary value; it does not throw.\n5. **ALWAYS start from the registered manual as the source of truth.** `magicpath-ai info -o json`'s `cli.commands` list is stale and under-reports; `magicpath-ai --help` is authoritative, and the registered manual is what an agent can actually call.\n6. **ALWAYS follow the read funnel**: reachability (`info`) -> search/list -> inspect/get detail -> share last; preserve unknown response fields.\n7. **ALWAYS treat this packet as read-only against this repo** (`mutatesWorkspace: false`). Reads happen against the external MagicPath service; Write, Edit, and Task are forbidden tools for this transport. The design persona is write-capable and this transport is not: on that conflict the transport's narrower surface wins, every time. Adopting the persona imports its judgment contract and its LEAF discipline, never its write authority.\n\n### NEVER\n\n1. **NEVER use Write, Edit, or Task through this packet.** It is a read-only TRANSPORT: it retrieves external facts and changes nothing in this workspace. Hand file changes to the owning workflow skill.\n2. **NEVER edit `.utcp_config.json`'s `magicpath` manual.** It is validated as-is (verify, do not re-add, do not modify), and never add a second MagicPath manual.\n3. **NEVER call, document, or expose the unregistered write surface** (`add`, `code`, `image`, `create-project`, `clone`, or any tool that writes `.tsx` files, installs npm packages, or creates remote projects or component revisions). Those are deliberately out of reach from a tool call; routing to them is a scope violation.\n4. **NEVER accept, print, or cache credentials.** Surface the credential step to the operator and wait; never inspect, clear, or repair auth state.\n5. **NEVER invent rate limits, page sizes, retry contracts, or backoff numbers.** No such contract is published for the CLI; on a failure, relay the CLI's own message.\n6. **NEVER treat search rank, similarity, or a theme's styling prompt as a taste verdict.** This transport supplies read-only facts. The judgment is `sk-design`'s, and it is loaded, so the verdict has an owner rather than being withheld.\n7. **NEVER answer a MagicPath request without the design pairing loaded**, and never treat a retrieved fact, a theme's variables, or a component's source as a finished design answer on its own.\n8. **NEVER infer the tool set from `magicpath-ai info -o json`'s `cli.commands`.** That list is stale and under-reports; the registered manual and `magicpath-ai --help` are authoritative.\n\n### ESCALATE IF\n\n1. **ESCALATE IF authentication is required** (`NOT_AUTHENTICATED`, a login prompt, or a token need). Completing `magicpath-ai login` or wiring `MAGICPATH_TOKEN` is **operator-only**; surface the step and wait.\n2. **ESCALATE IF discovery shows catalog drift**: a documented tool missing or renamed, unexpected new tools, or schemas that contradict [`references/tool-surface.md`](references/tool-surface.md). A provider-surface change requires a reviewed packet update.\n3. **ESCALATE IF the request needs the write surface** (generating, installing, adding, coding, imaging, creating projects, or cloning). This packet cannot perform those; hand the request to the operator or a workflow that runs the CLI outside a tool call.\n4. **ESCALATE IF `call_tool_chain` drops the connection** (`-32000 Connection closed`), which locally indicates a Node 25 runtime; the Node 24 pin is an operator-side fix.\n5. **ESCALATE IF retrieved MagicPath evidence conflicts with an `sk-design` decision** (a theme variable that fails a contrast floor, a component whose interaction contradicts the interaction guidelines), asking which source prevails before either is written into an answer.\n6. **ESCALATE IF a tool returns `CLI_UNAVAILABLE`** (`Could not run magicpath-ai`); the `magicpath-ai` CLI is not on PATH and must be installed by the operator.\n\n---\n\n## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\n**Wiring verification complete when:**\n- The `magicpath` manual was confirmed present in `.utcp_config.json` read-only (no edit, no re-add), and discovery (`list_tools` / `tool_info`) confirmed the `magicpath.<tool>` callables, or the credential/CLI blocker was escalated to the operator.\n\n**Retrieval complete when:**\n- The read funnel was followed (reachability -> search/list -> inspect/get -> share last), required arguments were supplied, cursor pagination used `after` (not page numbers) where applicable, returned values were inspected for `error`/`code`, and unknown fields were preserved.\n\n**Design-affecting use complete when:**\n- `sk-design` was loaded and the design agent persona adopted before the first tool call, the retrieved MagicPath facts were supplied as evidence rather than as a verdict, and any value, interaction, motion, or accessibility judgment in the answer came from `sk-design` and is attributable to it.\n\n**Always:**\n- No workspace file changed, no credential was printed or cached, no auth state was touched, no unregistered write capability was invoked or documented as reachable, no unpublished limit was invented, and every capability claim stayed within the registered manual. The persona's write capability was not exercised through this packet.\n\n---\n\n## 7. INTEGRATION POINTS\n\n### Tool Usage Guidelines\n\n- **Code Mode** (`mcp__code_mode__call_tool_chain`) owns every MagicPath call, including discovery (`list_tools`, `search_tools`, `tool_info`).\n- **Read/Grep/Glob** load references and verify the manual's presence in `.utcp_config.json` read-only.\n- **Bash** has no routine shell role here; the CLI is launched by the transport wrapper, not by this packet. A read-only reachability check (`magicpath-ai info -o json`) may be run to confirm the CLI is on PATH, but the packet never runs the bridge command itself.\n\n### Cross-Workflow Contracts\n\n- **`mcp-code-mode`** is the substrate: manuals, `{manual}.{tool}` naming, prefixed env vars (`magicpath_<NAME>`), discovery, and the synchronous-call discipline all come from it.\n- **`mcp-refero`** is the sibling design-reference transport in this hub; it searches real shipped UI from third-party apps. MagicPath is its own component library, not a reference corpus, and the two surfaces do not overlap.\n- **`sk-design`** is the unconditional pairing and the design authority: it owns values, interaction, motion, and the WCAG review pass. This packet retrieves MagicPath facts and hands them over; it never issues the verdict itself. Note the deliberate difference from the sibling transports — `mcp-figma`, `mcp-refero`, and `mcp-mobbin` pair with `sk-design-md-generator` to MEASURE a live surface into a Style Reference. MagicPath's own themes already carry named CSS variables and fonts, so there is nothing to re-measure; what this surface needs is the DECIDE skill. `sk-design-md-generator` still applies when the reference is an external live site rather than a MagicPath theme.\n- **The design agent** (resolved from the active runtime's agent directory) supplies the operating persona: LEAF-only, no sub-agent dispatch, read before edit, verify before claiming completion, mutate only what the request names. Its write capability is deliberately NOT inherited; this transport's forbidden Write/Edit/Task surface is the narrower contract and it wins.\n- **`sk-code`** owns adapting any resulting decision into application code and verifying it.\n\n### External Tools\n\n- **`magicpath-ai`** (Node CLI, installed version 2.6.1): the external service this transport reaches. Not vendored, not mirrored; must be on PATH.\n- **`magicpath-utcp-exec.cjs`** and **`magicpath-utcp-manual.cjs`** (this repo's `.skilled/bin/`): the wrapper that strips unfilled argument placeholders before shelling out, and the manual emitter. The wrapper emits structured JSON errors (`MISSING_REQUIRED_ARGUMENT`, `CLI_UNAVAILABLE`) so a caller parsing JSON meets one shape whether it succeeded or not.\n\n### Knowledge Base Dependencies\n\n**Required**: `references/design-authority.md` (the unconditional pairing) and `references/tool-surface.md` (tool contract baseline). **Conditional**: `credential-setup.md` + `assets/utcp-magicpath-manual.md` (wiring/auth), `mutation-boundary.md` (read/write boundary).\n\n---\n\n## 8. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Component Choice\n\nChoose the component type before authoring: an agent answers who should do the work, a skill answers how the work should be done, and a command answers how a user should trigger the workflow. Healthy systems often pair all three: the agent provides persona and boundaries, the skill provides detailed domain knowledge, and the command provides the ergonomic entry point.\n\n### Output Package\n\nCreate or update one markdown file in the active runtime agent directory.\n\n| Runtime profile | Agent directory |\n| --- | --- |\n| OpenCode | `.opencode/agents/` |\n| Claude Code | `.claude/agents/` |\n| Copilot/default OpenCode profile | `.opencode/agents/` |\n\nThe output file contract:\n\n1. The filename is kebab-case and ends in `.md`.\n2. The filename stem matches frontmatter `name` exactly.\n3. The stem matches `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`; reject underscores, empty segments, and ambiguous normalization instead of rewriting the name silently.\n4. The file lives in the active runtime directory, not under `sk-doc`.\n5. The body is self-sufficient for the agent's role, boundaries, workflow, limits, and output contract.\n6. Reusable or deep domain guidance stays in skills or references and is linked, not pasted into the agent.\n\n### Canonical Frontmatter\n\nFrontmatter schema is runtime-specific — never emit the same schema for both runtime directories:\n\n| Runtime directory | Canonical schema | Rationale |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `.opencode/agents/` | `permission:` object | OpenCode enforces the `permission:` object; it ignores a standalone `tools:` key. |\n| `.claude/agents/` | `tools:` allow-list | Claude Code enforces only `tools:` (a comma-separated allow-list); it silently ignores `permission:`. Omitting `tools:` makes the agent inherit the parent session's full, unrestricted tool set. |\n\nDecision rule:\n\n```text\nAuthoring for .skilled/agents/? -> emit `permission:` (never bare `tools:`)\nAuthoring for .claude/agents/?   -> emit `tools:` (never `permission:`)\n```\n\n**OpenCode (`.opencode/agents/`) frontmatter:**\n\n```yaml\n---\nname: agent-name\ndescription: One-line purpose statement with scope and boundary\nmode: subagent\ntemperature: 0.1\npermission:\n  read: allow\n  write: allow\n  edit: allow\n  bash: allow\n  grep: allow\n  glob: allow\n  webfetch: deny\n  chrome_devtools: deny\n  task: deny\n  list: allow\n  patch: deny\n  external_directory: deny\n---\n```\n\n**Claude Code (`.claude/agents/`) frontmatter:**\n\n```yaml\n---\nname: agent-name\ndescription: One-line purpose statement with scope and boundary\ntools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob\n---\n```\n\nMap the `permission:` allow-set to the `tools:` list when authoring the same role for both runtimes: include only the tools with `allow` (or `ask`) and drop the ones with `deny`. `mode` and `temperature` are OpenCode-only fields with no Claude Code equivalent — omit both from `.claude/agents/` frontmatter.\n\nFrontmatter rules:\n\n1. `name` must match the filename stem.\n2. `description` is one line describing role and scope.\n3. `mode` and `temperature` are OpenCode-only fields; set `mode` to match runtime invocation (commonly `subagent` for specialists) and `temperature` to reflect determinism needs (commonly `0.1`) — `.claude/agents/` frontmatter omits both.\n4. Under `.skilled/agents/`, `permission` values must be explicit, least-authority, justified by the role, and use only `allow`, `deny`, or `ask`.\n5. Under `.claude/agents/`, `tools:` is the runtime-specific canonical schema — a comma-separated least-authority allow-list; never emit `permission:` there, and never leave `tools:` absent or empty (an absent `tools:` inherits the parent session's full tool set).\n6. Set `task: allow` (or include `Task` in `tools:`) only for agents whose explicit authority is orchestration.\n\n### Required Body Shape\n\nStart from `assets/agent-template.md` when creating a new agent. At minimum, a production-ready agent includes:\n\n1. H1 and short purpose statement.\n2. Hard boundary section that states nesting, delegation, and write limits.\n3. Core workflow section that describes how the agent acts.\n4. Capability scan section that identifies relevant skills, tools, commands, or companion agents.\n5. Output verification section that defines checks required before claiming completion.\n6. Anti-patterns section that names failure modes.\n7. Related resources section with real supporting paths.\n\nBoundary variants: LEAF write-capable agents deny nested sub-agent dispatch and restrict mutation to explicitly scoped paths; LEAF read-only agents deny nested dispatch and all file mutation; orchestrators may dispatch only when orchestration is their explicit authority and `task` permission allows it; command-driven or machine-validated agents may need input/scope gates before workflow steps.\n\n### Sanctioned Section-Vocabulary Dialects\n\nThe skeleton above is the default; start new agents from it. One alternate section vocabulary is also sanctioned — the **deep-loop leaf-iteration agents** (`@deep-review` / `@deep-research`, in both runtime directories). A per-iteration loop worker reads more clearly under lane-named headings, so these agents carry the same responsibilities under a different vocabulary: `ROUTING SCAN`, a lane `CONTRACT` (`REVIEW CONTRACT`, or `ITERATION PROTOCOL` for the leaner research variant), `STATE MANAGEMENT` (`+ WRITE SAFETY` where the agent mutates), a lane `ADVERSARIAL CHECK` (`ADVERSARIAL SELF-CHECK`), and `RULES`.\n\nThis is a documented shape, not drift. `--type agent` requires only `## 1. CORE WORKFLOW`, and the dialect still carries every hard-block boundary, capability, verification, and anti-pattern responsibility from \"Required Body Shape\" above. Reach for it only when authoring another member of the deep-loop iteration family — do not invent a fresh dialect for a one-off agent. The concrete section order and its two sub-variants are in `assets/agent-template.md` §9.\n\n### Ordered Creation Workflow\n\nFollow this order for new agents and material rewrites:\n\n1. Link supporting skills, commands, references, and companion agents rather than copying their full guidance.\n12. Deliver only after validation passes or after reporting the exact blocker.\n\nWhen the user invokes `/create:agent`, treat the command as the preferred entry point, but keep this same creation contract as the source of truth for the generated file.\n\n### Validation Gate\n\nBefore delivery, verify document quality and runtime correctness.\n\n```bash\npython3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py .skilled/agents/agent-name.md --type agent\npython3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/extract_structure.py .skilled/agents/agent-name.md\npython3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/check_authored_name_kebab.py .skilled/agents/agent-name.md\n```\n\nUse `.claude/agents/agent-name.md` instead when Claude Code is the active runtime.\n\nRequired checks: frontmatter parses, filename stem matches `name`, the shared authored-name checker passes, required sections are present, runtime directory is correct, permissions match authority, `task` matches orchestration intent, related resources exist, and unresolved markdown links are reported.\n\n---\n\n## 4.
