Four gotchas that must be honored at routing time:\n\n- **Non-interactive requires `-p` (print) mode** — `claude -p \"prompt\" --output-format text 2>&1`. `--output-format` defaults to `text`; use `json` (adds role/content/cost metadata) or `stream-json` only when a pipeline needs it. Capture stderr with `2>&1`.\n- **`--permission-mode plan` is read-only** — use it for review/analysis/exploration (no file writes). `bypassPermissions` auto-approves all writes and **requires explicit user approval**; the default mode already allows writes.\n- **No `--search` flag** — Claude Code has no live web browsing. Route web research to cli-opencode.\n- **Check `$CLAUDECODE` before dispatch** — a set value means the caller is already inside Claude Code; do not dispatch the CLI, route to a native subagent instead.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. Verify Claude Code CLI is installed before first invocation (`command -v claude`); check `$CLAUDECODE` for nesting.\n2. Use `--permission-mode plan` for review/analysis/exploration (no file writes); `--output-format text` unless JSON is specifically needed.\n3. Validate output before applying — correctness, completeness, alignment, syntax checks if code generated.\n4. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) to catch errors and warnings.\n5. Specify `--model` explicitly: default `claude-sonnet-5-5` unless task needs Opus (deep reasoning). Use Haiku only when explicitly requested or after adoption.\n6. Route to the appropriate `--agent <name>` when the task matches a specialization (see Section 3 routing table).\n7. **Pass the spec folder to the delegated agent** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. Apply the CLEAR 5-question check from the canonical card via the local delegating card.\n9. **Code Standards Loading (surface-aware contract)** — When dispatching for code review or code generation, instruct the dispatched session to: (1) load `sk-code`; (2) let `sk-code` emit a surface tag matching the detected stack from markers and target files; (3) load the selected surface resources and run its verification commands; (4) load `sk-code`'s code-review mode only for formal findings-first review output. Fallback: if the surface cannot be determined confidently, ask for the runtime surface and verification command set. NEVER hardcode obsolete sibling code skills in dispatch prompts.\n10. **Design Standards Loading (measured-reference contract)** — When dispatching for design or UI work, instruct the dispatched session to: (1) load `sk-design-md-generator`; (2) extract a measured Style Reference DESIGN.md (named color tokens, type scale, components, Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind) from the live source before building UI; (3) build against those measured tokens and run the extraction's validate step to confirm hex/section fidelity. Fallback: if there is no live source to measure, ask for the reference URL or the exact tokens to build against. NEVER treat `mcp-figma` or `sk-design-md-generator` as a taste, visual-direction, or critique authority — the extraction measures real CSS, it does not judge design.\n11. **Pass the design reference manifest to the dispatched session** — when dispatching design or UI work, inline a `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST v1` block in the prompt (the child cannot resolve skill paths, so the manifest travels in the payload, not by reference): `styleReferenceExtracted` true, the live `source` that was measured, the measured design tokens / type scale / components the child must build against, `loadedFiles`, and `proofDemandBack`. If the manifest cannot be assembled — no Style Reference extracted, or no live source to measure — ASK before launching the child rather than starting a silent design dispatch. The child returns the demanded proof; the parent reconciles it on the return path.\n12. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped)** — Default: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-opencode, cli-claude-code). Wait for the dispatched agent's work to return, verify outputs exist, then SIGKILL the dispatcher process + any orphan children (`pkill -9 -f \"claude -p\"` for this skill, plus `gtimeout` / `positional_scoring_fallback:app` cleanup). Only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped. **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole multi-iteration session at start — iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration operator confirmation prompt. **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently — but still SIGKILL each as its work returns.\n13. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env AND state the exemption in the prompt.** The variable makes the waiver true; it does not make it observable. The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable, so a child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question and writes nothing, at exit code zero. Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt. when sessions may be launched through the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`). A dispatched `claude -p` run is an orchestrated sub-session, not a new top-level session, so it must SHARE the parent's worktree rather than allocate its own. The wrapper checks `AI_SESSION_CHILD` (plus a `git --git-common-dir` structural backstop) and exec's in place when set. Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 claude -p ...`. Harmless when the wrapper is not in use. See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → \"Worktree session isolation\". Prepend `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0` next to it so a dispatched child never inherits an enforced spec-gate from the parent shell (belt-and-suspenders alongside the wrapper's own neutralization and the core's complete `AI_SESSION_CHILD` classify/enforce no-op): `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 claude -p ...`.\n\n14. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).** Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}` — never a bare task. Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9 (`.claude/agents/<name>.md`, `.skilled/agents/<name>.md`, etc. — never hardcode one runtime), and map each subtask to the RIGHT agent (`code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, docs→`markdown`), not one default. **Claude Code has a native persona flag:** pass `claude -p --agent <name>` — the CLI resolves `.claude/agents/<name>.md` on the print path, which satisfies the rule. On a bare `claude -p` that omits `--agent`, **INLINE** the persona block into the payload using the same in-payload pattern as the `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 11) — the child cannot resolve agent paths by reference. A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant, silently dropping the agent's tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract. Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` \"Persona Injection\"; native precedent: `orchestrate.md` \"Agent Loading Protocol\". Rare exceptions (native surface used, focused summary for a small-context model, pure-mechanical command) are declared at the dispatch site.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. Use `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` without explicit user approval (auto-approves all writes/tool calls).\n2. Trust output blindly for security-sensitive code (review for XSS, injection, hardcoded secrets, eval), or send sensitive data (API keys, passwords, credentials) in prompts — Claude Code transmits to Anthropic's API.\n3. Hammer the API with rapid sequential calls — respect rate limits; use `--max-budget-usd` for cost control.\n4. Use Claude Code for tasks where context is already loaded — direct action by the calling AI is faster.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. Claude Code CLI is not installed and user has not acknowledged (provide `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`).\n2. Rate limits or budget caps are persistently hit (suggest increasing `--max-budget-usd` or checking quota).\n3. Output conflicts with existing code patterns (present both perspectives; user decides).\n4. Task requires `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` (describe risks; get explicit user approval).\n\n### Memory Handback Protocol\n\nWhen the calling AI needs to preserve session context from a Claude Code CLI delegation, run the canonical procedure (extract `MEMORY_HANDBACK` section → build structured JSON → scrub secrets → invoke `generate-context.js` via `--stdin`/`--json`/temp-file). The continuity writer is the last step; nothing is handed to an index. Full procedure and caveats: [`system-spec-kit/references/cli/memory-handback.md`](../../system-spec-kit/references/cli/memory-handback.md).\n\nClaude-Code-specific Memory Epilogue template: see [assets/prompt-templates.md](./assets/prompt-templates.md) §11.\n\nExample invocation:\n```bash\nprintf '%s' \"$JSON_PAYLOAD\" | node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js --stdin [spec-folder]\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. Enumerating\n# them keeps the routed inventory legible to a reader and to the connectivity\n# scan, which is what catches a new reference the keyed load silently picks up\n# but no documented route names.\nRESOURCE_MAP = {\n    \"MCP_PROMOTION\": [\n        \"references/shared/README.md\", \"references/shared/case-studies.md\",\n        \"references/shared/pitfalls.md\", \"references/shared/worked-example.md\",\n        \"assets/shared/benchmark-report-template.md\", \"assets/shared/source-template.md\",\n    ],\n    \"BEHAVIOR_BENCHMARK\": [\n        \"references/shared/README.md\", \"references/shared/case-studies.md\",\n        \"references/shared/pitfalls.md\", \"references/shared/worked-example.md\",\n        \"references/behavior-benchmark/behavior-benchmark-guide.md\",\n        \"assets/behavior-benchmark/behavior-benchmark-index-template.md\",\n        \"assets/behavior-benchmark/behavior-benchmark-scenario-template.md\",\n        \"assets/behavior-benchmark/behavior-benchmark-baseline-template.md\",\n    ],\n}\n\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [\n    \"Confirm the benchmark family (MCP promotion, behavior)\",\n    \"Confirm what is authored here vs lane-owned, then the storage location and run label\",\n]\n\ndef route_benchmark_request(request):\n    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()\n    loaded, seen = [], set()\n    routing_key = get_routing_key(request, FAMILIES)\n\n    if routing_key == \"unknown\":                                 # Tier 1\n        load_if_available(DEFAULT_RESOURCE, inventory, loaded, seen)\n        return {\"load_level\": \"UNKNOWN_FALLBACK\",\n                \"disambiguation_checklist\": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST, \"resources\": loaded}\n\n    disk_key = FAMILY_DISK_KEY.get(routing_key, routing_key.replace(\"_\", \"-\"))\n    keyed = sorted(p for p in inventory if p.startswith(\n        (f\"references/{disk_key}/\", f\"assets/{disk_key}/\", \"references/shared/\")))\n    if not keyed:                                                # Tier 2\n        load_if_available(DEFAULT_RESOURCE, inventory, loaded, seen)\n        return {\"routing_key\": routing_key,\n                \"notice\": f\"'{routing_key}' guide only; fixtures/scoring stay lane-owned\", \"resources\": loaded}\n\n    for path in keyed:                                           # Tier 3\n        load_if_available(path, inventory, loaded, seen)\n    return {\"routing_key\": routing_key, \"resources\": loaded}\n```\n\n### Family Boundary\n\nThis packet owns authoring, not measurement contracts: rubrics, renderers, scorers, and evaluator/verdict contracts stay lane-local. REQUIRED PACKAGE SHAPE\n\nUse this shape in the consuming skill:\n\n```text\nmcp-server/benchmarks/\n├── README.md\n└── benchmark-<YYYY-MM-DD>/\n    ├── benchmark-report.md\n    ├── results.csv\n    ├── per-probe.jsonl\n    ├── runtime-measurements.md\n    └── source.md\n```\n\nRequired and optional files:\n\n| File | Required | Purpose |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `README.md` | Yes | Index of all benchmark folders in this skill |\n| `benchmark-<YYYY-MM-DD>/` | One per promoted run | Dated subfolder using the benchmark execution date |\n| `benchmark-report.md` | Yes | Ten-section operator-facing report |\n| `results.csv` | Yes | Primary aggregate metrics, one row per candidate |\n| `per-probe.jsonl` | When applicable | Per-query or per-probe rows |\n| `runtime-measurements.md` | Optional | RAM, GPU, latency, cold-load, or runtime profile worth promoting |\n| `source.md` | Yes | Pointer back to the authoritative spec packet |\n\n`source.md` is navigation, not an audit duplicate. Include the packet path, purpose, question-to-file and evidence maps, follow-on and rename/renumber notes, and last-updated date.\n\nUse `assets/shared/benchmark-report-template.md` for `benchmark-report.md` and `assets/shared/source-template.md` for `source.md`.\n\nFor case studies, the worked example, and pitfalls, use `references/shared/README.md`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. HOW IT WORKS: AUTHORING WORKFLOW\n\nComplete these steps in order after the spec packet ships.\n\nBefore naming a folder, run label, fixture, or report, validate its resolved path or slug. Do not pass machine keys such as `behavior_benchmark` as filesystem names.\n\n```bash\npython3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/check_authored_name_kebab.py <artifact-path-or-slug>\n```\n\n1. **Confirm the promotion gate.** Read `decision-record.md`, `implementation-summary.md`, and benchmark evidence. Require an accepted decision, stable headline and fixture, replay commands, and a defensible winner or explicit provisional status.\n2. **Classify the task.** Decide whether this is a true promotion, a re-run update, or a retirement update.\n3. **Confirm the target skill.** Verify the consuming skill has `mcp-server/` and an appropriate measurable MCP surface.\n4. **Create or update the index.** Ensure `mcp-server/benchmarks/README.md` can hold date, folder link, winner/status, headline metric, and source path.\n5. **Choose the dated folder.** Name it `benchmark-YYYY-MM-DD/` using the benchmark execution date, not the document authoring date.\n6. **Copy source artifacts.** Copy aggregate CSV, applicable `per-probe.jsonl`, then only decision-relevant runtime or risk sidecars.\n7. **Write `benchmark-report.md`.** Use the ten-section template. Generalize the headline; separate a non-obvious load-bearing insight from the winner.\n8. **Write `source.md`.** Use the template with packet path, navigation and evidence maps, follow-on notes, and last-updated date.\n9. **Update the README index row.** Add or update the row with date, folder link, winner or status, headline metric, and source packet path.\n10. **Validate markdown.** Run `python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py --type readme <file>` on `benchmark-report.md` and `benchmarks/README.md`; fix blockers.\n\n### Authoring Order Rules\n\n- Stabilize the headline and section structure before polishing prose.\n- Write the load-bearing insight and caveats before recommendations.\n- Validate before adding or finalizing the README index row.\n- Keep raw evidence out of the report; curate and link through `source.md`.\n\n### Artifact Sources\n\n| Skill-local file | Source in spec packet |\n| --- | --- |\n| `benchmark-report.md` | Curated rewrite of `benchmark-results.md` or equivalent benchmark summary |\n| `results.csv` | Copy of `evidence/*comparison*.csv` or topic equivalent |\n| `per-probe.jsonl` | Copy of `evidence/*.jsonl` per-probe output when applicable |\n| `runtime-measurements.md` | Curated rewrite or copy of runtime evidence when the profile affects the decision |\n| `source.md` | Authored fresh; points back to the spec packet |\n\n---\n\n## 5. REPORT CONTRACT\n\nKeep this fixed ten-section `benchmark-report.md` structure; never merge, reorder, or omit:\n\n1. **HEADLINE / OVERVIEW**: one-line winner or status plus key metric.\n2. **AGGREGATE RESULTS**: one row per candidate, headline metrics, and verdict.\n3. **METHODOLOGY**: fixture, sample size, pipeline, environment, and replay context.\n4. **PER-CANDIDATE PROFILES**: RAM, disk, dim, release, strengths, and weaknesses.\n5. **PROCESS NOTES**: what was tried, what failed, and why.\n6. **FINDINGS**: unique wins, universal floor and ceiling, mismatch analysis, and load-bearing insight.\n7. **CAVEATS**: single-run signal, fixture limits, stack-level confounds, schema migration cost, reranker/runtime confounds.\n8. **RECOMMENDATIONS**: Tier 1 apply now, Tier 2 validate first, Tier 3 future.\n9. **REPRODUCIBILITY**: exact replay commands plus expected wall-clock.\n10. **CROSS-LINKS**: sibling MCP benchmarks, authoritative spec packet, follow-on packets.\n\nFor an empty section, retain its header and write: `Not applicable to this bench. Reason: ...`\n\n### Report Style\n\n- Match sk-doc reference quality and frontmatter.\n- Use H2 numbered headers with ALL CAPS section names.\n- Use tables for data and fenced code blocks for verbatim commands.\n- Keep slugs and anchors stable across revisions.\n- Do not paste the full spec packet decision trail into the report.\n- Do not compare numeric results across different MCP stacks as if equivalent.\n\n### Headline Pattern\n\nUse this shape near the top of the report:\n\n```markdown\n# <topic> bake-off: <date>\n\n> Headline: `<winner>` + <pipeline-config> is the production default for `<MCP-stack>`.\n> <primary-metric> <numeric-result>, <secondary-metric> <numeric-result>. Closes packet <packet-id>.\n```\n\nIf the load-bearing insight differs from the winner, state it in Sections 1 and 6.\n\n---\n\n## 6. DATE AND NAMING CONVENTION\n\n### Folder Names\n\nOne grammar governs every benchmark family. A run folder is named:\n\n```text\n<YYYY-MM-DD>--<subject>--<variant>/\n```\n\n- Fields are separated by a double hyphen. Words inside a field use a single hyphen.\n- Lowercase ASCII only. No underscores, no dots, no capitals.\n- The date is the **execution** date, not the authoring or publication date. Publication date belongs in\n  the report body, where a reader can see both.\n- `<subject>` names the corpus the run measured: `manual-testing-playbook`, `mcp-retrieval`,\n  `model-eval`, `behavior`.\n- `<variant>` names what most distinguishes the run. For a **feature-scoped** run — one validating a\n  single feature or scenario group rather than comparing executors — name the feature (e.g. `goal-hook`),\n  not the model; the model/executor is recorded inside the report (`model`/`providerModel` fields, the\n  byline, the command shape), so the folder stays legible when the same feature is later re-validated on\n  another model. For an **executor-scoped** run — one whose point is which model and effort produced it —\n  name the executor identity as `<runtime>-<model>-<effort>`; use `model-comparison` when it compares\n  several, or a short topic slug when no model applies.\n- Model versions flatten their dots: `glm-5.2` becomes `glm-5-2`, `kimi-2.7` becomes `kimi-2-7`. A dot\n  is rejected by the run-label validator, so this is a hard requirement rather than a style preference.\n- Two runs of the same subject and variant on one day disambiguate with a trailing topic field.\n\nExamples:\n\n```text\n2026-07-29--manual-testing-playbook--goal-hook/                 # feature-scoped: names the feature, model recorded inside\n2026-07-26--manual-testing-playbook--cursor-grok-4-5-high-fast/ # executor-scoped: names the model+effort that ran it\n2026-07-26--manual-testing-playbook--model-comparison/\n2026-05-18--mcp-retrieval--bge-confirmation/\n```\n\n**One exception: `baseline/`.** The frozen comparison anchor keeps its name. It is not a run, it is the\nbefore-snapshot every run is measured against, and the archiver refuses it as a run label for exactly\nthat reason. Dating it would make it look like one run among many.\n\nAuthored scenario contracts are not run folders. Behavior families keep their\n`<PREFIX>-NNN-<slug>.md` scenario identifiers, which name a scenario rather than a directory. Any run\nthose families produce follows the grammar above.\n\n### In-Document Dates\n\nUse readable long-form dates in prose, such as `May 18, 2026`.\n\n### Re-Runs\n\nFor a re-run confirming the same headline, update the existing report with `Re-run YYYY-MM-DD`; do not create a folder.\n\n### Retirement\n\nKeep retired benchmarks. Mark `README.md` as `RETIRED` with date; add report date, reason, and replacement if any.\n\n### Renamed or Renumbered Spec Packets\n\nDo not rename the dated folder. Update `source.md`, report and README cross-links, then record old slug, new slug, and date in `source.md`.\n\n---\n\n## 7. RULES: AUTHORITY AND GATES\n\n### Authority Hierarchy\n\nWhen documents disagree:\n\n1. Source spec packet `decision-record.md` and `implementation-summary.md` are authoritative.\n2. Skill-local `benchmark-report.md` is the curated operator-facing summary.\n3. Copied CSV and JSONL files preserve the source packet evidence.\n4. `source.md` is navigation, not a duplicate audit trail.\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. Read the source packet decision record, implementation summary, and benchmark evidence before writing.\n2. Use the benchmark execution date for `benchmark-<YYYY-MM-DD>/`.\n3. Keep `source.md` lean and navigational.\n4. Include caveats for single-run signal, fixture limits, stack mismatch, schema migration cost, and reranker/runtime confounds when present.\n5. Preserve retired benchmark folders.\n6. Validate authored markdown before delivery.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. Never promote an in-flight benchmark as a final skill-local record.\n2. Never compare numeric results across different MCP stacks as if equivalent.\n3. Never paste the full spec packet audit trail into `benchmark-report.md`.\n4. Never create a new dated folder for a confirming re-run.\n5. Never name the folder by authoring date, source packet slug, or candidate name.\n6. Never leave template placeholders in shipped benchmark files.\n7. Never add packet-local `graph-metadata.json`.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. The source packet has no accepted decision record or stable benchmark headline.\n2. The target skill lacks `mcp-server/` or an appropriate measurable MCP surface.\n3. Source artifacts are missing, non-replayable, or internally contradictory.\n4. The benchmark spans multiple stacks and the user wants a single comparative verdict.\n5. Validation fails on required markdown structure after local fixes.\n\n---\n\n## 8. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\n- The consuming skill has a dated `mcp-server/benchmarks/benchmark-<YYYY-MM-DD>/` folder.\n- `benchmark-report.md` uses the ten-section structure and includes winner or status, aggregate table, methodology, candidate profiles, findings, caveats, recommendations, replay commands, and cross-links.\n- `source.md` points to the authoritative spec packet and maps reader questions to source files.\n- Raw artifacts are copied or intentionally omitted with a documented reason.\n- The benchmarks README index links the new folder and source packet.\n- Shared sk-doc validation passes for authored markdown, or any remaining issue is escalated with exact command output.\n\n---\n\n## 9. WHEN TO USE\n\n### Activation Triggers\n\nUse the `sk-code-review` mode (of the sk-code family) when:\n- A user asks for code review, PR review, quality gate, or merge readiness.\n- A workflow dispatches `@review` for pre-commit or gate validation.\n- A user requests security/correctness risk analysis before merge.\n- A user wants severity-ranked findings with file:line evidence.\n\n### Keyword Triggers\n\n`review`, `code review`, `pr review`, `audit`, `security review`, `quality gate`, `request changes`, `findings`, `blocking issues`, `merge readiness`\n\n### Use Cases\n\n1. \"surface_evidence\": surface_evidence,\n        \"precedence\": precedence,\n        \"resources\": loaded,\n    }\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Phase 1: Scope and Baseline\n\n1. Inspect the review target (`git diff`, staged diff, file list, or commit range).\n2. Load baseline standards from the `sk-code-review` mode (of the sk-code family).\n3. Load `sk-code` surface standards evidence when a surface is detected.\n4. Read the connected code: the callers of each changed function, the functions each changed function calls, the tests that cover it, and the README or docs that describe it. Anything you could not read goes on the `Not checked:` line.\n\n### Phase 2: Surface Alignment\n\n1. Load standards from `sk-code` for the detected surface only.\n2. Apply precedence matrix:\n   - Baseline security/correctness minimums always apply.\n   - Surface style/process/verification conventions win on conflicts.\n3. If precedence cannot be resolved deterministically, escalate before scoring.\n\n### Phase 3: Findings-First Analysis\n\n1. Analyze for security and correctness first.\n2. Analyze quality/performance, test adequacy, contract safety, and architecture concerns.\n3. Analyze KISS/DRY and SOLID violations (SRP/OCP/LSP/ISP/DIP) with evidence.\n4. Analyze removal opportunities with safe-now vs deferred classification.\n5. Produce findings ordered by severity (`P0`, `P1`, `P2`), numbered once across all three groups so the first `P1` finding continues after the last `P0` finding. A finding with no case is not reported.\n6. For every actionable finding, classify fix scope as `instance-only`, `class-of-bug`, `cross-consumer`, `algorithmic`, `matrix/evidence`, or `test-isolation`. If unknown, default to class/cross-consumer until a producer/consumer inventory proves instance-only.\n\n#### Numeric Severity Calibration\n\nUse numeric calibration only as reviewer context, never as the gate. A finding may include an optional advisory `riskScore` to communicate relative risk, and reviewers may adjust that score by `+/-2` for local context such as exploitability, blast radius, user impact, confidence, or proven containment. The blocking decision still comes only from the `P0`/`P1`/`P2` severity contract. Do not introduce `score>=4` or any other numeric threshold as a blocker.\n\n#### Instance-Only Opt-Out\n\nA finding may use the narrow fix path only when all are true:\n\n- It is not P0/P1 security, path, auth/authz, sandboxing, env precedence, schema, persistence, or public-response behavior.\n- `rg` proves no same-class producer or consumer.\n- Verification is local and cheap: one focused test, one doc row, or one static audit command.\n- The fix response includes the exact command evidence for the opt-out.\n\nOtherwise, run the full fix completeness checklist.\n\n### Phase 4: Output and Next Action\n\nRequired output contract:\n\n```markdown\n## Code Review Summary\n\n**Files reviewed**: X files, Y lines changed\n**Overall assessment**: [APPROVED / REQUESTED_CHANGES / COMMENTED]\n**Baseline used**: [sk-code (`sk-code-review`)]\n**Surface evidence used**: [OPENCODE | OBSIDIAN | WEBFLOW | UNKNOWN]\n\n## Findings\n\n### P0 - Critical\n1. [path:line] Title\n   - Case: [the input or situation that produces the wrong result. A finding with no case is not reported]\n   - Risk (for a performance finding, name the workload it assumes, such as row count, request rate or payload size)\n   - User impact: what users or callers bear if this fix is deferred\n   - Finding class: [instance-only | class-of-bug | cross-consumer | algorithmic | matrix/evidence | test-isolation]\n   - Scope proof: [grep/test evidence proving class coverage or instance-only status]\n   - affectedSurfaceHints: [optional string array of short producer/consumer surface names; recommended for actionable findings, required for cross-consumer findings]\n   - riskScore: [optional advisory number only; never gating]\n   - Recommended fix\n\n### P1 - High\n2. [path:line] Title\n   ...\n\n## Removal/Iteration Plan\n\n## Next Steps\n\nNot checked: [one line naming what mattered but could not be checked, and why, or \"nothing material\"]\n```\n\nAfter reporting findings, request explicit next action before any implementation follow-up.\n\n### Final-line exact-string contract (MANDATORY)\n\nEvery review MUST end with exactly one of the following plain-text lines as the **absolute final line** of the output (no trailing whitespace, no variation):\n\n```\nReview status: APPROVED\n```\n\n```\nReview status: REQUESTED_CHANGES\n```\n\n```\nReview status: COMMENTED\n```\n\nDirectly above the status line, separated from it by one blank line, every full review carries one `Not checked:` line naming what mattered but could not be checked and why, or `Not checked: nothing material`. An optional `AGENT_IO_RESULT` block, when requested, goes above the `Not checked:` line and never below the status line. The M-1 and M-2 skip outputs (§9) are the status line alone and carry no `Not checked:` line.\n\n**Example output bottom:**\n\n```\n...\n## Next Steps\n1. Fix the null-deref at src/foo.ts:42\n2. Add input validation for the `/api/bar` endpoint\n\nNot checked: behavior under concurrent writes to /api/bar; no test database was available\n\nReview status: REQUESTED_CHANGES\n```\n\nDownstream automation parses this final line via exact string match — do not vary the format, add trailing punctuation, or wrap in Markdown formatting. The sole exception is the documented M-1 / M-2 skip output (§9): those lines begin with the exact `Review status: COMMENTED` and append a parenthetical reason, so a leading-verdict (grep / `startsWith`) parse still yields `COMMENTED`. A normal review must still end with one of the three exact lines above.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n- Keep findings first; summaries follow findings.\n- Enforce baseline security/correctness minimums regardless of surface.\n- Include file:line evidence for actionable findings.\n- State assumptions when evidence is incomplete.\n- Identify `sk-code` surface evidence used for standards alignment.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n- Override surface-specific conventions with generic baseline style preferences.\n- Approve code with unaddressed P0 security/correctness defects.\n- Produce vague findings without concrete evidence.\n- Mix unrelated cleanup into targeted fix recommendations.\n- Do not implement fixes during review. Report findings only; implementation is a separate follow-up step.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n- Surface detection is ambiguous and affects standards or verification commands.\n- Baseline and surface guidance conflict in a non-deterministic way.\n- Large diff size prevents reliable severity assignment without narrowed scope.\n- Requested remediation exceeds review scope and becomes architecture redesign.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Execute scenarios in Claude Code or OpenCode sessions for behavioral verification.\n\n---\n\n## 9. PR-STATE EFFICIENCY GATES\n\n### 9.1 M-1: PR-State Content-Hash Dedup\n\nPrevents redundant re-reviews when a PR has not changed since the last review.\n\n**Signature computation:**\n```\ndiff_content_hash = sha256(git diff <base-ref>...HEAD)\nsignature         = sha256(commit_subject + \"\\u001f\" + diff_content_hash)\n```\nWhere `commit_subject` is the first line of `git log <base-ref>...HEAD --format=%s` (latest commit subject).\n\n**Cache storage:**\n- Path: `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/sk-code-review/<repo-ref>.jsonl`, in the reviewing user's cache directory. The gate never writes into the reviewed repository. Its one side effect is this file, and deleting it resets the gate.\n- `<repo-ref>` is computed as `sha256(git remote get-url origin).slice(0, 12)`\n- Each line is a JSON object: `{\"signature\": \"<sha256-hex>\", \"timestamp\": \"<ISO-8601>\", \"prev_sha\": \"<commit-sha>\"}`\n- Retention: keep last **100 entries** per repo-ref, prune older entries on write\n\n**Skip behavior:**\nWhen the current signature matches a prior cache entry, the review emits:\n```\nReview status: COMMENTED (no changes since last review at <prev_sha>)\n```\nNo full review analysis runs. Automation may treat `COMMENTED` as a pass (no new findings).\n\n**Cache write:** After each full review completes, write the current signature + timestamp + HEAD SHA to the cache file.\n\n### 9.2 M-2: Opt-In Minimum Evidence Gate\n\nSkips full review for trivially small diffs to save compute, with a conservative taxonomy that **never skips** high-risk changes.\n\n**Enable gate:**\n```bash\nexport SK_CODE_REVIEW_MIN_CHANGED_LINES=50  # >0 enables; default 0 = disabled\n```\n\n**Changed-line counting command:**\n```bash\ngit diff --numstat <base-ref>...HEAD | awk '{added+=$1; removed+=$2} END {print added+removed}'\n```\n\n**Conservative skip taxonomy — NEVER skip when diff touches:**\n\n| Risk Class | Path/File Patterns | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| Security / Authentication / Authorization | `auth*`, `*-auth-*`, `*permission*`, `*credential*`, `*token*`, `*secret*`, `*oauth*`, `*sso*`, `*login*`, `*session*` | Compromised auth defeats everything |\n| Config files | `*.config.*`, `*config*.json`, `*config*.yaml`, `*config*.toml`, `*.env*`, `*.ini`, `*.cfg` | One-line config change can break production |\n| Persistence | `*.sql`, `*migration*`, `*schema*`, `*db*.ts`, `*repository*`, paths under `/db/` or `/migrations/` | Schema changes risk data loss |\n| Dependency manifests | `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `pyproject.toml`, `poetry.lock`, `requirements.txt`, `*.lock`, `Gemfile`, `Gemfile.lock` | Transitive dependency changes are high-risk |\n| Sandboxing / Subprocess | `*sandbox*`, `*subprocess*`, `*exec*`, `*spawn*`, `*eval*` | Arbitrary code execution boundaries |\n| Public-facing responses | `*.handler.ts`, `*-api*`, `*-route*`, `*-controller*`, paths under `/handlers/`, `/routes/`, `/api/` | User-visible behavior changes |\n\n**Skip behavior:**\nWhen `SK_CODE_REVIEW_MIN_CHANGED_LINES > 0`, total changed lines < threshold, AND no sensitive paths are touched:\n```\nReview status: COMMENTED (skipped: diff below evidence threshold of N lines, no sensitive paths touched)\n```\nIf sensitive paths ARE touched, the full review runs regardless of line count.\n\n**Gate is ALWAYS opt-in.** Without `SK_CODE_REVIEW_MIN_CHANGED_LINES` set, M-2 has zero effect — all diffs receive full reviews.\n\n### 9.3 SK_CODE_REVIEW_DEPTH (opt-in depth alias)\n\n`SK_CODE_REVIEW_DEPTH=lite|full|ultra` is an optional environment variable the **reviewing agent honors** (resolved env > config > default) — exactly like the §9.2 `SK_CODE_REVIEW_MIN_CHANGED_LINES` gate. Both are skill guidance the reviewer reads and applies in-loop, not a separate compiled dispatcher; this alias only NAMES and PERSISTS an already-existing routing behavior, adds no new tier, and relaxes no floor:\n\n- `full` (default / unset): the normal ALWAYS + CONDITIONAL + ON_DEMAND routing.\n- `ultra`: bias intent selection toward the existing `ON_DEMAND` reference set (the deep-dive tier) for the session, so a reviewer does not have to repeat \"comprehensive / full review\" each time.\n- `lite`: maps to the existing M-2 conservative skip (§9.2) — it NEVER lowers the ALWAYS tier, the baseline security/correctness minimums, or the P0/P1/P2 contract. It cannot skip a review on a sensitive path (auth/config/persistence/deps/sandbox/public-response), exactly as M-2 already enforces.\n\nThe depth alias is advisory routing only; it must never be read as permission to relax a floor.\n\n---\n\nRelated skills: `sk-doc` for skill authoring and packaging standards, `sk-code` for surface-aware standards, and `system-spec-kit` for packet-governed review workflows.\n"

When present, the prefix determines the operating mode directly. When absent, the router falls back to **keyword-weighted intent scoring** against the request text, selecting the top-scoring intent (or top-2 when scores are close). A zero-score fallback defaults to `TEXT_ENHANCE` with a disambiguation checklist.\n\n### Phase Detection\n\n```text\nUSER REQUEST\n    |\n    +- STEP 0: Detect mode ($command prefix or keyword signals)\n    +- STEP 1: Score intents (top-2 when ambiguity is small)\n    +- Phase 1: Framework Selection (7 frameworks evaluated)\n    +- Phase 2: DEPTH Processing (3-10 rounds based on mode)\n    +- Phase 3: Scoring & Validation (CLEAR)\n    +- Phase 4: Output Delivery (formatted prompt)\n```\n\n### Resource Domains\n\nThis skill uses a **simple intent router**, not a keyed resource-subdirectory router. Its real resources are flat markdown files under `references/` and `assets/`; there are no `references/<key>/` or `assets/<key>/` runtime-key directories to select. The router therefore discovers markdown resources recursively from `references/` and `assets/`, then applies command-prefix and intent scoring against the discovered inventory.\n\n- `references/` for DEPTH methodology, framework definitions, and CLEAR scoring.\n- `assets/` for format-specific deep-dives (Markdown, JSON, YAML).\n\n```text\nreferences/depth-framework.md            - DEPTH methodology, RICCE integration\nreferences/patterns-evaluation.md        - 7 frameworks, CLEAR scoring\nassets/format-guide-markdown.md          - Markdown format deep-dive\nassets/format-guide-json.md              - JSON format deep-dive\nassets/format-guide-yaml.md              - YAML format deep-dive\n```\n\n### Resource Loading Levels\n\n| Level       | When to Load             | Resources                                                                  |\n| ----------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| ALWAYS      | Every skill invocation   | SKILL.md (this file)                                                       |\n| CONDITIONAL | If intent signals match  | references/depth-framework.md, references/patterns-evaluation.md           |\n| CONDITIONAL | If design-generation signals match | references/patterns-evaluation.md                                 |\n| ON_DEMAND   | Only on explicit request | assets/format-guide-markdown.md, assets/format-guide-json.md, assets/format-guide-yaml.md |\n\nA run that loads `references/patterns-evaluation.md` reads three of its sections, not the whole file:\n\n1. `## 2. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Enhancement Pipeline\n\nEvery prompt enhancement follows this pipeline:\n\n```\nSTEP 1: Mode Detection\n       ├─ Command prefix check ($text, $improve, $refine, $short, etc.)\n       ├─ Keyword signal analysis (>=80% confidence = auto-route)\n       └─ Ambiguous? Ask ONE comprehensive question\n       ↓\nSTEP 2: Framework Selection\n       ├─ Evaluate 7 frameworks against request characteristics\n       ├─ Score: complexity, urgency, audience, creativity, precision\n       └─ Select primary framework + alternative\n       ↓\nSTEP 3: DEPTH Processing (5-10 rounds)\n       ├─ Discover: 5 perspectives, assumption audit, RICCE Role & Context\n       ├─ Engineer: Framework application, RICCE Constraints & Instructions\n       ├─ Prototype: Template build, RICCE validation\n       ├─ Test: Scoring (CLEAR), quality gates\n       └─ Harmonize: Final polish, RICCE completeness\n       ↓\nSTEP 4: Scoring & Delivery\n       ├─ Apply context-appropriate scoring system\n       ├─ Verify threshold met (CLEAR 40+/50)\n       └─ Deliver enhanced prompt with transparency report\n```\n\nSee the Smart Routing pseudocode (Section 2) for the complete routing logic.\n\n### Operating Modes\n\n| Mode | Command | DEPTH Rounds | Scoring | Use Case |\n|------|---------|-------------|---------|----------|\n| Interactive | (default) | 10 | CLEAR | Guided enhancement |\n| Text | `$text` | 10 | CLEAR | Standard text prompt |\n| Short | `$short` | 3 | CLEAR | Quick refinement |\n| Improve | `$improve` | 10 | CLEAR | Standard enhancement |\n| Refine | `$refine` | 10 | CLEAR | Maximum optimization |\n| JSON | `$json` | 10 | CLEAR | API-ready format |\n| YAML | `$yaml` | 10 | CLEAR | Config format |\n| Raw | `$raw` | 0 | None | Skip DEPTH |\n\n### Framework Selection Matrix\n\n| Complexity | Primary Need | Framework |\n|-----------|-------------|-----------|\n| 1-3 | Speed | RACE |\n| 1-4 | Clarity | RCAF |\n| 3-6 | Audience | COSTAR |\n| 4-6 | Instructions | CIDI |\n| 5-7 | Creativity | CRISPE |\n| 6-8 | Precision | TIDD-EC |\n| 7-10 | Comprehensive | CRAFT |\nSee [patterns-evaluation.md](./references/patterns-evaluation.md) for complete framework details.\nSee [depth-framework.md](./references/depth-framework.md) for the DEPTH methodology.\n\n### Scoring Systems\n\n**CLEAR** (50-point scale): Correctness (10) + Logic (10) + Expression (15) + Arrangement (10) + Reusability (5). Threshold: 40+.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. **ALWAYS ask ONE comprehensive question** before processing, in an interactive run whose request leaves the goal open\n   - Gather: What needs enhancement? Use case/goal? RULES\n\n### ALWAYS\n\n- Resolve the packet through `mode-registry.json`. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Execution Ownership\n\nThis packet owns provider-specific routing, the availability probe, and prompt construction. For research and review lineages, the shared deep-loop runtime owns process construction and execution: `cli-hermes` is an `ExecutorKind`, and `buildHermesLineageCommand` in `fanout-run.cjs` emits the dispatch shape below. That runner accepts only the `research` and `review` loop types, so a single build or doc dispatch runs the same shape directly, in the child environment that ALWAYS rule 11 sets. Do not add a packet-local wrapper, spawn path, or command builder.\n\n**One provider is reachable from the fan-out: `llmgateway`** (DevPass, the operator's LLM Gateway plan), declared as a Hermes custom provider block of that exact name in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` with `key_env: LLMGATEWAY_API_KEY`. That block is an operator step; the repo cannot carry it. Setup and the credential contract are in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md).\n\n**Closed roster, non-roster models are FORBIDDEN.** Dispatch ONLY the seven the gateway serves for Hermes: `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `glm-5.3-flash`, `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-sol`, `minimax-m3`, `mimo-v2.6-pro` and `qwen3.8-max`. These are the bare literals of Pi's roster. `mimo-v2.6-pro-ultraspeed` answers HTTP 400 \"not supported\" on this route and is on neither roster. Every id except the two GPT-6 ids was probed live; `gpt-6-luna` and `gpt-6-sol` replaced the probed GPT-5.6 Luna and Sol on 2026-09-23, when the gateway's `/v1/models` catalog listed both. `gpt-6-luna` passed its first live probe the same day; `gpt-6-sol`'s is still pending. The deep-loop fan-out hard-rejects any other id (`isHermesModelAllowed` over `HERMES_SUPPORTED_MODELS`), and even a direct `hermes chat --model` invocation must not use an unlisted id. To add a model, amend the roster (spec packet plus `HERMES_SUPPORTED_MODELS`) first.\n\n### The Dispatch Shape\n\n~~~bash\nhermes chat -Q --oneshot --query-file <prompt.md> --provider llmgateway --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \\\n  --reasoning max --ignore-rules --source tool --max-turns 200 --run-budget 840 \\\n  -t terminal,file,skills,todo,web --yolo --in <repo-root> </dev/null\n~~~\n\n- `chat -Q --oneshot` is the auditable headless form: response on stdout, `session_id: <id>` on stderr, hard exit codes (0 success, 1 `result.failed`, 130 interrupt). Never `hermes -z`: it drops the session id and auto-approves everything.\n- `--query-file` reads the prompt verbatim; `-` reads stdin, which is how the fan-out builder passes it. Argv `-q` is for short prompts only.\n- `--yolo` is required for writes; a read-only dispatch omits it and narrows `-t` to `file,todo`.\n- `--run-budget` stays one margin under the caller's timeout because budget expiry has no distinct exit code; the in-agent wrap-up must win the race.\n- `--in <repo-root>` pins the working directory on a manual dispatch; the fan-out omits it because the runner already spawns in the repo root.\n\n### Dispatch Lifecycle\n\n1. Verify the binary with `command -v hermes` and the provider with `hermes config get providers.llmgateway.base_url`.\n2. Classify the request as write, read-only review, or generation; pick the toolset accordingly.\n3. Compose the prompt using [prompt-quality-card.md](./assets/prompt-quality-card.md), persona inlined.\n4. Pass a research or review lineage to the shared deep-loop runtime; run a single build or doc dispatch with the dispatch shape above.\n5. Capture stdout (the response) and stderr (`session_id:`, `Error:`) separately.\n6. Validate the output, changed files, and required tests before handback.\n\n### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas\n\n- **No provider configured means exit 1 with the reason on stdout, not stderr.** Observed live 2026-09-14 before the provider block existed: `No inference provider configured. Run 'hermes model' ...` printed to stdout, stderr empty, no `session_id:` line. Read the exit code, then stdout.\n- **`--yolo` lifts only the dangerous-action gate.** Observed live 2026-09-14: without `--yolo` a headless chat wrote an ordinary scratch file (exit 0), while `rm -rf <scratch dir>` came back `BLOCKED: Command flagged as dangerous ... single-query mode (-q) runs without a user present to approve it`; with `--yolo` the same command ran. Ordinary writes and commands need no flag; a read-only dispatch is read-only because of its `-t` list, not because `--yolo` is absent.\n- **`--ignore-rules` is not optional.** Hermes injects `SOUL.md`, memories, session search, and the CWD `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `.cursorrules` unless told not to.\n- **`--worktree` writes inside the repo.** It runs `git worktree add`, which the fan-out containment guard reverts as an out-of-lineage write.\n- **The stock toolset roster enables `delegation` and `memory`.** A leaf must pass an explicit `-t` list without them.\n- **Hermes gates writes into any `.hermes/` directory.** Its file tools treat a write whose immediate parent is `.hermes` as a protected-instruction write needing approval (source-read: `tools/file_tools_write_guards.py`); author repo `.hermes/` files from outside Hermes.\n- **`hermes pause` does not stop a CLI dispatch.** It scopes to cron, kanban and gateway turns. The runner's kill is the emergency stop.\n- **Project skills load only after `hermes skills trust`**, and the repo mirrors every skill as a generated markdown-only copy under `.hermes/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (`sync-skills-hermes.cjs`), never as a symlink: Hermes's static scanner walks a linked directory in full (ten minutes for the tree, every hub quarantined; one linked skill quarantined on its references and scripts, observed 2026-09-14). Preload with `-s <name>`; `hermes skills list` shows the loadable copies as `local` rows, and a copy the scanner quarantines is absent from both the listing and `-s`. See [hermes-tools.md](./references/hermes-tools.md).\n- **`-Q` stdout can carry the model's reasoning before the answer** (observed with `deepseek-v4.1-flash` through the gateway). Read the tail for the answer; the fan-out validates artifacts, not stdout.\n- **A research iteration is slow.** One live fan-out iteration with `deepseek-v4.1-flash` at `max` made thirteen gateway calls on a 65k to 90k token context and finished at 1042 seconds; the `--run-budget` wrap-up notice at 537 seconds was advisory and the runner's ceiling (twice `iterations × timeoutSeconds`) is what binds. Give a `cli-hermes` research lineage `timeoutSeconds` 900 or more.\n- **`--run-budget` does not bound a stalled provider stream.** Hermes's stale-stream watchdog fires at 600 seconds and retries; the caller's own timeout is the real bound.\n- **MCP servers are reached only when named in `-t`.** `-t file,todo` hides a configured server; `-t file,todo,code_mode` reaches it.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. Run `command -v hermes` before every dispatch, and `hermes config get providers.llmgateway.base_url` for a configured provider.\n2. Delegate research and review lineages to the shared deep-loop runtime. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch runs the dispatch shape in §3 directly.\n3. Validate Hermes-generated changes with the repository's code and test gates.\n8. Keep the current runtime as conductor and Hermes as delegated executor.\n9. Treat source-read claims as confirmed only when the contract pin records the live run.\n10. Compose every dispatch as `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}`, never a bare task. Resolve the persona from the CALLING runtime's agent directory (AGENTS.md §9), because Hermes carries no agent directory of its own, and INLINE it: Hermes profiles are whole-home islands and `delegate_task` children cannot read agent files, so no native persona surface exists. Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` \"Persona Injection\".\n11. Never dispatch when `command -v hermes` fails.\n2. Never dispatch Hermes from inside Hermes, from inside a fan-out lineage, or when `cli-hermes` already appears in the dispatch stack.\n3. Never build a second Hermes adapter inside this packet.\n4. Never use `hermes -z` for an auditable dispatch, and never pass `--worktree`.\n5. Never run `hermes import-agent`: it copies repo state into the user home and bypasses the trust and quarantine path.\n6. Never claim a repo file configures Hermes hooks, MCP servers, or the provider; those are operator steps.\n7. Never pass an off-roster model id or a provider-prefixed id.\n8. Never pass secrets or provider keys in prompts.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. Hermes is missing from PATH or `hermes config get providers.llmgateway.base_url` prints nothing.\n2. The task needs a model outside the closed roster.\n3. The task depends on a source-read behavior the contract pin has not yet confirmed.\n4. The task requests `hermes skills trust`, `hermes mcp add`, or a config change; those are the operator's.\n5. A Hermes plugin or hook would need `--accept-hooks`.\n\n---\n\n## 5. It fills per-kind templates that are checked copies of the system-spec-kit goal template and keeps runtime goal state with its existing owners.\n\n---\n\n## 1. WHEN TO USE\n\n### Activation Triggers\n\nUse this packet to:\n\n- Author or revise a top-level goal or phase-parent goal.\n- Author or revise a nested phase-child goal.\n- Add `goal.md` to an existing packet that has no goal.\n- Add a binding row and matching child goal when someone adds a phase.\n- Cut an over-budget parent goal without dropping a completion criterion.\n- Print a parent goal's chat slice for the operator to set or resend.\n- Handle a request that enters through `/create:goal`.\n\nKeyword triggers: `create packet goal`, `author goal.md`, `revise packet goal`, `phase parent goal`, `nested phase child goal`, `add a goal file`, `goal chat slice`, `/create:goal`.\n\n### When NOT to Use\n\n- The target packet does not exist. Use system-spec-kit to create it first.\n- The packet's phase structure is not established. Use system-spec-kit to plan the phases first.\n- The request is to set, bind, inject or resend a session objective. Redirect it to the goal hooks or the host's native goal command.\n- The request changes runtime goal behavior or system-spec-kit template tooling. Those owners remain outside this packet.\n\nThis packet authors files only. Its goal-file work does not change session state.\n\n---\n\n## 2. SMART ROUTING\n\nRun these four decisions before writing:\n\n1. **File content or session state?** A request to author or revise a packet's `goal.md` is file work. A request to set, bind, inject or resend a session objective belongs to the goal hooks or the host's native goal command. Redirect session-state requests without editing a packet goal.\n2. **Does the packet exist? What role does it have?** Confirm the target directory exists. A nested phase child has a parent directory containing `spec.md`. A packet with direct phase-child directories is the phase parent. Otherwise, treat it as a top-level packet. If the packet is missing, route packet creation to system-spec-kit first.\n3. **Does `goal.md` exist?** Revise an existing goal. Add one to an existing packet that has none. Do not treat a missing packet as a goal-file request.\n4. **Does a child change alter a parent decision or criterion?** If it does, amend the parent first. Then print the updated parent chat slice for the operator to resend. Do not let a child goal override a parent decision.\n\nDiscover reference and asset documents at call time. Keep loads inside this packet. For top-level, phase-parent and nested-child authoring, retrofit, phase-add or parent amendment work, load [`references/parent-and-nested-goals.md`](references/parent-and-nested-goals.md) and follow the matching workflow. For every goal authoring or revision request, also load [`references/authoring-standards.md`](references/authoring-standards.md), [`assets/goal-exemplars.md`](assets/goal-exemplars.md) and the template for the goal's kind before drafting. For a budget measurement or chat-slice handoff, load [`references/budget-and-handoff.md`](references/budget-and-handoff.md). Fall back to the workflow reference when no specific resource applies:\n\n```python\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nRESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / \"references\", SKILL_ROOT / \"assets\")\nDEFAULT_RESOURCE = \"references/parent-and-nested-goals.md\"\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK = {\n    \"load_level\": \"UNKNOWN_FALLBACK\",\n    \"needs_disambiguation\": True,\n    \"resources\": [],\n}\n\ndef discover_markdown_resources():\n    documents = []\n    for base in RESOURCE_BASES:\n        if base.exists():\n            documents.extend(path for path in base.rglob(\"*.md\") if path.is_file())\n    return {path.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for path in documents}\n\ndef _guard_in_skill(relative_path):\n    resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()\n    resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)\n    if resolved.suffix.lower() != \".md\":\n        raise ValueError(\"Only packet-local markdown resources are routable\")\n    return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()\n\ndef route_references(selected):\n    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()\n    loaded = []\n    seen = set()\n    for relative_path in selected:\n        guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)\n        if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:\n            load(guarded)\n            loaded.append(guarded)\n            seen.add(guarded)\n    if not loaded:\n        fallback = _guard_in_skill(DEFAULT_RESOURCE)\n        if fallback in inventory:\n            load(fallback)\n            loaded.append(fallback)\n        return {**UNKNOWN_FALLBACK, \"resources\": loaded}\n    return {\"resources\": loaded}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\n\n1. Read the target packet's source specification and acceptance criteria. For a phase parent, read its phase map and inspect every direct phase-child directory on disk.\n2. Apply the four routing decisions above. For top-level, phase-parent, nested-child, retrofit, phase-add and amendment work, load and follow [`references/parent-and-nested-goals.md`](references/parent-and-nested-goals.md). Identify which goal files to add or revise and whether a child change requires a parent amendment first.\n3. Start each goal from the template for its kind: [`goal-top-level-template.md`](assets/goal-top-level-template.md), [`goal-phase-parent-template.md`](assets/goal-phase-parent-template.md) or [`goal-phase-child-template.md`](assets/goal-phase-child-template.md). Each is a checked copy of system-spec-kit's [`goal.md.tmpl`](../../system-spec-kit/templates/addons/goal.md.tmpl) at that kind's level. Copy the block between its template markers into `goal.md`. When [`create.sh`](../../system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh) `--with-goal` has already scaffolded a child's `goal.md`, keep that file and fill it with the child template's guidance. Child scaffolding alone does not create its parent goal.\n4. Before filling the template, load [`authoring-standards.md`](references/authoring-standards.md) and [`goal-exemplars.md`](assets/goal-exemplars.md). Fill it with packet-specific content and apply both resources. Use three to seven self-contained completion criteria that can be checked without opening another file. Leave no template placeholders. Copy the criteria verbatim into the objective text required by the goal contract.\n5. For a phase parent, make the binding table match the filesystem. Add one row for each direct phase-child directory, with that child's goal document as the target. Keep the table only in the phase-parent goal.\n6. Keep the durable slice at or below 4,000 characters wherever the cap applies. Load [`references/budget-and-handoff.md`](references/budget-and-handoff.md): section 2 says which goals carry the cap and how to read the packet report, and section 3 is the cut order for a goal that runs over. Never remove a criterion or make one uncheckable.\n7. Before handing off any authored or revised goal, run `node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-goal/scripts/check-goal.cjs <packet>` from the repository root and resolve each finding. A finding left open for any reason, an operator brief included, stops the run: report it, print no chat slice and end with `STATUS=FAIL`. To see which criteria may break rules 4 and 5 below, run the advisory lint `node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-goal/scripts/lint-goal-criteria.cjs <packet>`. It always exits 0 and never blocks the handoff.\n8. Only after the checker passes, and after authoring or amending a parent goal, load [`references/budget-and-handoff.md`](references/budget-and-handoff.md) for the projection distinction and runtime matrix, then print its chat slice with `node .skilled/hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs packet <packet> --workspace <root>`. The `chat_slice` is for the operator to set or resend. It is not a session bind.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. Run the four pre-write decisions before changing a goal file.\n2. Derive each goal from the existing packet's source documents, not from a guessed or remembered summary.\n3. Start every goal from the asset template for its kind. Keep each template's fixed text identical to `goal.md.tmpl`. The parity test fails when they drift.\n4. Use three to seven self-contained criteria.\n5. Make each criterion checkable without opening another file.\n6. Remove every template placeholder.\n7. Preserve every criterion when cutting an over-budget parent.\n8. Compare each binding row with the direct phase-child directories on disk.\n9. Print the updated parent chat slice for the operator when parent goal content changes.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. Never change an asset template's fixed text or structure on its own. Change `goal.md.tmpl` through system-spec-kit, then carry its new fixed text into all three templates.\n2. Never modify system-spec-kit's template tooling or shared validator from this packet.\n3. Never bind a packet to a session, set or resend a session objective, inject runtime state or track whether an operator has set the goal.\n4. Never put a binding table in a top-level goal or a phase-child goal.\n5. Never omit a phase child from the parent's binding table or drop a completion criterion to meet the budget.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. The source documents disagree about a decision or criterion. They also must describe the same phase structure. Report any conflict instead of choosing a truth silently.\n2. A phase child is missing the source documents needed to author its goal.\n3. The parent phase map and child directories do not agree.\n4. A child change requires a parent decision or criterion amendment, but the request would leave the parent untouched.\n5. A parent cannot meet the durable budget without losing a criterion or making one unclear. Do not cut the criterion count. Ask whether the packet scope should be split.\n6. The request requires session-goal state or a change to a system-spec-kit-owned contract.\n\n---\n\n## 5. REFERENCES\n\n- [`references/parent-and-nested-goals.md`](references/parent-and-nested-goals.md) defines the top-level, phase-parent, child, retrofit, phase-add and amendment workflows.\n- [`authoring-standards.md`](references/authoring-standards.md) gives the reader checks for goal content.\n- [`references/budget-and-handoff.md`](references/budget-and-handoff.md) explains the durable budget, the one full cut order, what a parent goal sent in chat contains and the runtime handoff.\n- [`goal-exemplars.md`](assets/goal-exemplars.md) records cited pass and failure examples.\n- [`goal-top-level-template.md`](assets/goal-top-level-template.md), [`goal-phase-parent-template.md`](assets/goal-phase-parent-template.md) and [`goal-phase-child-template.md`](assets/goal-phase-child-template.md) are the blanks each goal kind is filled from.\n- [`goal.md.tmpl`](../../system-spec-kit/templates/addons/goal.md.tmpl) is the system-spec-kit source the three templates copy.\n- [`scripts/README.md`](scripts/README.md) describes the checker, the advisory criteria lint, its scorer and their tests.\n- [`goal-set-string-playbook.md`](../../system-spec-kit/references/workflows/goal-set-string-playbook.md) documents the objective set string a runtime binds and when a changed goal is resent. The budget, the cut order and what a goal sent in chat contains are in `budget-and-handoff.md`.\n- [`goal hooks README`](../../../hooks/goal/README.md) documents the runtime session-state boundary.\n- [`goal.cjs`](../../../hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs) prints a packet's file-derived slices without binding a session.\n\n---\n\n## 6. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\n- Every authored goal starts from the template for its kind, and all three templates match `goal.md.tmpl`.\n- Every phase-parent binding row corresponds to a direct phase-child directory on disk. No child is omitted.\n- Each goal has three to seven self-contained criteria. The family is named here on purpose, without a version or an effort tier, so this line does not go stale when the family ships a point release; the runner resolves the current id. A drift test keeps the two in the same family.\n\n```bash\ncodex exec \\\n  --model gpt-5.5 \\\n  -c model_reasoning_effort=\"medium\" \\\n  -c service_tier=\"fast\" \\\n  -c approval_policy=never \\\n  --sandbox workspace-write \\\n  \"<prompt>\" </dev/null\n```\n\nThe trailing `</dev/null` is not optional in a non-interactive dispatch; Rule 6 below explains what a backgrounded codex does to an inherited stdin.\n\n**User override** (honor explicit user phrasing verbatim):\n\n| User says | Resolve to |\n|-----------|------------|\n| (nothing specified) | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort=\"medium\" -c service_tier=\"fast\"` |\n| \"Use gpt 5.5 high fast\" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort=\"high\" -c service_tier=\"fast\"` |\n| \"Use gpt 5.5 low\" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort=\"low\" -c service_tier=\"fast\"` (fast stays unless user drops it) |\n| \"Use gpt 5.5 xhigh\" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort=\"xhigh\" -c service_tier=\"fast\"` |\n| \"Use gpt 6 luna max\" | `--model gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort=\"max\" -c service_tier=\"fast\"` |\n| \"Use gpt 5.6 terra high\" | `--model gpt-5.6-terra -c model_reasoning_effort=\"high\" -c service_tier=\"fast\"` |\n| \"Use gpt 6 sol ultra\" | `--model gpt-6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=\"ultra\" -c service_tier=\"fast\"` |\n\nHonor whichever dimensions the user names. Model stays on `gpt-5.5` and service tier stays on `fast` unless the user explicitly names a different model or tier; keep the reasoning effort within the chosen model's ceiling (see Model Selection below and the roster in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md)).\n\n### Model Selection\n\n`gpt-5.5` at `medium` on the `fast` service tier (`-c service_tier=\"fast\"`) is the skill default for cross-AI delegation. Alternates: `gpt-6-luna` (≤ `max`), `gpt-5.6-terra` / `gpt-6-sol` (≤ `ultra`) — full roster, per-model effort ceilings, and the 8-level effort ladder in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md). Set effort with `-c model_reasoning_effort=\"<level>\"` (there is **no `--reasoning-effort` flag**).\n\n**Selection Strategy**: default `gpt-5.5 medium`; raise to `high` / `xhigh` for architecture, security, and complex planning; escalate the model when the task wants reasoning past `xhigh`; drop to `low` / `minimal` for trivial lookups. Per-task rationale table: [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) §5.\n\n### Codex Agent Delegation\n\nThe calling AI is the conductor; Codex profiles in `$CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml` shape HOW Codex processes the task (sandbox, reasoning). Route with `-p <name>` when the task matches a specialization. Full roster and invocation patterns: [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md).\n\n| Task Type | Profile |\n|-----------|---------|\n| Code review / security audit | `review` |\n| Architecture exploration | `context` |\n| Technical research | `research` (+ top-level `--search`) |\n| Documentation generation | `write` |\n| Fresh-perspective debugging | `debug` |\n| Multi-strategy planning | `ai-council` |\n\nGit diff review uses the built-in subcommand (no `-p`): `codex exec review \"...\" --commit HEAD`. Profiles may override `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode`, `approval_policy`. The `.codex/agents/*.toml` files define personas for the interactive multi-agent TUI, NOT the `-p` flag.\n\n### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas\n\nThe full flag glossary, sandbox modes, unique capabilities (`/review`, `--search`, `codex mcp`, session resume/fork, `--image`, `codex cloud`), essential command examples, and troubleshooting table are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md). Five gotchas that break a dispatch, or make a child misreport its result, and must be honored at routing time:\n\n- **`codex exec` defaults to `--sandbox read-only`** — file-modification tasks silently no-op (the agent plans changes but cannot write them). Pass `--sandbox workspace-write`; for headless no-prompt execution use top-level `-a never` before `exec` or `-c approval_policy=never`.\n- **`--search` is a top-level flag, not an `exec` flag** — enable live web search as `codex --search exec …` (it precedes the subcommand). On codex ≥ 0.144 `codex exec --search` hard-fails with `unexpected argument '--search'` (older 0.125 builds accepted it), so treat any `exec … --search` example as stale. Without it, `codex exec` has no web access and answers from training data only — every dispatch needing live data (latest versions, repo facts, advisories) MUST use `codex --search exec …`.\n- **Always pass `-c service_tier=\"fast\"` explicitly** — this routes through the fast tier instead of whatever the caller's `~/.codex/config.toml` defaults to. Explicit means reproducible regardless of who runs it.\n- **No `--reasoning-effort`, `--reasoning`, or `--quiet` flag exists** — set effort with `-c model_reasoning_effort=\"<level>\"`; capture the last message with `-o file.txt`; capture stderr with `2>&1`.\n- **`--sandbox workspace-write` blocks local IPC sockets, so a child cannot run checks that start `tsx`** — spec-kit's `npm --prefix runtime/cli run check` fails there with `listen EPERM`, also with `TMPDIR` pointed elsewhere (observed 2026-09-24 on codex-cli 0.156.1), and passes outside the sandbox. Tell the child which checks to leave to you, run them in the orchestrating session after it returns, and read that EPERM as a sandbox limit, not a code failure.\n\n---\n\n## 4. RULES\n\n### ✅ ALWAYS\n\n1. Verify Codex CLI is installed before first invocation (`command -v codex`).\n2. Delegate research and review lineages to `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` with executor kind `cli-codex`. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5. Never build a second adapter in this packet.\n3. Use `--sandbox read-only` for review/analysis/research; `--sandbox workspace-write` for code generation/file modification — `codex exec` defaults to `read-only`, so omitting it causes silent no-op on edit tasks. For unattended approval, put top-level `-a never` before `exec` or set `-c approval_policy=never`.\n4. Validate Codex-generated code (XSS, injection, eval, syntax checks via `node --check`, `tsc --noEmit`, etc.) before applying.\n5. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) so rate-limit messages and errors surface.\n6. **Redirect codex stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch** — not only inside a `while read` loop, which is the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped. Pattern: `codex exec \"$PROMPT\" > \"$LOG\" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Without `</dev/null`, the backgrounded codex process inherits the loop's stdin (the file after `done < input.jsonl`) and silently consumes the remaining lines — the loop exits after 3-6 iterations with no error. See `references/integration-patterns.md#background-execution` → \"Silent Stdin Consumption\".\n7. **Specify model + effort + service tier explicitly** — never rely on caller environment. Default: `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort=\"medium\" -c service_tier=\"fast\"`. Honor user overrides verbatim. Use `high`/`xhigh` for reasoning-heavy tasks (architecture, security, deep planning).\n8. Route to the appropriate `-p <profile>` when the task matches a specialization (see Section 3 routing table); use `codex exec review` (built-in subcommand) for git diff reviews.\n9. **Pass the spec folder to the delegated agent** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating — the delegated agent cannot answer Gate 3 in non-interactive mode.\n10. **Prompt construction & model-craft (cli-* family precedence).** Compose every dispatch prompt via the 2-tier rule canonical in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`:\n   1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.\n   2. **Deep path (escalation).** Dispatch `@prompt-improver` via the Task tool (never load full `sk-prompt` inline) when any canonical **Tier 2** trigger applies — the trigger list lives in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` under \"Tier 2 — Deep path\"; do not re-enumerate it here.\n11. **Never inject user-level voice/personalization content into AI-orchestrated Codex delegations.** Codex CLI reads user-level voice from `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (the human's global settings, loaded automatically). When an AI delegates via `codex exec`, the calling AI's own voice rules govern the response — do NOT read `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` and paste into delegation prompts. Keep delegations focused on task/model/sandbox/effort/(spec-folder pre-approval). If the user asks how to make Codex sound more like Claude in *their own* sessions, point to `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` — not any repo asset.\n12. **Code Standards Loading (surface-aware contract)** — When dispatching for code review or code generation, instruct the dispatched session to: (1) load `sk-code`; (2) let `sk-code` emit a surface tag matching the detected stack from markers and target files; (3) load the selected surface resources and run its verification commands; (4) add `code-review` only for formal findings-first review output. Fallback: if the surface cannot be determined confidently, ask for the runtime surface and verification command set. NEVER hardcode obsolete sibling code skills in dispatch prompts.\n13. **Design Standards Loading (measured-reference contract)** — When dispatching for design or UI work, instruct the dispatched session to: (1) load `sk-design-md-generator`; (2) extract a measured Style Reference DESIGN.md (named color tokens, type scale, components, Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind) from the live source before building UI; (3) build against those measured tokens and run the extraction's validate step to confirm hex/section fidelity. Fallback: if there is no live source to measure, ask for the reference URL or the exact tokens to build against. NEVER treat `mcp-figma` or `sk-design-md-generator` as a taste, visual-direction, or critique authority — the extraction measures real CSS, it does not judge design.\n14. **Pass the design reference manifest to the dispatched session** — when dispatching design or UI work, inline a `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST v1` block in the prompt (the child cannot resolve skill paths, so the manifest travels in the payload, not by reference): `styleReferenceExtracted` true, the live `source` that was measured, the measured design tokens / type scale / components the child must build against, `loadedFiles`, and `proofDemandBack`. If the manifest cannot be assembled — no Style Reference extracted, or no live source to measure — ASK before launching the child rather than starting a silent design dispatch. The child returns the demanded proof; the parent reconciles it on the return path.\n15. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped)** — Default: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-codex, cli-opencode, cli-claude-code). Wait for the dispatched agent's work to return, verify outputs exist, then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started: capture its PID at launch (`codex exec ... & CODEX_PID=$!`) and kill that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 \"$CODEX_PID\" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P \"$CODEX_PID\" 2>/dev/null`), then apply the same PID-scoped `gtimeout` cleanup. **Never use a blanket `pkill -9 -f \"codex exec --model\"` pattern** — that matches and kills EVERY running `codex exec` process on the machine, including the operator's unrelated codex sessions. Only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped. **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole multi-iteration session at start — iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt. **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently — but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.\n16. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env AND state the exemption in the prompt.** The variable makes the waiver true; it does not make it observable. The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable, so a child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question and writes nothing, at exit code zero. Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt. when sessions may be launched through the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`). A dispatched `codex exec` is an orchestrated sub-session, not a new top-level session, so it must SHARE the parent's worktree rather than allocate its own. The wrapper checks `AI_SESSION_CHILD` (plus a `git --git-common-dir` structural backstop) and exec's in place when set. Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 codex exec ... </dev/null`. Harmless when the wrapper is not in use. See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → \"Worktree session isolation\".\n\n17. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).** Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}` — never a bare task. Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9 (`.skilled/agents/<name>.md`, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, etc. — never hardcode one runtime), and map each subtask to the RIGHT agent (`code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, docs→`markdown`), not one default. **Codex has no native persona surface** — `.codex/agents/*.toml` is TUI-only, and `codex exec` / `-p <profile>` load sandbox/effort config, not a persona. So **INLINE** the persona block into the prompt payload on every dispatch, using the same in-payload pattern as the `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 14) — the child cannot resolve agent paths by reference. A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant, silently dropping the agent's tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract. Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` \"Persona Injection\"; native precedent: `orchestrate.md` \"Agent Loading Protocol\". Rare exceptions (focused summary for a small-context model, pure-mechanical command) are declared at the dispatch site.\n\n18. **Never dispatch `codex exec` from inside a running codex session.** A codex process cannot spawn another codex from inside its own sandbox. The nested child dies at startup with `failed to initialize in-process app-server client: Operation not permitted` (observed 2026-09-02 on codex-cli 0.151.0 under `--sandbox workspace-write`), and the parent reads that as a failed iteration rather than a route violation. So when codex is itself the executor of a deep-loop fan-out lineage or any other orchestrating session, it must do each iteration's work in-process with its own tools and never dispatch a second codex. Grep that exact message to confirm you are hitting this and not a model or network fault.\n\n### ⛔ NEVER\n\n1. Use `--sandbox danger-full-access` without explicit user approval (full shell beyond workspace = damage risk). A no-prompt approval policy does not remove the need for explicit scope approval.\n2. Trust Codex output blindly for security-sensitive code, send sensitive data (API keys, passwords, credentials) in prompts, or hammer the API with rapid sequential calls.\n3. Use Codex for tasks where context is already loaded — direct action by the calling AI is faster.\n4. Assume Codex output is correct without verification — cross-reference codebase and project standards.\n5. Build or maintain a packet-local Codex execution adapter; the deep-loop runtime is the execution authority.\n\n### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF\n\n1. Codex CLI is not installed and user has not acknowledged (provide `npm i -g @openai/codex`).\n2. Rate limits are persistently exceeded (suggest checking the ChatGPT OAuth account's plan and usage limits).\n3. Codex output conflicts with existing code patterns (present both perspectives; user decides).\n4. Task requires `--sandbox danger-full-access` (describe risks; get explicit user approval). A no-prompt approval policy still requires explicit scope approval.\n\n### Memory Handback Protocol\n\nWhen the calling AI needs to preserve session context from a Codex CLI delegation, run the canonical procedure (extract `MEMORY_HANDBACK` section → build structured JSON → scrub secrets → invoke `generate-context.js` via `--stdin`/`--json`/temp-file). The continuity writer is the last step; nothing is handed to an index. Full procedure and caveats: [`system-spec-kit/references/cli/memory-handback.md`](../../system-spec-kit/references/cli/memory-handback.md). Codex-specific Memory Epilogue template: [assets/prompt-templates.md](./assets/prompt-templates.md) §13.\n\n```bash\nprintf '%s' \"$JSON_PAYLOAD\" | node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js --stdin [spec-folder]\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5.
